title: Molecular Hydrogen: an Emerging Therapeutic Medical Gas for Brain Disorders.
abstract: Oxidative stress and neuroinflammation are the main physiopathological changes involved in the initiation and progression of various neurodegenerative disorders or brain injuries. Since the landmark finding reported in 2007 found that hydrogen reduced the levels of peroxynitrite anions and hydroxyl free radicals in ischemic stroke, molecular hydrogen's antioxidative and anti-inflammatory effects have aroused widespread interest. Due to its excellent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, hydrogen therapy via different routes of administration exhibits great therapeutic potential for a wide range of brain disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, depression, anxiety, traumatic brain injury, ischemic stroke, Parkinson's disease, and multiple sclerosis. This paper reviews the routes for hydrogen administration, the effects of hydrogen on the previously mentioned brain disorders, and the primary mechanism underlying hydrogen's neuroprotection. Finally, we discuss hydrogen therapy's remaining issues and challenges in brain disorders. We conclude that understanding the exact molecular target, finding novel routes, and determining the optimal dosage for hydrogen administration is critical for future studies and applications.

title: Hydrogen supplemented air inhalation reduces changes of prooxidant enzyme and gap junction protein levels after transient global cerebral ischemia in the rat hippocampus.
abstract: Transient global cerebral ischemia (TGCI) occurs during acute severe hypotension depriving the brain of oxygen and glucose for a short period of time. During reperfusion, several mechanisms can induce secondary neuronal damage, including the increased production of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Hydrogen gas-enriched air inhalation is a neuroprotective approach with proven antioxidant potential, which has not yet been examined in TGCI. Accordingly, we set out to describe the effect of inhalation of 2.1% hydrogen supplemented room air (H(2)-RA) in comparison with a well studied neuroprotective agent, rosiglitazone (RSG) in a TGCI rat model. Male Wistar rats were exposed to TGCI (n=26) or sham operation (n=26), while a third group served as intact control (naive, n=5). The operated groups were further divided into non-treated, H(2)-RA, RSG (6 mg/kg i.v.) and vehicle treated animals. Tissue samples from the hippocampus and frontal cortex were taken 3 days following surgery. Western blot analysis was applied to determine the expressions of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), neuronal and endothelial nitric oxide synthase (nNOS and eNOS, respectively), manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD) and glial connexin proteins: connexin 30 and connexin 43. The expressions of COX-2, and connexin proteins were upregulated, while nNOS was downregulated 3 days after TGCI. Both RSG and H(2)-RA prevented the changes of enzyme and connexin levels. Considering the lack of harmful side effects, inhalation of H(2)-RA can be a promising approach to reduce neuronal damage after TGCI.

During reperfusion, several mechanisms can induce secondary neuronal damage, including the increased production of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Hydrogen gas-enriched air inhalation is a neuroprotective approach with proven antioxidant potential, which has not yet been examined in TGCI.

title: LRRK2 Negatively Regulates BDNF/TrkB Signaling and Neurovascular Function After Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
abstract: Gain-of-function mutations of leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) are neurotoxic, cause Parkinson's disease, and associate with risk of ischemic stroke. We explored the role of LRRK2 in transient oxygen/glucose deprivation (tOGD)-induced HUVEC and HT-22 neuronal cells, and after transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) in rats. tOGD increased LRRK2 protein and suppressed BDNF, Notch signaling, CD31, capillary-like network formation, and cellular viability in HUVEC. These suppressions were blocked by LRRK2 siRNA or the LRRK2 inhibitor MLi-2. HSC70-dependent chaperone-mediated autophagy can clear LRRK2. Using the HSC70 activator salidroside, HSC70 siRNA, and the HSC70 inhibitor Ver155008, we showed that the tOGD-dependent increases in LRRK2 and their effects were reversed by activating HSC70. The TrkB inhibitor ANA-12 and the Notch inhibitor DAPT both blocked the salidroside-dependent activation of Notch after tOGD, although DAPT did not prevent salidroside-induced increases in BDNF. Similarly, tOGD increased LRRK2 protein in HT-22 cells, and LRRK2-dependent reductions in BDNF and neuronal differentiation were prevented by salidroside via an HSC70-dependent mechanism. In vivo, tMCAO increased cerebral LRRK2 protein, an effect prevented by salidroside. tMCAO also suppressed cerebral BDNF, Notch activation, NeuN expression, neurological function, CD31 protein, and the number of CD31+ cells and blood flow. Both MLi-2 and salidroside prevented these suppressive effects, without additive benefit when combined, whereas inhibition of HSC70 or TrkB abolished salidroside-mediated restoration of Notch activation, CD31, and NeuN. These findings identify LRRK2 as a negative regulator of BDNF/TrkB signaling after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and demonstrate that targeting the HSC70-LRRK2-BDNF axis preserves neurovascular integrity and function.

title: Electroacupuncture Alleviates Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Regulating Copper Overload and Cuproptosis.
abstract: The role of cuproptosis, triggered by copper (Cu) overload in mitochondria and driving lipoylated tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle enzyme aggregation, in ischemic stroke has not been fully elucidated. Electroacupuncture (EA), a complementary therapy, plays a crucial role in treating ischemic stroke. To clarify whether cuproptosis is involved in the neuroprotective effects of EA, we analyzed the treatment of EA and the copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate (TTM) in rats with middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R). The results showed that EA decreased intracellular copper accumulation, downregulated the copper importer solute carrier family 31 member 1 (SLC31A1) and upregulated the copper exporters ATPase copper transporting alpha/beta (ATP7A and ATP7B) in the hippocampus of MCAO/R rats. These effects were accompanied by improved mitochondrial damage, decreased mitochondrial copper accumulation, upregulated mitochondrial copper transporter solute carrier family 25 member 3 (SLC25A3), and decreased mitochondrial translocation of the mitochondrial copper transporter cytochrome c oxidase assembly homolog 17 (COX17) in the hippocampus of MCAO/R rats after EA treatment. Moreover, cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (CIR) exhibited features of cuproptosis, including the loss of iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster proteins ferredoxin-1 (FDX1) and lipoic acid synthetase (LIAS), decreased lipoylated dihydrolipoamide S-acetyltransferase (Lip-DLAT), and DLAT oligomer aggregation, all of which were reversed by EA treatment. Additionally, CIR induced a larger infarct area, more severe neurological deficits, and hippocampal neuronal loss, which were rescued by the copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate (TTM) and EA treatment. Collectively, EA regulates intracellular and mitochondrial copper homeostasis in hippocampal neurons, suppresses cuproptosis, and thereby alleviates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI).

To clarify whether cuproptosis is involved in the neuroprotective effects of EA, we analyzed the treatment of EA and the copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate (TTM) in rats with middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R).

title: Celastrol partially restores Prodh expression in oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-injured astrocytes: A candidate mechanism relevant to ischemic stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) is an acute cerebrovascular disease caused by obstruction of the cerebral arteries, which deprives brain tissue of oxygen and glucose. This deprivation perturbs endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis and activates the unfolded protein response (UPR). When ER stress (ERS) is severe or sustained, the UPR can no longer restore homeostasis and cell injury ensues. Celastrol, a pentacyclic triterpene compound derived from Tripterygium wilfordii, a medicinal plant used in traditional Chinese medicine, alleviates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by regulating astrocyte function. However, whether celastrol can treat IS by relieving ERS remains unclear.

METHOD: Bulk transcriptomic (GSE202659) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; GSE233812) datasets were downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Differential expression analysis, functional enrichment analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, random-forest, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction, and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were used to identify candidate gene of celastrol in IS. scRNA-seq analysis was then applied to examine the cell-type distribution of these genes and the biological functions of the astrocytes in which they act.

RESULTS: Integrated analysis suggested that Prodh is a candidate ERS-related gene predominantly expressed in astrocytes. In cultured astrocytes subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R), Prodh mRNA was downregulated, and celastrol treatment partially restored its expression; this restoration was accompanied by improved cell viability in the CCK-8 assay. In addition, scRNA-seq analysis revealed that Prodh expression decreased at days 1 and 3 after IS and increased by day 7.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify Prodh as a candidate gene in astrocytes after ischemic stroke. Celastrol partially restored Prodh expression in OGD/R-injured astrocytes, and this restoration was accompanied by improved cell viability , which supports further investigation into the functional significance of this restoration.

This deprivation perturbs endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis and activates the unfolded protein response (UPR). When ER stress (ERS) is severe or sustained, the UPR can no longer restore homeostasis and cell injury ensues.

title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase without mechanical thrombectomy and regional cerebral perfusion in acute ischemic stroke with medium- and distal-vessel occlusions.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of intra-arterial tenecteplase (IA-TNK) without mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke due to medium-vessel occlusions (MeVOs) and distal-vessel occlusions (DiVOs).

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with MeVO or DiVO treated with IA-TNK at doses of 2.5 to 10 mg. Computed tomography perfusion (CTP) was performed at baseline and immediately after treatment, with hypoperfused tissue volume defined as Tmax > 6 seconds and processed using RAPID software. Neurological status was assessed using the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) at baseline, 24 hours, 7 days, and discharge; functional outcome using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 30 days.

RESULTS: Ten patients considered unsuitable for mechanical thrombectomy received IA-TNK (mean age 64.3 ± 12.3 years). Mean baseline NIHSS was 10.2 ± 4.7, and mean baseline ASPECTS was 9.1 ± 0.7. Angiographic improvement (≥1 mTICI grade) occurred in 4 of 10 patients, and tissue-level reperfusion (≥50% reduction in Tmax > 6-second volume) in 7 of 9 patients with paired CTP. Among 9 patients with paired CTP, median Tmax > 6-second volume decreased significantly from 48.0 mL to 17.0 mL (p = 0.02, Wilcoxon signed-rank test). Early neurological improvement at 24 hours occurred in 7 of 9 evaluable patients. Functional independence (mRS ≤ 2) at 30 days was achieved in 6 of 9 patients with follow-up. No intracranial hemorrhage of any Heidelberg class was observed.

CONCLUSION: IA-TNK without thrombectomy in selected MeVO/DiVO patients was associated with a significant reduction in CTP-defined hypoperfusion, encouraging early neurological improvement, and no symptomatic hemorrhage, supporting further prospective evaluation.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with MeVO or DiVO treated with IA-TNK at doses of 2.5 to 10 mg. Computed tomography perfusion (CTP) was performed at baseline and immediately after treatment, with hypoperfused tissue volume defined as Tmax > 6 seconds and processed using RAPID software.

title: Hospital frailty risk score and one-year mortality after intravenous thrombolysis in older patients with acute ischemic stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is a clinical syndrome characterized by a decline of function across multiple organ systems. It is also associated with higher short-term mortality following ischemic stroke. However, the impact of frailty on functional outcome in acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. This study examines the association between frailty and one-year mortality after ischemic stroke in patients receiving intravenous thrombolysis.

METHODS: In this monocentric retrospective cohort study, we calculated the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS) for all patients over 65 years with ischemic stroke who received intravenous thrombolysis from 2014 to 2019. Kaplan-Meier-Analysis and Cox-regression analysis were used to assess the impact of frailty on one-year mortality after ischemic stroke in these patients.

RESULTS: A total of 423 patients were included in our analysis. Of these, 360 patients (85.2%) had a low risk of frailty (HFRS < 5) and 63 patients (14.9%) had an increased frailty risk with an HFRS ≥ 5. The NIHSS at discharge (3 [IQR 1-6] vs. 4 [ IQR 2-9] was higher in patients with frailty-risk. One-year mortality was 20.6% and 34.9%, respectively (log-rank p = 0.016). In multivariable Cox regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, NIHSS at admission and ASPECTS, each one-point increase in the HFRS was associated with a higher hazard of one-year mortality (HR 1,085 (95% KI 1,015-1,160), p = 0,017). Adding the HFRS to the baseline clinical model improved model fit (likelihood ratio test, p = 0.028).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients aged ≥ 65 years who received intravenous thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke, a higher administratively derived HFRS was independently associated with a higher hazard of one-year mortality. These findings support further evaluation of the HFRS as a pragmatic prognostic marker but should not be interpreted as evidence for withholding reperfusion therapy.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: not applicable.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Frailty is a clinical syndrome characterized by a decline of function across multiple organ systems. It is also associated with higher short-term mortality following ischemic stroke. However, the impact of frailty on functional outcome in acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain.

title: Hydrogen-rich saline alleviates inflammation-associated depression-like behaviors in mice.
abstract: Despite the crucial role of inflammation in depression-like behavior, the low blood-brain barrier penetration of existing anti-inflammatory agents presents a substantial obstacle to effective treatment. Owing to the excellent blood-brain barrier permeability and anti-inflammatory ability of hydrogen-rich saline, this study explores its therapeutic effects on lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation-associated depression-like behavior in mice. In this study, mice intraperitoneally received lipopolysaccharide (0.83 mg/kg). Thirty minutes later, they intraperitoneally received hydrogen-rich saline (5 mL/kg). Results showed that hydrogen-rich saline significantly alleviated anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in lipopolysaccharide-treated mice, as assessed by open field tests, elevated plus maze tests, forced swim tests, and the tail suspension test. Peripheral inflammation was significantly reduced, associated with inhibited splenomegaly and decreased serum levels of interleukin-1β and tumor necrosis factor-α. Central inflammation was also decreased, related to the reduced number of activated microglia, inhibition of Tolllike receptor 4/myeloid differentiation primary response 88/nuclear factor-κB signaling, and repaired synaptic damage in the hippocampus. These findings suggest that early hydrogen-rich saline administration may attenuate lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation-associated depression-like behaviors, at least in part, by suppressing microglial pro-inflammatory activation and Tolllike receptor 4/nuclear factor-κB signaling.

Owing to the excellent blood-brain barrier permeability and anti-inflammatory ability of hydrogen-rich saline, this study explores its therapeutic effects on lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation-associated depression-like behavior in mice. In this study, mice intraperitoneally received lipopolysaccharide (0.83 mg/kg).

title: Molecular hydrogen modulates neutrophil reactivity in vitro.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human neutrophil granulocytes are key effector cells of innate immune system and play a central role in host defense and inflammatory responses. Owing to their critical functions, they are an important focus of immunological research. Molecular hydrogen has been reported to exert antioxidative, cytoprotective, and anti-inflammatory effects in various disease models; however, its specific impact on neutrophil functionality remains insufficiently understood. This study therefore aims to systematically characterize the effects of H₂ on polymorphonuclear neutrophils and to compare them with those induced by the volatile anesthetic Sevoflurane, which has also been shown to modulate immune responses and reactive oxygen species production. Functional readouts include migratory behavior, reactive oxygen species generation, myeloperoxidase activity, NET formation, and the surface expression of selected activation markers. To assess chemotactic responsiveness, PMNs were additionally stimulated with different fMLP concentrations.

METHODS: To investigate the effects of molecular hydrogen and Sevoflurane on the function and characteristics of PMNs, both microscopic techniques and flow cytometry were employed.

RESULTS: The functional responses of neutrophil granulocytes were markedly affected by molecular hydrogen. Maximal DHR-, MPO-, and DAPI-associated fluorescence appeared later under the microscope in H₂-exposed cells compared with both untreated and Sevoflurane-treated cells. High concentrations of fMLP reduced chemotaxis and inhibited directed polarization. Flow cytometry further revealed a significant decrease in reactive oxygen species production in H₂-exposed cells compared with untreated controls following stimulation with PMA, fMLP, TNF-α, and LPS.

CONCLUSION: Overall, molecular hydrogen markedly modulates neutrophil function by delaying TmaxROS, ET50MPO, and ET50NETosis, whereas Sevoflurane exerts a less pronounced effect with an earlier onset, highlighting the therapeutic potential of H₂ in inflammatory conditions.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Human neutrophil granulocytes are key effector cells of innate immune system and play a central role in host defense and inflammatory responses. Owing to their critical functions, they are an important focus of immunological research. Molecular hydrogen has been reported to exert antioxidative, cytoprotective, and anti-inflammatory effects in various disease models; however, its specific impact on neutrophil functionality remains insufficiently understood.

title: Benzbromarone targets HSP47 to inhibit platelet activation via the collagen/GPVI axis and ameliorates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in mice.
abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a major strategy for ischemic stroke. Studies have identified heat shock protein 47 (HSP47) as a safe and effective novel target for antiplatelet therapy, but clinically available HSP47 inhibitors remain lacking. Benzbromarone, a commonly used urate-lowering drug, has been reported to bind HSP47; however, whether it exerts antithrombotic effects by targeting platelet HSP47 remains unclear. In this study, cellular thermal shift assay and drug affinity responsive target stability assay demonstrated that benzbromarone directly interacted with platelet HSP47 and enhanced its stability. Benzbromarone disrupted the HSP47-collagen interaction and selectively inhibited collagen-induced platelet adhesion, spreading, aggregation, P-selectin expression, and reactive oxygen species production, with little effect on thrombin- or arachidonic acid-induced aggregation. In a FeCl3-induced mouse carotid artery thrombosis model, benzbromarone dose-dependently prolonged occlusion time and reduced thrombus formation, with efficacy comparable to aspirin and clopidogrel, without obvious bleeding risk, coagulation disturbance, or hepatic or renal toxicity at effective doses. Mechanistically, benzbromarone inhibited phosphorylation of Syk, PKC, and PLCγ2 downstream of the collagen-GPVI signaling pathway. Importantly, its antiplatelet and antithrombotic effects were largely abolished in platelet-specific HSP47 knockout mice, confirming the dependence on platelet HSP47. In a middle cerebral artery occlusion model, benzbromarone reduced cerebral microthrombosis, infarct volume, and neurological deficits, and this neuroprotection was largely HSP47-dependent. Together, these findings support benzbromarone as a clinically available HSP47-targeting candidate that suppresses platelet activation, arterial thrombosis, and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, warranting further evaluation for ischemic stroke.
englishSummary: Antiplatelet therapy is a major strategy for ischemic stroke. Studies have identified heat shock protein 47 (HSP47) as a safe and effective novel target for antiplatelet therapy, but clinically available HSP47 inhibitors remain lacking. Benzbromarone, a commonly used urate-lowering drug, has been reported to bind HSP47; however, whether it exerts antithrombotic effects by targeting platelet HSP47 remains unclear.

title: Protein Phosphatase Signaling and Lipid Metabolic Remodeling in Ischemic Stroke: Evidence Boundaries, Candidate Interfaces, and Translational Questions.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ischemic stroke couples phosphorylation-dependent stress signaling with lipid metabolic remodeling, but the evidence for a direct phosphatase-lipid pathway remains uncertain.

METHODS: This narrative mini-review appraised 79 cited studies through July 2026. Evidence was graded by disease-model relevance, intervention type, cell specificity, and causal strength; stroke-specific findings were separated from cross-context inference.

RESULTS: PTP1B had the strongest stroke-specific phosphatase evidence, although support was concentrated in one rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion study paired with prophylactically treated microglial oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation models. Direct PTP1BPERK catalytic directionality remains unresolved. ACSL4 had interventional support for ferroptotic injury, whereas lipid-droplet-rich microglial states were time- and context-dependent. Acylcarnitines served primarily as metabolic signatures, with mediator-level evidence limited to selected long-chain species in a single model. No direct stroke study has demonstrated PTP1B control of ACSL4, lipid droplet turnover, or carnitine shuttle flux.

DISCUSSION: The available literature supports candidate interfaces among ER-stress signaling, autophagy-related readouts, oxidative injury, and lipid handling, but not an established upstream- downstream pathway. Carnitine-related metabolism is therefore best treated as an independent translational module.

CONCLUSION: Future work should prioritize cell-specific causality, target engagement, and clinically relevant exposure before phosphatase or carnitine strategies are advanced as stroke therapies.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Ischemic stroke couples phosphorylation-dependent stress signaling with lipid metabolic remodeling, but the evidence for a direct phosphatase-lipid pathway remains uncertain. METHODS: This narrative mini-review appraised 79 cited studies through July 2026. Evidence was graded by disease-model relevance, intervention type, cell specificity, and causal strength; stroke-specific findings were separated from cross-context inference.

title: GRSF1 Ameliorates Neurological Impairment in Cerebral Ischemia/Reperfusion Mice via Regulating Mul1/Mfn2-Mediated Mitochondrial Dynamics and Bioenergetics.
abstract: Guanine-rich RNA sequence binding factor 1 (GRSF1), a mitochondrial RNA-binding protein, plays a critical role in maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis and mitigating oxidative DNA damage. Whether GRSF1 contributes to cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI) by regulating mitochondrial dynamics remains to be elucidated. Male C57BL/6 J mice underwent middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) to induce CIRI. Principal component analysis and enrichment analysis were employed to validate impairment in mitochondrial dynamics in CIRI mice. GRSF1 was then evaluated for its effects on neurological function and histology. The role of GRSF1 on mitochondrial dynamics following CIRI was examined through enrichment analysis, electron microscopy, and respiratory chain complex activity assays. The relationship between GRSF1 and mitofusin 2 (Mfn2) in mitochondrial fusion was further investigated. The regulatory mechanism of mitochondrial E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (Mul1) on Mfn2 was assessed using co-immunoprecipitation and denaturing immunoprecipitation assays. CIRI mice were characterized by disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, and restoring this balance ameliorates pathological progression. GRSF1 improved neurological function in CIRI mice, an effect confirmed to associate with maintenance of neuronal mitochondrial dynamics. Mechanistically, GRSF1 promoted mitochondrial fusion by suppressing the expression or activity of Mul1, thereby reducing Mul1-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of Mfn2. Ultimately, GRSF1 attenuated CIRI by inhibiting neuronal mitochondrial dynamic imbalance via the Mul1/Mfn2 pathway. It uncovers GRSF1 as a novel neuroprotective regulator in CIRI and identifies the Mul1/Mfn2 pathway as a critical mechanistic pathway underlying its protective effects. Targeting GRSF1 may hold therapeutic potential by modulating mitochondrial dynamics in CIRI.

Male C57BL/6 J mice underwent middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) to induce CIRI.

title: From first-principles to quantum electrodynamics: high-precision rovibrational spectra of molecular hydrogen isotopologues.
abstract: Modern high-resolution spectroscopy of molecular hydrogen and its isotopologues has reached a level of accuracy at which subtle nonadiabatic, relativistic, and quantum electrodynamic (QED) effects can be probed and stringently tested. In our previous work (part I), we introduced a fully nonadiabatic treatment of H2 based on four-particle, explicitly correlated exponential basis functions, achieving relative accuracies of 10-9 for dissociation energies and rovibrational level spacings in the electronic ground state, in agreement with the most precise experimental data. In the present contribution (part II), this methodology is applied to the remaining bound isotopologues of molecular hydrogen, including HD, HT, D2, DT, and T2, providing a unified, high-precision theoretical description of their rovibrational structures. Within the four-body framework, we evaluate the leading relativistic and QED corrections of the lowest rovibrational levels of the ground electronic state. For all isotopologues considered, dissociation energies and selected rovibrational transition frequencies are obtained with sub-MHz uncertainties, typically of order 10-5 cm-1 (1 MHz = 3.33564 × 10-5 cm-1). The resulting theoretical data are compared with the most precise spectroscopic measurements for each isotopologue and are found to be consistent within the combined uncertainties. The present calculations for the molecular hydrogen family achieve uncertainties previously attainable only for two- and three-body systems, such as hydrogen and helium atoms and the molecular ion H2+. Taken together, parts I and II establish a high-precision benchmark for the rovibrational spectra of all molecular hydrogen isotopologues, including those containing tritium, and provide a reliable test of molecular quantum electrodynamics at the four-body level.

title: The 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association Guideline Updates to Management of Patients with Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Guide for Radiologists.
abstract: The 2026 guideline for early management of acute ischemic stroke retains many foundational recommendations while introducing clinically meaningful updates spanning imaging, broader inpatient management, and reperfusion strategies including IV thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy. Notably, it provides expanded guidance for medium vessel occlusions and introduces pediatric recommendations that were largely absent from prior iterations. Given their impact on imaging workflows in acute ischemic stroke, the authors present a focused review of the updated guidelines for the radiologist.

title: Electroacupuncture Alleviates Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury by Inhibiting TLR4/NF-κB-Mediated Pyroptosis and Restoring Metabolic Homeostasis.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia‑reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major complication of ischemic stroke and is characterized by neuroinflammation and metabolic dysregulation. Electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated neuroprotective effects; however, the precise mechanisms involving the TLR4/NF‑κB signaling pathway and associated metabolomic alterations remain incompletely understood. A rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) was established. Rats received daily EA at acupoints GV20 and GV14 for seven consecutive days or were treated with the selective TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, and cell death were evaluated. Serum levels of IL‑1β and IL‑18 were measured by ELISA. The mRNA and protein expression of TLR4, NF‑κB p65, NLRP3, ASC, Caspase‑1, GSDMD, GSDMD‑N, IL‑1β, and IL‑18 in brain tissue were assessed by quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) and Western blot. Metabolomic profiling of the cerebral cortex was performed using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC‑Q‑TOF‑MS). EA significantly reduced neurological deficit scores, infarct volume, and cell death, with effects comparable to those of TAK-242. EA suppressed both the mRNA and protein levels of all tested TLR4/NF‑κB pathway and pyroptosis‑related molecules, and also decreased serum concentrations of IL‑1β and IL‑18. Metabolomic analysis revealed that EA reversed numerous I/R‑induced metabolic alterations, with significant enrichment in glycerophospholipid metabolism, glutamatergic synapse, and the TCA cycle. The data suggest that EA might protect against cerebral I/R injury, potentially through concurrent suppression of the TLR4/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3/GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, along with partial restoration of metabolic homeostasis, supporting EA as a promising therapy for ischemic stroke.

Electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated neuroprotective effects; however, the precise mechanisms involving the TLR4/NF‑κB signaling pathway and associated metabolomic alterations remain incompletely understood. A rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) was established.

title: Disrupting the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia: Mechanism of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction in the treatment of ischemic stroke.
abstract: Our previous studies have shown that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively suppresses central immune-inflammatory responses, modulates peripheral inflammatory mediators, reduces the infiltration of peripheral T lymphocytes into the central nervous system, and promotes the conversion of infiltrated T lymphocytes in the brain into Treg cells. However, whether Huanglian Jiedu Decoction can influence M2 microglial polarization by regulating T-lymphocyte phenotypic transformation and thereby modulate neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke remains unclear. This study focused on Treg-mediated microglial polarization to investigate the potential of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction to modulate interactions between T lymphocytes and microglia in the treatment of ischemic stroke. We established a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion, an inflammatory model of Jurkat T cells stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate and ionomycin, and a Transwell co-culture model of T lymphocytes and HMC3 microglia. The results showed that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively alleviated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model of middle cerebral artery, inhibited central inflammatory responses, and promoted the polarization of microglia toward the M2 phenotype. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction also promoted the conversion of CD4+ T cells in brain tissue into regulatory T cells and regulated regulatory T cells through the interleukin-10/Janus kinase 1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 pathway, thereby promoting the activation of M2 microglia. These findings suggest that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction, which has heat-clearing and detoxifying properties, can regulate immune homeostasis, inhibit secondary neuroinflammation associated with ischemic stroke, and exert neuroprotective effects. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction may therefore treat ischemic stroke by modulating the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia, providing a traditional Chinese medicine-based strategy for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

title: Cyclosporine A modulates the ER-mitochondria-mitophagy axis in experimental cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia‑reperfusion injury involves mitochondrial dysfunction, intracellular calcium dysregulation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, and neuronal damage. Cyclosporine A has demonstrated neuroprotective activity in experimental ischemia, yet its relationship with endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondrial coupling and mitophagy remains incompletely understood. In this study, male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to Control, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R), or MCAO/R plus cyclosporine A groups, and infarct volume, blood-brain barrier permeability, neurological deficits, and motor performance were assessed; PC12 cells were subjected to oxygen‑glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) with or without cyclosporine A treatment, and IP3R-VDAC1 and LC3B-FUNDC1 colocalization were evaluated by immunofluorescence, while intracellular calcium levels were measured using Fluo‑4 AM flow cytometry and confocal imaging. Cyclosporine A treatment was associated with reduced infarct volume and Evans Blue extravasation and with improved neurological and motor outcomes after MCAO/R. In OGD/R‑treated PC12 cells, cyclosporine A increased IP3R-VDAC1 and LC3B-FUNDC1 colocalization and reduced intracellular calcium accumulation compared with untreated model cells. Collectively, these findings indicate that cyclosporine A attenuates experimental cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and is associated with restoration of IP3R-VDAC1 proximity, enhanced LC3B-FUNDC1 colocalization, and improved calcium regulation; however, additional genetic and mitophagy‑flux studies are required to determine whether the proposed ER-mitochondria-FUNDC1 pathway is necessary for cyclosporine A-mediated neuroprotection.

title: Impact of race, sex, and insurance status on outcomes following endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Racial, sex, and socioeconomic differences in stroke outcomes are well documented, but their associations with outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remain uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with acute ischemic stroke who underwent EVT at a comprehensive stroke center during 2016-2022. The analytic dataset contained 527 patients. Endpoint-specific available observations were used without imputation. Outcomes included expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) grade, admission and discharge National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), discharge and 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS), treatment-time metrics, and discharge disposition. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for seven clinical and procedural endpoints.

RESULTS: Final eTICI grade was available for 493 patients. Successful reperfusion (eTICI ≥2b) occurred in 449 (91.1%), and near-complete reperfusion (eTICI ≥2c) in 309 (62.7%). No demographic or payer variable was significantly associated with either reperfusion endpoint. Poor functional outcome occurred in 344 of 448 patients (76.8%) at discharge and 247 of 376 (65.7%) at 90 days. Black race and Medicare insurance were associated with poor discharge outcome. Female sex, Black race, and Medicare insurance were associated with poor 90-day outcome. Medicare and commercial insurance were associated with non-home discharge. Among 516 patients with available door-to-puncture time, the median was 69 min (interquartile range, 54-91), without statistically significant differences by sex, race, ethnicity, or payer.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing EVT at a single comprehensive stroke center, reperfusion rates were high and were not significantly associated with observed demographic or payer variables. Differences in functional outcomes and discharge destination were observed, but residual confounding, endpoint-specific missingness, and the single-center design limit causal interpretation.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with acute ischemic stroke who underwent EVT at a comprehensive stroke center during 2016-2022. The analytic dataset contained 527 patients.

title: Carotid plaque morphology on computed tomography angiography associated with cervical recanalization strategy in acute ischemic stroke with anterior circulation tandem lesions.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether carotid plaque morphology on preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) is associated with the cervical recanalization strategy used during endovascular treatment (EVT) of acute ischemic stroke caused by anterior circulation tandem atherosclerotic lesions.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospective single-center database of consecutive adults treated with mechanical thrombectomy within 24 h of last known well between January 2022 and February 2025. CTA features of the extracranial internal carotid artery lesion included plaque composition, occlusion-cap morphology, string sign, and calcification pattern (none, eggshell, or dystrophic). Patients were categorized according to cervical recanalization strategy: aspiration alone or percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with or without stenting (PTA±stent). Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with PTA±stent.

RESULTS: Seventy-nine patients were included (median age, 68 years). Cervical recanalization was achieved with aspiration alone in 40 patients (50.6%) and with PTA±stent in 39 (49.4%); stents were implanted in 14 patients. Dystrophic calcification was more frequent in the PTA±stent group (38.5% vs. 17.5%; p = 0.038). Dystrophic calcification (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 4.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.37-17.05; p = 0.014) and male sex (adjusted OR, 4.97; 95% CI, 1.43-17.31; p = 0.012) were independently associated with PTA±stent. Successful intracranial reperfusion was more frequent in the PTA±stent group (89.7% vs. 70.0%; p = 0.029), with no significant differences in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or 90-day functional outcome.

CONCLUSION: Dystrophic calcification on preprocedural CTA was independently associated with the use of cervical PTA with or without stenting in patients with anterior circulation tandem lesions. This finding may help anticipate the potential need for cervical angioplasty and facilitate technical procedural preparation.

title: Astrocyte-derived small extracellular vesicles deliver Serpina3k to attenuate cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by restraining neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis.
abstract:
AIM: To determine whether astrocyte-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) deliver Serpina3k to recipient neural cells and protect against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI).

METHODS: A mouse transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion model was combined with pharmacological inhibition of sEV release, astrocyte-targeted Serpina3k knockdown and intrathecal delivery of astrocyte-derived sEVs. Brain sEV cargo was profiled by label-free proteomics and Transwell co-cultures were subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Neurological outcomes, infarct volume, apoptosis and inflammatory mediators were assessed, and Serpina3k-interacting proteins were identified by co-immunoprecipitation.

RESULTS: Blocking sEV release aggravated neurological deficits, neuronal apoptosis and inflammation. Brain-derived sEVs increased after ischemia-reperfusion and protected neurons against oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Serpina3k was enriched in ischemia-derived sEVs and localized predominantly to astrocytes; astrocytic Serpina3k knockdown reduced sEV-associated Serpina3k and worsened deficits, whereas Serpina3k-deficient sEVs increased neuronal apoptosis, microglial IL-1beta and IL-18 release, infarct volume and Caspase-6/NLRP3 signalling. Serpina3k co-immunoprecipitated with Caspase-6 and Omi/HtrA2. In vivo, Serpina3k-deficient astrocytic sEVs were associated with larger infarct volume, increased Omi/HtrA2 expression and reduced HAX-1 expression.

CONCLUSION: Astrocyte-derived sEV-associated Serpina3k is an endogenous protective cargo that limits cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by restraining microglial inflammatory activation and neuronal apoptosis.

title: Targeting Fibroblast Foxc2 Promotes Neurovascular Recovery by Suppressing Sdc4 After Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability, with current reperfusion therapies limited by narrow therapeutic windows and inability to promote sustained neurovascular repair. Here, we developed YZD-27, a rationally designed Tanshinone IIA (TSA) derivative with improved druggability, and show that it remains therapeutically effective when administered up to 24 h after ischemic injury in transient and permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO and dMCAO) mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and cell-cell communication analysis revealed broad cellular responses to YZD-27 and identified fibronectin-1 (Fn1)/syndecan-4 (Sdc4) as a predicted endothelia-fibroblast ligand-receptor interaction. Mechanistically, YZD-27 directly binds forkhead box protein C2 (Foxc2), enhances its protein stability by limiting proteasomal degradation, and increases its occupancy at the Sdc4 promoter, thereby repressing Sdc4 transcription in fibroblast. Fibroblast-conditioned medium experiments further supported a role for Foxc2/Sdc4 regulation in modulating endothelial barrier-related protein expression. These findings identify Foxc2/Sdc4 signaling as a regulatory mechanism associated with the therapeutic effects of YZD-27, and establish YZD-27 as a promising neurovascular therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke.

title: Outcomes of acute ischemic stroke and reperfusion therapy in patients with Moyamoya disease.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is an uncommon cerebrovascular condition associated with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and intracranial hemorrhage. This study examines outcomes of AIS in patients with MMD (MMD-AIS) and associated outcomes of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) and intravascular thrombolysis (IVT).

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional analysis used the National Inpatient Sample database (2015-2022), including adult (≥18 years-old) U.S. hospitalizations for AIS with reported NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS). Inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted for confounding factors. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 1,733,390 AIS hospitalizations, 3,735 (0.2%) involved comorbid MMD; 150 (4.0%) underwent EVT while 300 (8.0%) received IVT. MMD was associated with reduced use of EVT (aOR: 0.362, 95% CI [0.238-0.553], p < 0.001) and IVT (0.315 [0.242-0.412], p < 0.001) compared with non-MMD AIS. Following IPTW, MMD was associated with similar inpatient mortality (1.29 [0.797-2.09], p = 0.299), reduced routine discharge (0.639 [0.540-0.757], p < 0.001), and similar hemorrhagic transformation (1.13 [0.742-1.74], p = 0.560). Among the MMD-AIS group with NIHSS > 5, EVT was not associated with differences in routine discharge (0.672 [0.398-1.14], p = 0.137), inpatient mortality (0.072 [0.004-1.20], p = 0.067), or hemorrhagic transformation (1.61 [0.896-2.88], p = 0.111). IVT was associated with increased routine discharge (1.96 [1.35-2.85], p < 0.001), and no difference in hemorrhagic transformation (0.948 [0.542-1.66], p = 0.852) or mortality (1.74 [0.811-3.75], p = 0.155).

DISCUSSION: MMD-AIS was associated with reduced routine discharge without increased hemorrhagic risk. EVT and IVT were infrequently used but may be feasible in selected patients. Prospective studies are needed to determine the efficacy of reperfusion therapy in this population.

title: KLF5-mediated NRP1 upregulation contributes to neurovascular dysfunction after ischemic stroke in male diabetic mice through dysregulated VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) exacerbates the outcomes of ischemic stroke by disrupting neurovascular homeostasis. However, the molecular mechanisms linking diabetic metabolic stress to impaired vascular and glial responses after ischemic injury remain incompletely understood. Neuropilin-1 (NRP1), a co-receptor involved in VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling, and Krüppel-like factor 5 (KLF5), a transcription factor implicated in vascular remodeling, may contribute to diabetic ischemic neurovascular dysfunction.

METHODS: Male diabetic db/db mice and male non-diabetic db/+ mice were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R). Human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMECs) and primary cortical astrocytes were exposed to high glucose combined with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R). The expression and regulatory relationship between KLF5 and NRP1 were investigated using qRT-PCR, western blotting, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-qPCR, and luciferase reporter assays. The effects of KLF5 knockdown and NRP1 overexpression on endothelial and astrocytic functions were evaluated using migration, tube formation, and cell viability assays.

RESULTS: T2DM aggravated ischemic brain injury, characterized by increased infarct volume, enhanced neuronal degeneration, worsened neurological deficits, reduced CD31 immunoreactivity, and elevated expression of KLF5 and NRP1. Mechanistically, KLF5 directly bound to the NRP1 promoter and promoted NRP1 transcription. Under high-glucose OGD/R conditions, increased KLF5 and NRP1 expression was accompanied by enhanced VEGFR2 phosphorylation and impaired endothelial migration and tube formation. KLF5 knockdown reduced NRP1 expression and VEGFR2 phosphorylation, thereby improving endothelial migration, tube formation, and astrocyte viability/migration. Conversely, NRP1 overexpression partially reversed the protective effects of KLF5 knockdown.

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetic ischemic stress induces maladaptive activation of the KLF5/NRP1 axis, contributing to neurovascular dysfunction through dysregulated VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling. Targeting the KLF5/NRP1 pathway may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for alleviating diabetic ischemic brain injury.

title: Evaluation of the effect of provincial and municipal emergency green channels (post-informatization and process optimization) on the treatment of acute ischemic stroke and study on influencing factors such as DNT and DPT.
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of informatization and process optimization on the treatment efficacy of the emergency green channel for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in provincial and municipal hospitals and analyzes its key influencing factors. A retrospective cohort study was conducted, enrolling patients with AIS who received reperfusion therapy via the emergency green channel from September 1, 2024, to August 31, 2025. Patients were divided into a control group (pre-optimization, n = 50) and a study group (post-optimization, n = 50) based on whether the informatization optimization was implemented ("Stroke One-Click Start," full-process electronic timestamps, cloud imaging platform, point-of-care rapid testing, and parallel pathways). Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline characteristics. The door-to-needle time (DNT), door-to-puncture time (DPT), compliance rates for key time nodes, clinical prognosis, and safety indicators were compared between the 2 groups. Baseline characteristics were balanced between the 2 groups after matching. The median DNT in the study group was significantly shorter than that in the control group (42 vs 68 minutes, P < .001), and the median DPT was also significantly shortened (92 vs 128 minutes, P < .001). The compliance rate for DNT ≤ 45 minutes increased from 22.0 to 70.0% (P < .001), and the compliance rate for DPT ≤ 90 minutes increased from 16.0 to 48.0% (P < .001). The times for key nodes (e.g., door-to-CT completion time, CT completion-to-treatment time) were significantly shortened (all P < .001). The study group had a higher proportion of favorable outcomes (mRS 0-2) at discharge and at 90 days (58.0 vs 36.0%, P = .027; 64.0 vs 44.0%, P = .046), and a shorter ICU stay (P = .044), with no significant differences in safety indicators. Subgroup analysis showed that DNT was significantly shortened in all subgroups, and there was an interaction between NIHSS score and optimization effect (P = .039), with the greatest benefit observed in patients with severe stroke. In this retrospective before-and-after cohort, implementation of the bundled informatization and process-optimization pathway was associated with shorter DNT and DPT, higher compliance with key time targets, and better functional outcomes without an observed increase in safety events. These findings should be interpreted in light of the nonrandomized design and support broader implementation in appropriately resourced institutions.

title: Effects of Exercise Preconditioning on Promoting Endogenous Recovery Responses After Ischemic Stroke in Late-Adult Mice.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological impairment, and although poststroke rehabilitation can support recovery, neurological deficits often limit the feasibility of exercise in clinical settings. Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated whether a treadmill exercise preconditioning regimen confers neuroprotection and improves recovery-related responses in late-adult mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion.

METHODS: Eight-month-old male mice were assigned to sedentary or exercise groups. Following 5 weeks of treadmill running (5 days per week after 1 week of acclimatization), mice underwent 45 minutes of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion. Behavioral assessments and body-weight monitoring were performed before and after middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume and cellular responses were evaluated 14 days after stroke.

RESULTS: Fourteen days after stroke, lesion volume was significantly reduced in the exercise group compared with sedentary controls. Exercise preconditioning enhanced neurogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and CD31-positive vascular responses while suppressing reactive astrocyte activation. Functional improvements were consistently observed across multiple behavioral assays in late-adult mice.

CONCLUSIONS: Preconditioning with treadmill exercise provides neuroprotection against ischemic stroke in late-adult mice by reducing infarct volume and promoting recovery-associated cellular responses. These findings demonstrate that the functional benefits of prestroke exercise extend beyond the young adult stage and support the potential value of regular physical activity as a strategy to mitigate ischemic brain injury later in adulthood.

Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized.

title: [Echinacoside attenuates microglial pyroptosis after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in mice by inhibiting STING/NLRP3 pathway].
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the regulatory effect of echinacoside (ECH) on microglial pyroptosis in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and its underlying mechanism.

METHODS: Fifty 8-week-old specific-pathogen-free male C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into a sham group, a model group, and an ECH intervention group (n=15 per group). A mouse model of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) was established to mimic cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The ECH intervention group received ECH (9 mg/kg) for 7 days after modeling. Neurological function, infarct volume, and cerebral blood flow were assessed by Longa neurological deficit scoring, TTC staining, and laser speckle imaging, respectively. The expression levels of proteins related to the NLRP3 inflammasome and the STING signaling pathway were determined by Western blotting and immunohistochemical staining. Microglia were labeled with ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule-1 (Iba-1), and the proportions of STING-positive and GSDMD-positive microglia were determined by double immunofluorescence colocalization staining. GSDMD-mediated membrane pore formation was observed by transmission electron microscopy.

RESULTS: Compared with the model group, the ECH intervention group showed improved neurological deficit scores, reduced infarct volume, and restored cerebral blood flow (all P<0.01). ECH significantly downregulated the expression of NLRP3, apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD domain (ASC), cleaved caspase-1, GSDMD, STING, phosphorylated nuclear factor-κB p65, and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (all P<0.01). Double immunofluorescence colocalization showed that GSDMD and STING were co-expressed with Iba-1, respectively, indicating that pyroptosis and STING pathway activation occurred predominantly in microglia. Transmission electron microscopy revealed that ECH reduced GSDMD-mediated membrane pore formation in microglia.

CONCLUSIONS: ECH may inhibit microglial pyroptosis by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and the STING signaling pathway.

title: RORα contributes to melatonin-mediated neuroprotection in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by promoting microglia/macrophage M2 polarization through the AMPK-mTOR signaling pathway.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (CI/R) injury is a neurological disorder in which microglia and macrophages regulate repair by switching M1/M2 phenotypes. RORα, a regulator of circadian rhythm and a mediator for melatonin effects, has an unclear role in CI/R injury and melatonin-mediated neuroprotection, particularly in microglial/macrophage polarization. An in vivo transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion model was established in C57BL/6J mice, and in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) models were developed for BV-2 and HT22 cells. In vivo, Flag-tagged RORα overexpression lentivirus were intracranially injected and melatonin (10 mg/kg) was injected intraperitoneally; in vitro, BV2 cells were exposed to 200 µM melatonin and infected with an RORα-overexpressing lentiviral vector, while HT22 cells were cultivated in conditioned medium. Western blot, immunofluorescence, TTC staining, and ELISA were used to evaluate RORα expression, neurological function, microglia/macrophage M2 polarization, inflammatory responses, and cellular apoptosis, respectively. The role of the AMPK-mTOR pathway was confirmed using the AMPK inhibitor Compound C in vitro. The viability, apoptosis, and ROS levels of HT22 cell were assessed using CCK-8 assay, TUNEL staining, and flow cytometry, respectively. In both in vivo and BV-2 cell in vitro models, RORα levels gradually decreased within 24 h, followed by a gradual recovery. Melatonin reduced neurological scores and enhanced blood-brain barrier protection, promoting M2 microglia/macrophage polarization and inhibiting subsequent inflammatory responses, with RORα overexpression further amplifying these effects. In an HT22 cell model, RORα overexpression enhanced the protection by melatonin against OGD/R-induced reductions in cell viability, as well as against increased apoptosis and elevated ROS levels. Mechanistically, RORα overexpression promoted M2 microglial polarization via activation of the AMPK-mTOR pathway, thereby amplifying the melatonin-mediated neuroprotection. RORα enhanced neuroprotection by melatonin against CI/R injury through promoting microglia/macrophage M2 polarization, suggesting a possible treatment target for CI/R injury.

title: Atomically dispersed nanoactivators drive innate mitochondrial biogenesis for active neuroprotection in ischemic stroke.
abstract: Mitigating mitochondrial bioenergetic failure is a pivotal yet formidable neuroprotective goal in treating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). However, conventional pharmacological interventions remain largely confined to passive antioxidant defense, which temporarily scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS) without restoring organelle function. Here, we report a bimetallic nanoactivator (RMV) designed to drive active mitochondrial revival for rescuing ischemic tissues. RMV comprises atomically dispersed ruthenium sites anchored within an oxygen-deficient manganese hydroxide matrix via synergistic Ru-O-Mn bridges. Benefiting from its intrinsic mitochondriotropic properties, RMV effectively intercepts aberrant electron leakage and breaks the self-amplifying cycle of ROS-induced ROS release through cascade multi-enzyme mimetic activities. Importantly, transcriptomic profiling and ultrastructural analysis reveal that RMV transcends passive antioxidant defense by functioning as a bioactive switch. It revives the suppressed SIRT1-PGC1α-TFAM signaling axis, fundamentally driving mitochondrial biogenesis and the reconstruction of functionally intact respiratory chains. In a murine stroke model, RMV treatment induces a 1.52-fold expansion of the neuronal mitochondrial biomass under ischemic stress, thereby suppressing neuronal apoptosis, reducing infarct volumes, and favorably reshaping an M2-polarized neuroimmune microenvironment. These integrated effects yield robust and sustained neurofunctional recovery. Our study shifts the neuroprotective paradigm from reactive damage control to active mitochondrial biogenesis, offering an atomically engineered strategy for ischemic stroke management.

Here, we report a bimetallic nanoactivator (RMV) designed to drive active mitochondrial revival for rescuing ischemic tissues.

title: Laminarin attenuates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by inhibiting Notch1 signaling and reprogramming microglial inflammatory responses.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuroinflammation contributes to cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, and microglial inflammatory responses are regulated in part by Notch signaling. This study investigated whether laminarin, a brown algae-derived β-glucan polysaccharide, protects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by modulating Notch1-dependent microglial responses.

METHODS: A rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion model was established, and laminarin was administered intraperitoneally at 10 mg/kg for seven consecutive days. Neurological deficits and infarct volume were assessed by modified neurological severity score and 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining. Transcriptomic and bioinformatic analyses were used to identify laminarin-associated pathways. BV2 microglial cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide, and Jagged1 was used to reactivate Notch signaling. Inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), Arginase 1 (Arg1), Notch pathway proteins, and inflammatory cytokines were examined by immunofluorescence, western blotting, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.

RESULTS: Laminarin reduced infarct volume and improved neurological recovery in rats. Bioinformatic analysis and immunofluorescence indicated involvement of the Notch pathway. In vivo and in vitro , laminarin decreased iNOS-associated pro-inflammatory activation and increased Arg1-associated reparative responses, accompanied by reduced Notch1/Hes1/Hes5 activation. Jagged1 attenuated these effects and partially reversed laminarin-mediated changes in inflammatory markers and cytokine production.

CONCLUSION: Laminarin attenuates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by reprogramming microglial inflammatory responses, at least partly through inhibition of the Notch1/Hes1/Hes5 signaling pathway. These findings support laminarin as a potential marine-derived immunomodulatory candidate for ischemic stroke research.

This study investigated whether laminarin, a brown algae-derived β-glucan polysaccharide, protects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by modulating Notch1-dependent microglial responses. METHODS: A rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion model was established, and laminarin was administered intraperitoneally at 10 mg/kg for seven consecutive days.

title: EXPRESS: Brain Age Gap from Non-Contrast CT Is Independently Associated with Functional Outcome after Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BackgroundOutcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) vary beyond lesion burden and clinical severity, suggesting a role for baseline structural brain vulnerability. We evaluated whether brain age gap (BrainAGE) derived from routine non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is associated with functional outcome after AIS.MethodsWe analyzed 1,173 AIS patients from a prospective multicenter cohort. A deep learning model estimated brain age from contralesional baseline NCCT to minimize lesion-related confounding. BrainAGE was defined as predicted minus chronological age. The primary outcome was 90-day functional status, assessed using proportional odds regression adjusted for age, sex, baseline stroke severity, early ischemic changes, and reperfusion therapy.ResultsBrainAGE was higher in AIS patients than in controls (+3.1 ± 9.1 years; p<0.001). Higher BrainAGE was associated with worse functional outcome after adjustment for age, sex, and other clinical predictors (POR 1.091 per 5 years; 95% CI 1.023-1.162; p=0.008). BrainAGE improved model fit but modestly improved discrimination.ConclusionsBrainAGE from routine NCCT provided modest incremental prognostic information beyond age and conventional clinical predictors. These findings support CT-based BrainAGE as a marker of brain health complementary to established prognostic factors. Whether BrainAGE improves patient-level risk stratification or clinical decision-making requires independent external validation and prospective evaluation.

We evaluated whether brain age gap (BrainAGE) derived from routine non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is associated with functional outcome after AIS.MethodsWe analyzed 1,173 AIS patients from a prospective multicenter cohort. A deep learning model estimated brain age from contralesional baseline NCCT to minimize lesion-related confounding.

title: Post-ischemic inhibition of the mitochondrial Ca2+ uniporter with Ru265 protects in ex vivo and in vivo models of cerebral ischemia.
abstract: Brain ischemia is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the aging population, yet no effective neuroprotective interventions currently exist. This therapeutic gap stems from two key challenges: the inability to deliver neuroprotective drugs before reperfusion and limited understanding of post-reperfusion events leading to delayed neurodegeneration. Zn2+ is an important contributor to ischemic brain injury, with mitochondrial Zn2+ uptake playing a central role in its neurotoxic effects. Ongoing Zn2+ accumulation occurs through the mitochondrial Ca2+ uniporter (MCU) in selectively vulnerable CA1 neurons after transient ischemia, contributing to delayed mitochondrial dysfunction. We previously demonstrated that post-ischemic administration of the non-selective MCU antagonist, ruthenium red attenuated neuronal damage in both an ex vivo oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) mouse brain slice model and in an in vivo rat cardiac arrest (CA) model. In the present study, we test post-ischemic treatment with Ru265, a novel selective MCU blocker, in both ischemic models. In the slice model, OGD induced delayed Zn2+ accumulation in CA1 neuronal mitochondria (as previously reported), followed by late-onset persistent mitochondrial depolarization and sustained elevation of cytoplasmic Ca2+ levels, indicating loss of Ca2+ homeostasis. Application of Ru265 after OGD termination inhibited the mitochondrial Zn2+ accumulation and largely prevented subsequent mitochondrial depolarization and loss of cytosolic Ca2+ homeostasis. In the CA model, intravenous Ru265 administration during cardiopulmonary resuscitation largely mitigated mitochondrial damage, markedly reduced neuronal injury and improved behavioral outcomes 20-24 h after ischemia. These findings suggest that post-ischemic MCU blockade may constitute a promising neuroprotective therapeutic strategy.
englishSummary: Brain ischemia is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the aging population, yet no effective neuroprotective interventions currently exist. This therapeutic gap stems from two key challenges: the inability to deliver neuroprotective drugs before reperfusion and limited understanding of post-reperfusion events leading to delayed neurodegeneration. Zn2+ is an important contributor to ischemic brain injury, with mitochondrial Zn2+ uptake playing a central role in its neurotoxic effects.

title: Geographic disparities and aging-related burden in reperfusion service output for acute ischemic stroke in China: A national sample spatial analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite expanding stroke centers, regional disparities and population aging challenge acute ischemic stroke (AIS) care in China. We aimed to map the spatial distribution of AIS reperfusion therapy and identify aging-related service mismatch.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed hospital-level data from 2,522 mainland Chinese hospitals participating in the Survey of National Stroke Telemedicine Treatment Project. Spatial analysis was used to assess service output distribution. Multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression evaluated factors associated with treatment efficiency. A four-quadrant matrix compared regional aging rates with observed thrombolysis volume to identify high-aging-burden, low-service-output mismatch.

FINDINGS: Thrombolysis output showed an east-to-west gradient that became more pronounced after adjusting for aging population. Compared with secondary and below hospitals, tertiary hospitals had a higher monthly thrombolysis volume (10 [5-16] versus 4 [2-8]) and shorter door-to-needle time (DNT) (43 [36-50] versus 48 [41-56]). Core service mismatch, defined by high aging and low output, was concentrated in county-and-below hospitals, which accounted for 70.9% of the total area. Aging rate was associated with achieving a median DNT of ≤60 min (absolute probability difference (%), 2.85; 95% confidence interval, 0.97-4.73; p = 0.003, per 10% increase). Exploratory analysis suggested that larger aging populations were associated with greater thrombolysis volume, which was, in turn, associated with shorter DNT.

CONCLUSION: Geographic disparities and service output mismatch persisted within China's AIS care network. Given the dual associations between population aging and reperfusion therapy service, capacity building in basic hospitals and demographic-based resource allocation may help align services with regional needs.

title: Pharmacological AQP4 inhibition attenuates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and modulates oxidative stress- and cell death-related signaling in mice.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury involves oxidative stress and changes in regulated cell death (RCD) pathways. Aquaporin-4 (AQP4), an astrocytic water channel, contributes to water homeostasis and has been implicated in edema, but whether its pharmacological inhibition alters injury-associated responses remains unclear. Male C57BL/6J mice underwent transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) and received AER-271, TGN-020, or vehicle. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, edema, protein expression, and subcellular localization were assessed using markers related to apoptosis (Bax, Bcl-2, cleaved caspase-3), necroptosis and pyroptosis (MLKL, GSDMD), autophagy (LC3-II, p62), ferroptosis-related defense (GPX4), and redox responses (HIF-1α, SOD1). I/R was accompanied by neurological impairment, infarction, edema, and changes in these markers, including increased Bax, cleaved caspase-3, MLKL, GSDMD, and HIF-1α; reduced Bcl-2, GPX4, and SOD1; and time-dependent changes in autophagy-related markers, with early LC3-II elevation followed by p62 accumulation. AER-271 treatment was associated with improved neurological outcomes and reduced infarct volume and edema. It was also associated with lower levels of apoptotic and lytic cell-death markers, altered autophagy-related marker profiles, normalization of redox-related markers, and reduced MLKL/GSDMD membrane redistribution. Similar changes were observed with TGN-020, although dosing regimens differed, potency was not assessed, and lack of a TGN-020-matched vehicle control limits definitive interpretation of these exploratory findings. These protein-level findings are correlative and do not establish causality. PANoptosome assembly, reactive oxygen species, lipid peroxidation, iron metabolism, autophagic flux, and perivascular AQP4 polarization were not assessed. Pharmacological AQP4 inhibition was associated with reduced I/R injury and changes in oxidative stress- and cell-death-related markers. These findings identify AQP4 inhibition as a candidate for further investigation, while causal links among AQP4, redox responses, autophagy and regulated cell death require direct validation in stroke.

Male C57BL/6J mice underwent transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) and received AER-271, TGN-020, or vehicle.

title: Targeting mitochondrial dysfunction and ferroptosis in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by a self-assembled nanomedicine with dual functions: GPX4 mimicry and energy metabolism restoration.
abstract: Neuronal apoptosis induced by mitochondrial dysfunction and neuronal ferroptosis induced by glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) inactivation are the root causes of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). Inspired by the "catalytic tetrad" of the GPX4 catalytic center, this study ingeniously developed a self-driving neural guardian nanomedicine (SNG). SNG successfully retains the most critical selenol group for GPX4's catalytic function and a strategically positioned carboxyl group in close proximity, allowing SNG to exhibit excellent GPX-mimicking activity. Due to the genipin-like group, SNG can autonomously navigate to target ischemic brain areas, and further precisely anchor to neuronal mitochondria. Based on its potent GPX4 mimetic activity and released active Se, SNG can fundamentally reverse neuronal ferroptosis. Furthermore, SNG itself possesses antioxidant properties and can spontaneously degrade to release genipin. Therefore, it ameliorates neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction during CIRI through the dual effects of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) scavenging and inhibition of excessive activation of mitochondrial uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2). SNG suppresses the release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), which subsequently inhibits inflammation. This work provides a breakthrough approach for the treatment of CIRI by synergistically inhibiting neuronal ferroptosis, neuronal apoptosis, and neuroinflammation, while also offering new directions for the treatment of other ischemia-reperfusion diseases.

title: PVT1 inhibition alleviates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and is associated with stroke diagnosis and severity via MyD88-mediated inflammatory signaling.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major cause of neurological disability. This study investigated the role of lncRNA PVT1 in I/R-induced cerebral injury and its clinical relevance. MCAO/reperfusion mouse and OGD/R neuronal cell models were established. Neurological function, infarct volume, brain edema, and neuronal apoptosis were assessed. For clinical validation, 50 acute ischemic stroke patients and 50 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum PVT1/miR-187-3p were measured by qRT-PCR; plasma MyD88 and inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-18) by ELISA. Machine learning (Random Forest) and correlation analyses were performed to evaluate diagnostic utility and relationships with clinical severity (NIHSS score, infarct volume). PVT1 was significantly upregulated under I/R both in vivo and in vitro. Clinically, AIS patients showed markedly elevated PVT1 (3.92 vs. 1.02, p < 0.0001) and reduced miR-187-3p (0.42 vs. 1.01, p < 0.0001), with increased MyD88 and inflammatory cytokines (all p < 0.001). The Random Forest model achieved AUC = 0.92, with PVT1 as the top predictor. PVT1 correlated positively with MyD88 (r = 0.68, p < 0.001) and NIHSS score (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). PVT1 silencing in MCAO mice significantly improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume and brain edema, and attenuated neuronal apoptosis (all p < 0.01). Mechanistically, PVT1 sponged miR-187-3p to derepress MyD88/TLR4 signaling, which was reversed by miR-187-3p restoration. In vivo rescue experiments confirmed that miR-187-3p antagomir reversed the protective effects of PVT1 silencing across multiple endpoints. PVT1 inhibition protects against cerebral I/R injury by restoring miR-187-3p and blocking the MyD88/TLR4 pathway. PVT1 and its downstream axis are associated with stroke diagnosis and severity, and represent promising therapeutic targets and diagnostic biomarkers for ischemic stroke.

title: Association of Advanced Age With Functional Recovery After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Large-core Ischemic Stroke.
abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Evidence supporting endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large-core ischemic stroke has expanded, but outcomes in patients aged ≥80 years remain insufficiently characterized. We evaluated outcomes after EVT in this population, with particular attention to prestroke disability-adjusted functional recovery.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with anterior-circulation large vessel occlusion and large-core stroke (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score 0 to 5 or CT perfusion core volume ≥50 mL) treated with EVT between October 2019 and September 2025. The primary outcome was prestroke disability-adjusted functional recovery, defined as 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≤ prestroke mRS + 1.

RESULTS: Among 377 patients, 75 were aged ≥80 years, and 302 were <80 years. Functional recovery occurred in 14.7% and 18.9%, respectively. Age ≥80 years was not significantly associated with functional recovery (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.45-2.22; p = 0.992). Patients aged ≥80 years had lower odds of mRS 0 to 3 (aOR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.21-0.79) and higher odds of mortality (aOR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.01-3.16). Successful reperfusion and hemorrhagic outcomes did not differ significantly between groups. Each 10-year increase in age was associated with lower odds of functional recovery (aOR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.46-0.77).

CONCLUSION: Among selected patients aged ≥80 years with large-core ischemic stroke, successful reperfusion and functional recovery remained achievable after EVT, despite poorer conventional functional outcomes and higher mortality. Advancing age was associated with progressively worse outcomes when modeled continuously. These findings support individualized prognostic assessment after EVT rather than reliance on chronological age alone.

We evaluated outcomes after EVT in this population, with particular attention to prestroke disability-adjusted functional recovery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with anterior-circulation large vessel occlusion and large-core stroke (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score 0 to 5 or CT perfusion core volume ≥50 mL) treated with EVT between October 2019 and September 2025.

title: Microglia promote infiltration and polarization of macrophages in cerebral ischemia‑reperfusion via the reactive oxygen species‑SPI1‑CCL9 axis.
abstract: The aim of the present study was to investigate the role of microglia in promoting macrophage infiltration and polarization during cerebral ischemia‑reperfusion (I/R) injury through the reactive oxygen species (ROS)‑Spi‑1 proto‑oncogene (SPI1)‑chemokine (C‑C motif) ligand 9 (CCL9) signalling axis. Using a cerebral I/R in vitro and in vivo model, microglial activation and macrophage dynamics were assessed. ROS levels were quantified, and SPI1 expression in microglia was analysed. CCL9 secretion was measured, and its impact on macrophage migration and polarization was evaluated in vitro. CCL9 antibody and RNA interference approaches were used to interrogate the signalling pathway. Following cerebral I/R, microglial activation led to increased ROS production, and increased SPI1 and CCL9 expression. This, in turn, increased CCL9 secretion, which attracted macrophages to the site of ischemia and promoted their polarization towards a pro‑inflammatory phenotype. Inhibition of the ROS‑SPI1‑CCL9 axis significantly reduced macrophage infiltration and altered their polarization state. The results of the present study demonstrated that microglia facilitated macrophage infiltration and polarization in cerebral I/R via the ROS‑SPI1‑CCL9 axis, highlighting a potential therapeutic target for mitigating neuroinflammatory damage after a cerebral ischemic stroke.

Using a cerebral I/R in vitro and in vivo model, microglial activation and macrophage dynamics were assessed. ROS levels were quantified, and SPI1 expression in microglia was analysed.
