title: Ghrelin treatment is associated with attenuated microglial inflammation and preserved mitochondrial integrity after cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CI/RI) causes neurological disability. Microglial inflammation and mitochondrial apoptosis are key pathological events. Ghrelin's role in these processes following CI/RI remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To examine whether ghrelin treatment is associated with reduced microglial inflammation and preserved mitochondrial integrity in CI/RI models, using in vitro OGD/R primary microglia and in vivo MCAO rat models.

METHODS: Primary microglia underwent OGD/R (8 h/24 h) with ghrelin (0.1-1 mM). Cell viability, apoptosis, GHSR, inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-8), ROS, ATP, mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), and ultrastructure were measured. Rats underwent MCAO (2 h/24 h) and received ghrelin (50 μg/kg/d, i.p.) or saline for 7 days. Infarct volume, histology, IBA-1, mitochondrial complexes I/IV, cytochrome c distribution, NF-κB p65 translocation, TNF-α/IL-1β/IL-6, and Bcl-2/Bax/Caspase-9 were assessed.

RESULTS: In OGD/R-exposed microglia, ghrelin dose-dependently attenuated viability loss and apoptosis, restored GHSR, reduced TNF-α/IL-6/IL-8, lowered ROS, increased ATP, and preserved ΔΨm and ultrastructure. In MCAO rats, ghrelin treatment was associated with smaller infarct volume, less neuronal damage, lower IBA-1, restored ATP and complexes I/IV, increased mitochondrial cytochrome c retention, reduced NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation, decreased TNF-α/IL-1β/IL-6, and altered Bcl-2/Bax/Caspase-9 (higher Bcl-2 and full-length Caspase-9, lower Bax).

CONCLUSION: In both models, ghrelin treatment correlates with attenuated microglial inflammation and preserved mitochondrial integrity. These findings indicate a potential protective association of ghrelin against CI/RI.

title: Proanthocyanidin ameliorates BCCAO-induced neuroinflammation in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) in rats by targeting NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome pathway.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is a major cause of mortality and long-term neurological disability, characterized by excessive oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neuronal degeneration following the restoration of cerebral blood flow. The present study investigated the neuroprotective effects of proanthocyanidin (PAC) against bilateral common carotid artery occlusion (BCCAO)-induced cerebral ischemia in Wistar albino rats, with particular emphasis on the NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling pathway. Rats subjected to BCCAO received PAC at two dose levels or standard therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel). Neurological and cognitive functions were evaluated using the rotarod, actophotometer, and elevated plus maze tests. Biochemical assays were performed to determine oxidative stress markers and antioxidant enzyme activities, while histopathological examination assessed neuronal integrity. The molecular mechanism was further investigated by Western blot analysis and densitometric quantification of NF-κB (p65), NLRP3, and caspase-1 protein expression. BCCAO significantly impaired motor coordination, locomotor activity, and memory retention, accompanied by increased lipid peroxidation, myeloperoxidase, and acetylcholinesterase activities, depletion of endogenous antioxidants (glutathione, superoxide dismutase, and catalase), and marked neuronal degeneration in the hippocampal and cortical regions. PAC treatment significantly improved behavioral performance, restored antioxidant defense, reduced oxidative stress and biochemical alterations, and preserved neuronal architecture in a dose-dependent manner. Western blot analysis demonstrated that PAC markedly downregulated the overexpression of NF-κB (p65), NLRP3, and caspase-1 proteins, indicating suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated neuroinflammation. Overall, PAC exhibited significant neuroprotective efficacy comparable to aspirin plus clopidogrel, suggesting that its beneficial effects are mediated through the attenuation of oxidative stress and the inhibition of NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling. These findings support PAC as a promising phytotherapeutic candidate for the management of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.

title: ATP-sensitive potassium channel openers inhibit the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps to protect against neuroinflammation in ischemic stroke.
abstract: Neuroinflammation is a key contributor to brain injury and poor functional recovery after ischemic stroke, yet no clinically approved therapy targets the neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-cGAS-STING axis that drives it. This study investigates the effects of the clinically used K-ATP channel opener nicorandil on neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and evaluates its potential to attenuate NET-cGAS-STING-associated neuroinflammation. A mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion (MCAO/R) and BV-2 microglial cell oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) were used to assess NET formation, cGAS-STING pathway activation, inflammatory responses, and neurological injury. Significant increases in NET markers, such as MPO-DNA and CitH3, were found in plasma and brain tissue after MCAO/R. This was accompanied by elevated TNF-α, IL-6,IL-1β, brain edema, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits. Both DNase I-mediated NET degradation and Nicorandil treatment reduced NET formation, suppressed microglial activation, lowered phosphorylation of STING and TBK1, and alleviated brain infarction, neuronal death, and impairment. In vitro, exogenous NETs enhanced OGD/R-induced cGAS-STING activation and IL-1β release, effects reversed by DNase I and Nicorandil. In summary, extracellular DNA associated with NETs promotes microglial cGAS-STING activation and contributes to neuroinflammatory injury after stroke. Nicorandil exerts neuroprotective effects by inhibiting the upstream formation of NETs and attenuating this signaling axis, suggesting a promising and readily translatable therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke.

This study investigates the effects of the clinically used K-ATP channel opener nicorandil on neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and evaluates its potential to attenuate NET-cGAS-STING-associated neuroinflammation. title: Benzbromarone Attenuates Collagen-evoked Platelet Activation and Cerebral Ischemia-reperfusion Injury in a Rat Model.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Benzbromarone (BBR), a clinical drug for gout, has recently been identified as an inhibitor of Heat Shock Protein 47 (HSP47). HSP47 is known to participate in platelet- collagen interactions and thrombus formation. However, whether BBR exerts antiplatelet and neuroprotective effects in ischemic stroke remains unclear.

METHODS: Bleeding risk and cytotoxicity of BBR were assessed using tail bleeding time, coagulation parameters, LDH and CCK-8 assays, with aspirin and clopidogrel as comparators. The effects of BBR (1, 5, 10 μM) on collagen-induced platelet aggregation, adhesion, calcium mobilization and clot retraction were examined. The antithrombotic potential of BBR was evaluated in a FeCl3-induced carotid artery thrombosis model, and its neuroprotective potential in a Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion (MCAO) model in rats. Phosphorylation levels of the Syk-PLCγ2-PKC and PI3K-Akt-GSK3β pathways were detected by western blotting.

RESULTS: In this study, BBR exhibited low bleeding risk and low cytotoxicity, similar to aspirin and clopidogrel. BBR dose-dependently reduced collagen-induced platelet aggregation, adhesion, [Ca2+] mobilization, and clot retraction. BBR delayed the Time to Occlusion (TTO) and inhibited arterial thrombosis. In MCAO rats, BBR also reduced infarct volume and ameliorated neurological deficits. Western blotting revealed that BBR decreased the phosphorylation levels of proteins in the Syk-PLCγ2-PKC and PI3K-Akt-GSK3β pathways.

DISCUSSION: As a known inhibitor of HSP47, BBR may suppress collagen-induced platelet activation and arterial thrombosis, possibly through modulating downstream signaling pathways of GPVI. Compared with conventional antiplatelet agents, BBR showed a favorable safety profile in rats, without significantly prolonging bleeding time or affecting liver and kidney function. These findings suggest that BBR represents a promising antiplatelet candidate with both efficacy and safety for ischemic stroke management.

CONCLUSION: The present study demonstrates that BBR inhibits platelet activation and thrombosis, and attenuates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats. Its protective effect may be associated with suppression of GPVI-related signaling pathways. BBR thus warrants further investigation as a potential candidate for acute-stage treatment of ischemic stroke.

HSP47 is known to participate in platelet- collagen interactions and thrombus formation. However, whether BBR exerts antiplatelet and neuroprotective effects in ischemic stroke remains unclear.

title: An endoplasmic reticulum-targeted near-infrared fluorogenic probe reveals butyrylcholinesterase upregulation and baicalein-mediated neuroprotection in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
abstract: The cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway is an important neuroimmune regulatory axis that endogenously counteracts cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). As a key hydrolase in the cholinergic system, there remains a lack of direct imaging evidence regarding changes in BChE during this pathological process. To address this challenge, we developed DCIO-B, an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-targeted near-infrared fluorogenic (NIRF) probe, to track changes in BChE activity during CIRI at both the cellular and in vivo levels. Upon catalysis by BChE, DCIO-B produced a detectable fluorescence response at 660 nm with a detection limit of 0.041 U/mL and maintained a stable response across a wide pH range. In PC12 cells, iso-OMPA markedly blocked fluorescence, while hydrocortisone and forskolin induced opposite fluorescence changes, demonstrating that DCIO-B could visualize the bidirectional regulation of endogenous BChE. Following OGD/R treatment, intracellular BChE protein expression increased, and enhanced DCIO-B fluorescence was observed. In MCAO/R mice, brain fluorescence rapidly increased following tail-vein injection of DCIO-B, indicating elevated BChE activity. Treatment with baicalein decreased brain fluorescence signals, reduced the extent of cerebral infarction, and improved neuronal histological damage. The results verified that BChE activity increased in CIRI and provided a reliable NIRF probe, DCIO-B, for the diagnosis and intervention of CIRI.

title: Niwan Bazhen acupuncture activates CLEC3B-Mediated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway to suppress autophagy and exerts neuroprotection against ischemic stroke.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is one of the leading causes of disability and mortality worldwide. Excessive autophagy triggered by cerebral ischemia exacerbates neuronal apoptosis and necrosis. Acupuncture at Niwan Bazhen (Acu) has unique advantages in stroke rehabilitation, and our previous studies have demonstrated its ability to alleviate neuronal apoptosis after IS. However, the mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects remain elusive. Transcriptomic microarray expression profiling revealed that C-type lectin domain family 3 member B (CLEC3B) was significantly downregulated in the brain of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rats, and this downregulation was reversed by Acu. Lentivirus-mediated overexpression of CLEC3B improved neurological function, reduced cerebral infarction, and alleviated cerebral edema in MCAO/R rats, and decreased neuronal apoptosis in the peri-infarct cortex. Western blot analysis demonstrated that CLEC3B overexpression activated the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, reduced the LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, and decreased autophagosome numbers. Conversely, knockdown of CLEC3B nearly abolished the neuroprotective effects of Acu in MCAO/R rats. In vitro, CLEC3B dificiency inhibited the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and impaired autophagic flux in rat cortical neurons under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) conditions. Treatment of OGD/R-exposed rat cortical neurons with recombinant CLEC3B protein or CLEC3B-overexresing lentivirus activated the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and inhibited autophagy, an effect that was abrogated by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Collectively, these findings indicate that CLEC3B, as a core target of Acu regulation, exerts neuroprotection against IS by inhibiting excessive neuronal autophagy via activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway.

Excessive autophagy triggered by cerebral ischemia exacerbates neuronal apoptosis and necrosis. Acupuncture at Niwan Bazhen (Acu) has unique advantages in stroke rehabilitation, and our previous studies have demonstrated its ability to alleviate neuronal apoptosis after IS.

title: Neutrophil-hitchhiking and microglia-homing liposomes co-delivering artemisinin and edaravone for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury treatment.
abstract: Clinical outcomes of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) remain unsatisfactory, largely because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts the delivery of most neuroprotective agents to the brain parenchyma. Although artemisinin (ART) and edaravone (EDV) have shown promising therapeutic potential for CIRI, their clinical application is hindered by their short in vivo half-lives and poor aqueous solubility. Neutrophil infiltration triggered by CIRI provides a unique opportunity for drug delivery across the BBB, whereas targeted modulation of microglia represents a key strategy for mitigating reperfusion-induced injury. However, existing neutrophil hitchhiking delivery systems primarily focus on BBB traversal and generally lack a secondary targeting mechanism to promote preferential drug accumulation within the inflammatory core of the ischemic brain. Here, we developed a dual-modified liposomal system functionalized with sialic acid (SA) and phosphatidylserine (PS) (ART/EDV-PS/SAL) for the co-delivery of ART and EDV. This system enables sequential two-step targeting through SA-mediated neutrophil hitchhiking for BBB traversal, followed by PS-mediated microglial homing within ischemic brain tissue. In a mouse model of CIRI, ART/EDV-PS/SAL markedly reduced cerebral infarct volume, preserved BBB integrity, and significantly improved neurological and behavioral outcomes. Mechanistically, ART/EDV-PS/SAL exerted neuroprotective effects by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation, attenuating pyroptosis, and promoting microglial polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. By harnessing endogenous immune cells to achieve efficient and sequential drug targeting, this study establishes a promising nanodelivery platform for the treatment of ischemic stroke and other neuroinflammatory disorders.

Although artemisinin (ART) and edaravone (EDV) have shown promising therapeutic potential for CIRI, their clinical application is hindered by their short in vivo half-lives and poor aqueous solubility. Neutrophil infiltration triggered by CIRI provides a unique opportunity for drug delivery across the BBB, whereas targeted modulation of microglia represents a key strategy for mitigating reperfusion-induced injury.

title: Characteristic Dihydrophenanthrenes from Spiranthes sinensis with Therapeutic Potential for Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Spiranthes sinensis, known as "Panlongshen", is an edible traditional Chinese medicine, widely used in herbal teas and health-promoting foods. In this study, we investigated the neuroprotective properties of S. sinensis against ischemic stroke for the first time. Bioactivity-guided isolation yielded 19 dihydrophenanthrenes, including 9 undescribed compounds (7a/7b, 9-11, 12a/12b-13a/13b). These dihydrophenanthrenes demonstrated significant antineuroinflammatory activity against NO production in LPS-induced BV-2 microglia cells, with IC50 values ranging from 1.5 to 34.8 μM, which were greater than that of the positive drug (minocycline, IC50: 34.9 μM). Furthermore, coelonin (2) reduced inflammatory cytokines in BV-2 microglia and preserved PC12 cells' viability under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Mechanistic investigations revealed that coelonin (2) exerts its antineuroinflammatory effects by targeting MAP3K7 and suppressing the NF-κB signaling cascade. In vivo, coelonin alleviated ischemic-reperfusion injury after MCAO. These findings revealed the neuroprotective and anti-ischemic stroke effects of S. sinensis and identified dihydrophenanthrenes as its key active constituents.

title: Stage-Associated Efficacy of Systemically Administered Neural Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in Ischemic Stroke through the Prevention of Cx43 Degradation.
abstract: Ischemic stroke pathology is highly dynamic, making the optimal timing for biological interventions highly elusive. This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. The in vivo evaluations identified a restricted therapeutic window closely associated with the temporal evolution of the ischemic microenvironment. Early exosome intervention (4 or 24 h post-ischemia) significantly reduced infarct volume, restored blood-brain barrier integrity, and improved neurological functional recovery. In contrast, delayed administration (48 h) failed to reduce the mortality rate and provide meaningful neuroprotection. To examine the molecular basis of this time dependence, we integrated temporal proteomic profiling of the ischemic penumbra with small RNA sequencing of NSC-Exos. The analytical and functional data suggest that early NSC-Exo delivery transfers miR-9-5p to suppress Nedd4 expression, thereby restoring the Connexin 43 protein pool and stabilizing the astrocytic network to halt initial microenvironmental collapse. Collectively, this study underscores the critical importance of intervention timing and provides a potential translational strategy for utilizing NSC-Exos as a targeted, stage-specific therapy in acute ischemic stroke.

This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. title: Research progress on neurovascular and neuroimmune interactions during thrombolysis and reperfusion in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains a leading cause of adult mortality and lasting disability worldwide. Although intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy have established the reperfusion era, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve favorable functional outcomes because macrovascular recanalization does not guarantee effective perfusion at the tissue level. This review systematically examines the neurovascular unit (NVU) and the expanded neurovascular immune network as integrated frameworks for understanding brain injury following reperfusion. We delineate the temporal cascade of pathophysiological events, beginning with acute ischemic energy failure, excitotoxicity, and innate immune sensing by cerebral microvascular endothelial cells and microglia. We then focus on the reperfusion phase as the critical window of neuroimmune interaction, characterized by reactive oxygen species burst, nod-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation, and matrix-metalloproteinase (MMP) mediated disruption of the blood-brain-barrier (BBB). The chronological infiltration and phenotypic transitions of peripheral immune cells, including neutrophils, classical monocytes, and T lymphocytes, are analyzed in relation to biphasic dynamics of the BBB and evolving therapeutic time windows. Furthermore, we evaluate translational advances in combination strategies that pair agents with anti-inflammatory properties and thrombolysis, interventions targeting NETs, blood brain barrier protection, and immunomodulation strategies tailored to specific time windows, alongside emerging biomarkers and novel delivery technologies. This review aims to provide a framework grounded in evidence for mechanistic understanding and therapeutic optimization toward comprehensive neurovascular and neuroimmune repair in the reperfusion era. Unless otherwise specified, mechanistic findings cited in this review derive predominantly from experimental rodent models (mainly transient middle cerebral artery occlusion, tMCAO) or in vitro studies, and human evidence is explicitly indicated where available.

Although intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy have established the reperfusion era, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve favorable functional outcomes because macrovascular recanalization does not guarantee effective perfusion at the tissue level. This review systematically examines the neurovascular unit (NVU) and the expanded neurovascular immune network as integrated frameworks for understanding brain injury following reperfusion.

title: Traditional Chinese medicine interventions and mitochondrial communication in myocardial and cerebral ischemia: a critical review.
abstract: Myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke share mitochondrial disturbances, but evidence that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) interventions regulate mitochondrial communication rather than general mitochondrial injury remains uncertain. This critical review evaluates that distinction. A structured search of PubMed, Lens Scholarly Search, and CNKI from inception to 28 August 2026 identified 1,663 records; 29 reports (24 preclinical/mechanistic and 5 clinical or systematic-review reports) informed the focused evidence map. We organized the evidence across four levels: intramitochondrial coordination, communication among mitochondria, contacts between mitochondria and other organelles, and intercellular mitochondrial signaling. Selected formulations, botanical drugs, and plant metabolites were associated most consistently with calcium-redox balance, bioenergetics, mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, and immune-metabolic responses. However, most studies measured static proteins or downstream injury markers, used preventive dosing or poorly defined exposure, and did not test direct target engagement. Evidence for altered organelle contacts or transfer of intact mitochondria was sparse. Clinical studies of selected standardized commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations reported possible functional benefits, but product heterogeneity, trial limitations, and the absence of mitochondrial pharmacodynamic biomarkers preclude mechanistic attribution. We therefore distinguish communication-specific evidence from pathway association and appraise product identity, exposure plausibility, causal validation, methodological quality, and clinical relevance. Future studies should use taxonomically authenticated and chemically characterized preparations, clinically achievable dosing, dynamic communication-specific assays, causal perturbation, and prospectively defined mitochondrial biomarkers. Current evidence supports mitochondrial communication as a useful hypothesis-generating framework, but not yet as an established clinical mechanism of TCM in myocardial or cerebral ischemia.

title: Impact of human serum albumin in acute large-core ischemic stroke: an exploratory randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion with a large ischemic core remains associated with substantial disability despite successful endovascular therapy (EVT). Human serum albumin (HSA) has shown neuroprotective effects in preclinical models, but its clinical benefit after successful reperfusion is uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, prospective, open-label, endpoint-blinded exploratory randomized controlled trial in 60 adults with anterior-circulation large-core acute ischemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion. Participants were randomized 1:1 before EVT. After angiographic confirmation of successful reperfusion (eTICI 2b-3), the albumin group received 100 mL of 20% HSA intravenously and the control group received 100 mL of normal saline with matched timing. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2). Net water uptake (NWU) was an exploratory imaging biomarker; symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) and 90-day mortality were safety outcomes.

RESULTS: All 60 randomized participants achieved successful reperfusion, received the allocated intervention, and were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. In the albumin and control groups, respectively, 21/30 (70.0%) and 20/30 (66.7%) participants were male; mean ± SD age was 68.0 ± 9.3 and 66.3 ± 10.7 years, admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 16.3 ± 4.8 and 16.4 ± 7.1, and admission Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) on noncontrast CT (NCCT) was 5.0 ± 1.5 and 4.9 ± 1.3. Functional independence occurred in 11/30 participants (36.7%) in each group (risk ratio, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.51-1.94]; risk difference, 0.0 percentage points [95% CI, -24.4 to 24.4]; odds ratio, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.35-2.86]; Fisher exact p = 1.000). The NWU treatment-by-time interaction was not statistically significant (Wald chi-square = 3.40, 2 df; p = 0.182). sICH occurred in 2/30 participants (6.7%) in each group, and 90-day mortality occurred in 2/30 (6.7%) versus 4/30 (13.3%).

CONCLUSION: In this small exploratory randomized trial, immediate post-reperfusion 20% HSA did not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in 90-day functional independence or NWU. Wide confidence intervals do not exclude clinically meaningful benefit or harm; larger adequately powered multicenter trials are needed.

Human serum albumin (HSA) has shown neuroprotective effects in preclinical models, but its clinical benefit after successful reperfusion is uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a single-center, prospective, open-label, endpoint-blinded exploratory randomized controlled trial in 60 adults with anterior-circulation large-core acute ischemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion.

title: Thrombus stiffness depends on occlusion site and influences thrombectomy outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Only 60% of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) achieve successful reperfusion after the first endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) attempt. In vitro studies have shown that thrombus stiffness influences thrombus-device interaction and retrieval efficacy. This prospective observational study investigates how thrombus stiffness relates to clinical factors, thrombus imaging characteristics and histological composition. It further explores the association between thrombus stiffness and EVT success, as measured by the modified first-pass reperfusion (mFPR).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 281 thrombus samples were collected from 51 AIS patients undergoing EVT. Thrombus stiffness was quantified using compressive mechanical testing, composition from histological staining and radiological characteristics from pre-interventional non-contrast computed tomography (CT) and CT angiography. Statistical analysis was performed using linear and logistic mixed-effects regression models.

RESULTS: Thrombi retrieved from the proximal M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery showed significant lower stiffness (0.236 kPa, 95% CI, 0.136-0.409) compared to those from the M1 segment (0.760 kPa, 95% CI, 0.492-1.174) and from the ICA (1.106 kPa, 95% CI, 0.558-2.192). Occlusion location was the strongest clinical marker of thrombus stiffness. Adjusted mFPR probability was 40.4% (95% CI, 24.5-67.0) for thrombi retrieved from the ICA, 89.7% (95% CI, 79.5-97.0) for M1 occlusions, and 53.0% (95% CI, 30.8-84.7) for M2 occlusions.

CONCLUSION: Thrombi in distal vessels of the anterior cerebral circulation are significantly softer than those in proximal intracranial arteries. First-pass EVT success is lower for the stiffest thrombi from the ICA and for the softest thrombi from M2, providing a foundation for future biomechanically informed thrombus removal strategies to optimise AIS treatment.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Only 60% of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) achieve successful reperfusion after the first endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) attempt. In vitro studies have shown that thrombus stiffness influences thrombus-device interaction and retrieval efficacy. This prospective observational study investigates how thrombus stiffness relates to clinical factors, thrombus imaging characteristics and histological composition.

title: Stable In-Hospital Mortality Despite Increasing Thrombectomy Use in Young Adults With Ischemic Stroke: A Nationwide Study in Spain (2016-2022).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) in young adults is increasing in incidence and carries a disproportionate socioeconomic burden. The adoption of reperfusion therapies, particularly mechanical thrombectomy, has transformed stroke care; however, their impact on mortality in this low-risk population remains uncertain.

METHODS: We performed a nationwide, population-based retrospective study using the Spanish Minimum Basic Data Set (MBDS), including all hospital admissions for IS in patients aged 18-50 years from 2016 to 2022. Temporal trends in admissions, reperfusion therapies, and in-hospital mortality were assessed. Independent predictors of mortality were identified using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 20,533 admissions, the number of hospitalizations increased over time, accompanied by a rise in reperfusion therapies. Mechanical thrombectomy rates nearly doubled from 6.3% in 2016 to 12.1% in 2022 (p < 0.001). Despite this expansion, in-hospital mortality remained low and stable throughout the study period (2.8%). Mortality was independently associated with malignant neoplasm (OR 8.45), followed by orotracheal intubation (OR 4.85), coma (OR 3.73), cerebral edema (OR 2.16), acute kidney injury (OR 1.85), acute respiratory failure (OR 1.38), posterior circulation stroke (OR 1.42), and All Patient Refined Diagnosis Related Groups (APR-DRG) mortality risk level (all p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In young adults with IS, the expansion of reperfusion therapies was not associated with reduced in-hospital mortality, which remained low over time. Malignant neoplasm was the strongest independent predictor of death, followed by acute neurological complications and organ dysfunction. These findings highlight the need for further multicentre clinical research to better understand the causes of death in young adults with IS.

title: Neuroprotective Mechanisms of Electroacupuncture at Baihui (GV20) in Experimental Ischemic Stroke: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Ischemic stroke is a major cause of death and disability, and reperfusion therapy has a narrow time window and may cause further injury after recanalization. Baihui (GV20) is the acupoint used most often in experimental studies of acupuncture for stroke, and electroacupuncture (EA) at GV20, applied alone or combined with other acupoints, has been tested in a large body of animal work. Taking GV20 as its organizing focus, this review systematically summarizes the mechanisms by which GV20-based EA protects against ischemic stroke in animal models. GV20-based EA has been reported to reduce neuroinflammation through the α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor-high-mobility group box 1 pathway, nuclear factor-κB and inflammasome signaling, and glial responses; to prevent apoptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis and engage adenosine A1 receptor signaling; to preserve mitochondrial dynamics, energy metabolism, and redox balance; to protect the blood-brain barrier and promote cerebral perfusion and angiogenesis; and to enhance neurotrophic signaling, synaptic plasticity, and white matter repair. GV20 alone has been studied mainly as preconditioning, and GV20-based combinations have been applied primarily after ischemia; the effects on hypoxia-inducible factor-1α, autophagy, and microglial polarization vary with the timing of EA and assessment. Because these findings derive largely from young, healthy rodents and most mechanistic results are based on changes in expression, they do not yet support direct clinical application; future studies should compare GV20 alone with GV20-based combinations under the same conditions and validate key mechanisms with causal designs in clinically relevant models.

title: Early Fibrinogen-to-Albumin Ratio and Poor Functional Outcome After Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR) has been linked to functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke, but reported exposure definitions and numerical scales vary. We assessed whether higher early FAR was associated with poor functional outcome.

METHODS: We searched five databases through July 23, 2026 for adult acute ischemic stroke studies that measured FAR during initial assessment or before reperfusion and reported adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for modified Rankin Scale outcomes. Categorical and continuous estimates were pooled separately using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs). Continuous effects were harmonized to a common FAR_100 scale. We performed leave-one-out, scale-restriction, and reperfusion analyses and assessed risk of bias with Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS). The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261459955).

RESULTS: Twelve studies included 13,253 participants; 12,579 contributed effect estimates. Study-defined higher FAR was associated with poor outcome (five studies; 10,968 participants; OR, 2.32; 95% CI: 1.37-3.91; I2 = 82.7%). Across seven continuous studies (1611 participants), each 1-unit increase in FAR_100 was associated with poor outcome (OR, 1.30; 95% CI: 1.14-1.48; I2 = 51.1%). Leave-one-out CIs remained above 1. Excluding studies requiring scale conversion produced a similar estimate (five studies; 1173 participants; OR, 1.29; 95% CI: 1.16-1.45; I2 = 10.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher early FAR was associated with poor functional outcome in both categorical and continuous analyses. Prospective studies should test whether FAR adds prognostic information to established stroke models. Available evidence came from observational studies.

We assessed whether higher early FAR was associated with poor functional outcome. METHODS: We searched five databases through July 23, 2026 for adult acute ischemic stroke studies that measured FAR during initial assessment or before reperfusion and reported adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for modified Rankin Scale outcomes.

title: KDM4B Knockdown Attenuates Neurological Deficits in Ischemic Stroke by Inhibiting Neuronal Apoptosis Associated With Birc5 Upregulation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: KDM4B (Lysine demethylase 4B), a histone lysine demethylase, exerts a crucial epigenetic regulatory role in the progression of numerous disorders by catalyzing demethylation reactions on target proteins. However, the precise biological function and molecular mechanism by which KDM4B regulates neurological deficits in ischemic stroke remains elusive.

METHODS: In this study, we employed a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in HT22 neurons to mimic ischemic stroke. Targeted loss-of-function approaches were executed utilizing in vivo siRNA delivery and in vitro lentiviral shRNA transduction. The neuroprotective effects were systematically evaluated through infarct volume quantification, histopathological staining, and diverse sensorimotor behavioral tests. Furthermore, transcriptomic profiling (RNA-seq) coupled with molecular biology assays was performed to elucidate the downstream apoptotic cascades and key targets governed by KDM4B.

RESULTS: Herein, we found that KDM4B is predominantly localized in neurons, with its expression significantly decreasing initially and then gradually increasing following ischemic stroke. Loss-of-function experiments demonstrated that KDM4B knockdown mitigated brain damage, attenuated tissue structure disruption, and improved sensorimotor dysfunctions in mice with ischemic stroke. Additionally, KDM4B knockdown protected neurons against OGD/R insult. Furthermore, KDM4B knockdown inhibited the expression of Bax and the activation of the pro-apoptotic caspase cascade (caspase-3/6/7/8/9), while upregulating the expression of the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2, thereby reducing neuronal apoptosis. Mechanistically, KDM4B knockdown is associated with an upregulation of Birc5 expression, which in turn inhibits apoptotic progression in neurons.

CONCLUSIONS: These results demonstrate that KDM4B knockdown alleviates neurological deficits following ischemic stroke by inhibiting neuronal apoptosis, partially accompanied by Birc5.

However, the precise biological function and molecular mechanism by which KDM4B regulates neurological deficits in ischemic stroke remains elusive. METHODS: In this study, we employed a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in HT22 neurons to mimic ischemic stroke.

title: Early Acupuncture Following Thrombolysis in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials on Efficacy and Safety.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intravenous thrombolysis is standard for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but many patients still have poor outcomes. Acupuncture may confer additional neuroprotection, yet its safety and efficacy when initiated early post-thrombolysis remain unclear.

METHODS: A systematic search of databases and registries was conducted from inception to March 31, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing thrombolysis plus acupuncture with thrombolysis plus conventional post-thrombolytic care in AIS patients within 14 days of onset. Meta-analyses were performed using mean differences (MD) or risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; publication bias was evaluated via Egger's test. Pre-specified subgroup analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Ten trials (1116 patients) were included. Adjunctive acupuncture reduced neurological deficit (NIHSS MD -2.90, 95% CI -3.62 to -2.17), improved activities of daily living (Barthel Index MD 12.07, 95% CI 8.10-16.03), and increased clinical response (RR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11-1.21; all p < 0.001). Adverse events did not differ significantly (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.25-1.08). Only one study reported symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (zero acupuncture vs. six control). Benefits were consistent across subgroups.

CONCLUSION: In AIS patients receiving thrombolysis, acupuncture initiated early following thrombolysis improves neurological and functional outcomes. In available safety data, adverse events did not differ significantly between groups; however, systematic surveillance for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage was lacking in most trials. These findings support further rigorous evaluation of early post-thrombolysis acupuncture in adequately monitored randomized trials.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261358943.

METHODS: A systematic search of databases and registries was conducted from inception to March 31, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing thrombolysis plus acupuncture with thrombolysis plus conventional post-thrombolytic care in AIS patients within 14 days of onset.

title: Intranuclear localisation of KLF3-AS1 under the balance of histone acetylation and methylation in BMSCs ameliorates cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury by preserving microglial mitochondrial function and inhibiting inflammatory polarisation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischaemic stroke occurs when blood flow to the brain is obstructed. Rapid restoration of blood supply frequently induces cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury (CIRI). Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC)-derived exosomes exhibit promising therapeutic potential for CIRI. In-depth exploration of their therapeutic mechanisms holds crucial significance for CIRI management.

METHODS: The middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO) model was established in mice. An in vitro ischaemic stroke model was established by treating BV-2 cells with oxygen‒glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Exosomes were isolated from BMSCs and intranasally administrated into mice or added into BV-2 cells. Neurological deficits, grasping and coordination function were evaluated. Cell viability, apoptosis, proliferation and migration were examined. The localisation of KLF3-AS1 was examined by combined staining of immunofluorescence and fluorescence in situ hybridisation. Intracellular Ca2+ and adenosine triphosphate levels, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and membrane potential were assessed.

RESULTS: KLF3-AS1 enhanced BMSC viability, proliferation and migration, accompanied by epigenetic reprogramming at its promoter characterised by increased H3K27 acetylation (H3K27Ac) and decreased H3K27 trimethylation (H3K27Me3). BMSC-derived KLF3-AS1-enriched exosomes indicated therapeutic efficacy in both in vivo and in vitro models of cerebral ischaemia. In MCAO-induced mice, these exosomes alleviated neurological deficits and shifted microglial polarisation from pro-inflammatory M1-like to anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotypes. Similar effects were observed in OGD/R-treated BV-2 microglia, where KLF3-AS1-enriched exosomes attenuated oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction while upregulating Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3) expression. Mechanistically, KLF3-AS1 facilitated ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) nuclear translocation to activate SIRT3 transcription in microglia, and inhibition of SIRT3 abolished the neuroprotective effects of exosomal KLF3-AS1.

CONCLUSION: BMSC-derived exosomes delivering KLF3-AS1 ameliorates CIRI by preserving microglial mitochondrial function and inhibiting inflammatory polarisation, highlighting KLF3-AS1 as a critical epigenetic regulator and exosome-mediated therapeutic agent for CIRI through the ETV4/SIRT3 axis.

KEY POINTS/HIGHLIGHTS: KLF3-AS1 enhances bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) function via promoter H3K27Ac/H3K27Me3 reprogramming. KLF3‑AS1 directly binds ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) to activate Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3), preserving mitochondrial integrity. BMSC‑derived exosomal KLF3‑AS1 promotes M2 microglial polarisation and ameliorates cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion injury.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Ischaemic stroke occurs when blood flow to the brain is obstructed. Rapid restoration of blood supply frequently induces cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury (CIRI). Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC)-derived exosomes exhibit promising therapeutic potential for CIRI.

title: Lipid Droplet-Associated Hsp70 Palmitoylation Drives Lysosomal Dysfunction in Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Lipid droplet (LDs) accumulate in glial cells across neurodegenerative and ischemic brain pathologies. LDs modulate cellular stress via organelle crosstalk, particularly with lysosomes, whose dysfunction and cathepsin leakage drive glial activation after cerebral ischemia. However, the molecular link between accumulated LDs and lysosomes in pathological glial activation remains incompletely understood. Using a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) model and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/Re) cell models, we found that both LD signal intensity and lysosomal cathepsin B leakage progressively increased from day 1 to day 14 after I/R. Etomoxir, an inhibitor of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1 A (CPT1A), the rate-limiting enzyme for fatty acid β-oxidation, aggravated I/R-induced LD accumulation and lysosomal damage in glial cells. Exogenous LDs derived from OGD/Re-treated glial cells aggravated lysosomal damage and promoted the proliferation of astrocytes and microglia. LD accumulation was associated with Hsp70 palmitoylation and redistribution of Hsp70 from lysosomes to the extracellular space, leading to lysosomal damage and reactive glial activation. Mechanistically, using multiple genetic and pharmacological approaches, including Plin3 knockdown, an Hsp70 palmitoylation‑site mutant, recombinant human Hsp70 (rhHsp70), as well as a pan-palmitoylation inhibitor and TLR2/4 antagonist, we consistently validated that Plin3, an LD surface protein, interacts with lysosomal Hsp70, causing Hsp70 palmitoylation and redistribution, and lysosomal damage. Extracellular Hsp70 activates TLR2/4 on glial cells, promoting cell proliferation and pro-inflammatory cytokine release. Collectively, these findings indicate that pathological LDs interacting with lysosomes drive Hsp70 palmitoylation and redistribution, causing lysosomal impairment and astrogliosis in ischemic stroke. We uncover Hsp70 palmitoylation as a potential drug target for ischemic stroke therapy.

LDs modulate cellular stress via organelle crosstalk, particularly with lysosomes, whose dysfunction and cathepsin leakage drive glial activation after cerebral ischemia. However, the molecular link between accumulated LDs and lysosomes in pathological glial activation remains incompletely understood.

title: Atractylenolide I ameliorates microglia-mediated cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by suppressing the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome axis.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Inflammatory responses play a pivotal role in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury, with microglia‑driven neuroinflammation further exacerbating neuronal damage. Atractylenolide I (ATR-I), a natural bioactive compound derived from Atractylodes macrocephala, exhibits anti-inflammatory properties by modulating signaling cascades. Nevertheless, its potential neuroprotective effects against cerebral I/R injury require further investigation.This study examined ATR-I's impact on microglial involvement in I/R-induced injury using two models: (i) BV2 microglial cells subjected to OGD/R in vitro, and (ii) a murine model of MCAO/R in vivo. Assessments included cellular viability, apoptosis, and inflammatory mediator secretion in vitro, while infarct volume, neurological function, neuronal apoptosis, and microglial activation were evaluated in vivo. Molecular mechanisms were explored via western blot and immunofluorescence. ATR-I substantially enhanced cellular survival while reducing apoptotic cell death and suppressing inflammatory cytokines secretion in OGD/R-treated BV2 cells. On the mechanistic front, ATR-I blocked two key inflammatory pathways: NLRP3 inflammasome activation and the TLR4/NF-κB signaling cascade. In experiments using the MCAO/R model, ATR-I treatment reduced infarct extent, improved neurological recovery, decreased neuronal apoptosis, and suppressed microglial activation-effects mediated by suppressing the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway. The ability of ATR-I to counteract cerebral I/R injury arises from its suppressive effect on the TLR4/NF‑κB/NLRP3 cascade. On account of this effect, ATR-I is considered a promising therapeutic agent for acute cerebral ischemia therapy, given its capacity to modulate microglia‑mediated neuroinflammatory reactions.

title: Cytoflavin's neuroprotective effect in acute ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains a leading cause of long-term disability globally. While reperfusion therapies are effective, there is a growing need for adjunct neuroprotective strategies to minimize secondary brain injury. Cytoflavin, a metabolic and antioxidant compound, has shown potential neuroprotective effects. However, its clinical efficacy remains underexplored. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the efficacy of Cytoflavin in AIS, focusing on neurological recovery (NIHSS), functional independence (Barthel Index), cognitive performance (MMSE), and infarct volume. A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases for studies evaluating Cytoflavin in AIS. Nine studies were included, with a combined enrollment of 3,254 participants across treatment arms (sample sizes reported per arm); the number of unique participants contributing to each pooled outcome was smaller after correcting for shared control groups and repeated-measures overlap across evaluation time points (e.g., 1,379 for NIHSS). Data were analyzed using random-effects models; where a shared control group was compared against two Cytoflavin dose arms within the same study, the control group was split proportionally between the two comparisons to avoid double-counting participants (unit-of-analysis correction). Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Cytoflavin significantly improved NIHSS scores (MD = -2.63, 95% CI: -3.15 to -2.10; moderate certainty) and Barthel Index (MD = 19.29, 95% CI: 9.52 to 29.07; moderate certainty), and showed improvements of low certainty in MMSE scores (MD = +6.93, 95% CI: 1.39 to 12.47) and mRS scores (MD = -0.41, 95% CI: -0.74 to -0.09), the latter derived from continuous summary statistics for an inherently ordinal scale (see Limitations). For infarct volume, effects diverged by evaluation time point: a marginal increase was observed at Day-10 (MD = +0.17 cm3, based on a single study), while a non-significant reduction was observed at Day-21 (MD = -4.73 cm3, 95% CI: -11.41 to 1.95; very low certainty). High heterogeneity (I2 ranging from 0% to 100%) was observed across outcomes and persisted after the unit-of-analysis correction, indicating genuine clinical and methodological diversity across studies. In conclusion, cytoflavin shows promising neuroprotective effects in AIS. However, due to heterogeneity and methodological limitations, further large-scale, high-quality studies are needed to confirm its efficacy and optimize treatment protocols. Systematic review registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251112430, identifier: CRD420251112430.

While reperfusion therapies are effective, there is a growing need for adjunct neuroprotective strategies to minimize secondary brain injury. Cytoflavin, a metabolic and antioxidant compound, has shown potential neuroprotective effects.

title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes electrophysiological slowing within minutes which may precede detectable structural changes, making electroencephalography (EEG) a sensitive bedside marker of tissue at risk. Prior quantitative EEG (qEEG) studies often averaged bilateral or frontal activity, focused on thrombectomy, and were recorded at 24 h. We tested whether a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) within 72 h after reperfusion is associated with malignant cerebral edema (MCE) and functional outcomes.

METHODS: In a prospective single-center cohort of anterior-circulation ischemic stroke treated with intravenous alteplase (IV-rtPA), endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), or both, a 7-min EEG was obtained ≤72 h after reperfusion. Lesion-ADR was defined as the mean ADR of ipsilesional electrodes; the reperfusion-to-EEG interval (ΔT) was recorded. The primary outcome was MCE (midline shift ≥5 mm and/or decompressive hemicraniectomy). Secondary outcomes were favorable functional outcomes at discharge and 90 days (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Model discrimination was assessed using ROC analysis and AUC with bootstrap internal validation. Adjusted associations were assessed using parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression models.

RESULTS: Forty-nine patients were included. For MCE, the combined lesion-ADR + ΔT model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.888 (95% CI 0.765-0.960); bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.889. For discharge independence (mRS ≤ 2; n = 9), the ADR-only model showed an apparent AUC of 0.899. Lesion-ADR remained associated with favorable outcome after separate adjustment for admission NIHSS (OR 1.438 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.009) and reperfusion treatment modality (OR 1.367; p = 0.022). For 90-day independence (n = 13), the ADR-only AUC was 0.759 (95% CI 0.615-0.869) and the ADR-only model showed moderate discrimination for 90-day functional independence. The association with 90-day outcome was attenuated after accounting for admission NIHSS (OR 1.245 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.088).

CONCLUSION: A brief lesion-directed ADR obtained within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with functional outcomes, while its combination with EEG timing showed encouraging discrimination for MCE in this cohort. These exploratory findings suggest lesion-directed qEEG may serve as a potential adjunctive biomarker after reperfusion therapy and warrant validation in larger cohorts.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes electrophysiological slowing within minutes which may precede detectable structural changes, making electroencephalography (EEG) a sensitive bedside marker of tissue at risk. Prior quantitative EEG (qEEG) studies often averaged bilateral or frontal activity, focused on thrombectomy, and were recorded at 24 h. We tested whether a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) within 72 h after reperfusion is associated with malignant cerebral edema (MCE) and functional outcomes.

title: Chemical Mechanisms of Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury and Neuroprotection in the Thrombectomy Era.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has significantly improved outcomes for patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke. However, restoring the artery does not always re-establish full microvascular blood flow, tissue rescue, or a good neurological outcome. Ischemia-reperfusion injury varies over time, with distinct biochemical mechanisms dominating during ischemia, early reperfusion, and the subsequent hours. During ischemia, factors like adenosine triphosphate (ATP) depletion, ionic imbalance, calcium overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, acidosis, and metabolic changes such as succinate build-up render brain tissue highly vulnerable. When blood flow resumes, oxygen delivery to this stressed tissue can induce rapid mitochondrial redox shifts, electron leakage, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species formation, iron-dependent radical generation, and lipid peroxidation. Damage may then persist for hours through ongoing mitochondrial dysfunction, phospholipid hydroperoxide accumulation, reactive aldehydes, ferroptosis, blood-brain barrier breakdown, microvascular issues, and inflammation. Much of the mechanistic evidence supporting these processes derives from experimental studies, and their relevance to clinical outcomes after thrombectomy requires further validation. This narrative review tracks these chemical changes across the main phases of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and connects them to modern thrombectomy practices. It also explores how the timing of each process may inform neuroprotective strategies, drug delivery methods, patient selection via imaging, and future clinical trial approaches.

title: Molecular Networks of Cell Death in Ischemic Stroke: From Mechanisms to Interventions.
abstract: Ischemic stroke involves a complex network of interconnected processes, including bioenergetic failure, excitotoxicity, ionic dyshomeostasis involving Na+, K+, Ca2+, and Cl-, oxidative stress, DNA damage, and neurovascular dysfunction. Apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and parthanatos contribute to experimental ischemic injury with different levels of mechanistic support. Autophagy primarily maintains cellular homeostasis and modulates these pathways. Autophagy-dependent cell death requires separate evidence that the autophagic machinery causes death. These processes operate across the ischemic core and penumbra and evolve during ischemia, reperfusion, and recovery. Their effects extend beyond neurons to microglia, astrocytes, brain microvascular endothelial cells, pericytes, and other neurovascular components. This narrative review evaluates pathway execution, shared molecular nodes, and the spatial and temporal limits of the available evidence. It emphasizes receptor-complex regulation, mitochondrial and lysosomal function, phospholipid peroxidation, DNA damage, and inflammatory signaling as points of convergence. Preclinical interventions are assessed according to their models, molecular endpoints, and functional outcomes. A cell- and stage-specific network perspective supports the development of targeted therapies, while the efficacy and safety of coordinated pathway intervention in patients remain to be established.

Autophagy primarily maintains cellular homeostasis and modulates these pathways.

title: Remote ischemic preconditioning protects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury through lactate-dependent AMPK/ULK1 signaling and autophagy.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major contributor to ischemic cerebral damage and poor functional outcomes following ischemic stroke, and effective neuroprotective strategies remain limited. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) has emerged as a promising, noninvasive approach; however, its underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether lactate serves as a key metabolic mediator linking RIPC to neuroprotection through regulation of autophagy. Using an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in PC12 cells and a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model in rats, we demonstrate that I/R impairs autophagic flux, as evidenced by p62 accumulation and reduced LC3-II and Beclin-1 expression, leading to increased cellular apoptosis and injury. Lactate supplementation restored autophagic flux, enhanced cell viability, and suppressed apoptosis under OGD/R conditions. Mechanistically, lactate activated the AMPK/ULK1 signaling pathway, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AMPK or ULK1 attenuated lactate-induced autophagy and cytoprotection. In vivo, RIPC elevated plasma and cerebral lactate levels, activated AMPK/ULK1 signaling, promoted autophagy, reduced infarct volume, and improved acute neurological outcomes. Notably, blockade of lactate transport or inhibition of AMPK/ULK1 signaling attenuated these protective effects. Collectively, our findings suggest that lactate serves as an important mediator of RIPC-induced neuroprotection and reveal a novel lactate-AMPK/ULK1-autophagy axis that mitigates cerebral I/R injury. These results provide mechanistic insight into RIPC and suggest potential therapeutic targets for ischemic stroke.

Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) has emerged as a promising, noninvasive approach; however, its underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether lactate serves as a key metabolic mediator linking RIPC to neuroprotection through regulation of autophagy.

title: Performance of the Lausanne Ischemic Stroke Pathway prehospital triage system in identifying acute reperfusion candidates: a quality-control study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Accurate identification is one of the cornerstones of prehospital care for patients with suspected acute ischaemic stroke (AIS). In the Lausanne Ischemic Stroke Pathway triage system, emergency medical service (EMS) providers use dedicated criteria to identify acute reperfusion candidates and call a coordinated medical team (CMT, including a neurologist and an emergency physician), which can activate the stroke code pathway. The objective of this study was to evaluate the performance of the system in identifying acute reperfusion candidates.

METHODS: This was a retrospective single-centre quality-control study conducted in a Swiss university-based stroke centre, from 1 January 2019 to 31 May 2022. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥18 years, for whom the EMS called the CMT or patients with AIS eligible for acute reperfusion managed by the EMS. The main outcomes were the performance of both the EMS and the CMT in detecting AIS patients eligible for acute reperfusion, as assessed through their respective under- and overtriage rates. A secondary outcome was the identification of alternative diagnoses in overtriaged patients.

RESULTS: Of 1071 patients included, the EMS phone-contacted the CMT for 937 (87.5%) of them. Among the 1071 patients, 440 (41%) had an AIS eligible for reperfusion. The system's undertriage rate was 30% (133 patients without stroke pathway activation among the 440 patients with an AIS eligible for acute reperfusion). The undertriage rates were 21% for the EMS and 11% for the CMT. The overtriage rates were 63% for the EMS and 57% for the CMT. The main alternative diagnoses in overtriaged patients were seizures (14%), intracranial haemorrhages (9.9%) and functional disorders (6.5%).

CONCLUSION: Undertriage and overtriage rates were relatively high, but both were reduced by the CMT call, highlighting the added value of a second expert assessment step, with a higher level of expertise. Concerning overtriage, a better prehospital identification of alternative diagnoses, such as seizures or functional disorders, could help to better classify our patients.

In the Lausanne Ischemic Stroke Pathway triage system, emergency medical service (EMS) providers use dedicated criteria to identify acute reperfusion candidates and call a coordinated medical team (CMT, including a neurologist and an emergency physician), which can activate the stroke code pathway. The objective of this study was to evaluate the performance of the system in identifying acute reperfusion candidates.

title: Diffusion-weighted imaging reversal after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke: associations with white matter hyperintensities and cerebral microbleeds.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) and cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) are common MRI markers of chronic small-vessel brain injury and have been associated with adverse outcomes after ischemic stroke. However, whether these markers influence early ischemic tissue reversibility following reperfusion therapy remains unclear. We therefore investigated their associations with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion reversal, hemorrhagic complications, and short-term functional outcome after MRI-guided reperfusion therapy.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke undergoing MRI-guided intravenous thrombolysis, with or without additional mechanical thrombectomy, were included. According to the institutional protocol, follow-up MRI was planned 24 ± 6 h after treatment to assess DWI lesion evolution, WMH volume, and CMBs. DWI reversal was defined as a reduction of ≥ 25% in baseline DWI lesion volume. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of DWI reversal, intracerebral hemorrhage, and functional outcome at hospital discharge.

RESULTS: Among 345 patients (median age 74 years [IQR 63-82], 48.1% female), 45 (13%) additionally underwent mechanical thrombectomy. DWI reversal occurred in 76 patients (22.0%) and was not associated with baseline WMH volume, CMBs, initial infarct volume, treatment modality, or thrombolysis time window. Higher baseline NIHSS and modified Rankin Scale scores were associated with lower odds of DWI reversal, whereas hypercholesterolemia was independently associated with increased odds of DWI reversal. We found no evidence of an association of WMH burden or CMB presence with intracerebral hemorrhage or of an independent association with functional outcome. Fourteen patients (4.1%) developed new CMBs on follow-up MRI.

CONCLUSIONS: We found no evidence of an association between baseline WMH volume or CMB presence and early DWI lesion reversal or hemorrhagic complications following reperfusion therapy in this cohort. These findings provide no evidence that these two chronic MRI markers are major determinants of early infarct tissue reversibility. Larger multicenter studies incorporating comprehensive small-vessel disease phenotyping and long-term follow-up are warranted.

However, whether these markers influence early ischemic tissue reversibility following reperfusion therapy remains unclear. We therefore investigated their associations with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion reversal, hemorrhagic complications, and short-term functional outcome after MRI-guided reperfusion therapy.

title: Panax notoginseng-Derived Carbon Quantum Dots as a Novel Administration Strategy for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Therapy.
abstract: The present study aimed to synthesize Panax notoginseng-derived carbon quantum dots (PN-CDs) and explore their role in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). PN-CDs were synthesized by the hydrothermal method, and characterization and biocompatibility were assessed. Next, CIRI models were established using SH-SY5Y cells, primary neurons were treated with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R), and rats were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R). After PN-CDs treatment, inflammation, apoptosis, and oxidative stress were detected in neuronal cells and rats using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, flow cytometry, Western blot, and 2',7'-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate probe. Meanwhile, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling, Nissl, and hematoxylin and eosin staining were employed to measure the pathological damage of rats. Additionally, CIRI rats were administered with PN-CDs, Panax notoginseng saponins (PNS), Panax notoginseng (PN), or edaravone to investigate whether PN-CDs had the best effect. The findings revealed that PN-CDs exhibited favorable biocompatibility and crossed the blood-brain barrier. In vitro, PN-CD treatment inhibited oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammation, as evidenced by the decrease of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), IL-6, Bax, C-caspase-3, tumor necrosis factor-α, malondialdehyde, and reactive oxygen species and the increase of superoxide dismutase, Bcl-2, and glutathione. In CIRI rats, PN-CDs improved pathological damage and suppressed inflammation, apoptosis, and oxidative stress. The therapeutic effect of PN-CDs on CIRI was distinctly better than that of PNS and PN, and comparable to that of the first-line drug edaravone. In short, PN-CDs, a novel and efficient administration strategy, alleviates CIRI by inhibiting apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
abstract: Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion, and mesenchymal stem cell-treated samples. In this exploratory dataset, the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion samples showed relatively greater representation of inflammatory and antigen-presenting microglial states and elevated expression of selected microglial state-associated genes, including Slfn4, Apoe, and Gpnmb. In the corresponding exploratory comparison, the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample showed relatively greater representation of homeostatic-associated and Lgals3/Spp1-enriched microglial states and lower expression of several inflammatory-associated genes. Spatial mapping further revealed regionally restricted expression of microglial and neuronal markers within the injured tissue. Excitatory neurons displayed preliminary mesenchymal stem cell-associated transcriptional patterns involving mitochondrial transcripts, oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic signaling, calcium-related functions, and apoptosis/autophagy-associated pathways. CellChat analysis computationally predicted relatively high levels of tumor necrosis factor, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand, and complement signaling in the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion sample, whereas the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample had relatively high levels of predicted activity of neuregulin, pleiotrophin and selected semaphorin. Together, these integrated datasets provide a hypothesis-generating framework linking microglial state remodeling, neuronal metabolic and synaptic programs, and predicted neuroimmune communication patterns after ischemic stroke. Because each omics condition or time point was represented by one biological sample, all the transcriptomic findings should be considered preliminary and exploratory and should be validated in independently replicated cohorts.

title: Engineering a Translational Human Thrombus Platform to Evaluate Clinical Therapies in Ischemic Stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recanalization failure after ischemic stroke remains a major clinical challenge, partly because cerebral thrombi display marked spatial heterogeneity that is poorly reproduced by experimental models. Here, we engineered a translational human blood-based thrombus platform that recapitulates key histological features of patient-derived stroke clots.

METHODS: Under controlled conditions, the platform generated reproducible thrombi with pronounced interthrombus and intrathrombus heterogeneity, including alternating red blood cell-rich and platelet-rich territories. Multiscale structural and biochemical analyses confirmed the successful replication of the clinical biphasic organization associated with resistance to rtPA (recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator): a compact outer fibrin shell containing focal accumulations of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, and a dense inner core further stabilized by neutrophil extracellular traps.

RESULTS: Functional thrombolysis assays demonstrated that this architecture directly dictates lytic susceptibility. Specifically, artificially breaching the outer fibrin shell (halved thrombi) significantly accelerated early rtPA-mediated lysis, proving its role as an effective physical barrier. Furthermore, lytic response was inherently linked to clot composition: platelet-rich thrombi with dense plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and neutrophil extracellular trap networks exhibited profound resistance to standard rtPA compared with red blood cell-rich clots. Supporting the platform's translational relevance, this structural resistance was successfully overcome by clinically relevant strategies, including tenecteplase and adjunctive DNAse, consistent with observations from human stroke cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: By accurately reproducing the spatial organization and differential thrombolytic responses of human cerebral thrombi, this translational framework provides a robust preclinical tool to dissect lytic resistance and evaluate next-generation precision reperfusion therapies. Furthermore, developing robust ex vivo human platforms is increasingly critical to align with the replacement, reduction, refinement ethical guidelines for animal research.

Here, we engineered a translational human blood-based thrombus platform that recapitulates key histological features of patient-derived stroke clots. METHODS: Under controlled conditions, the platform generated reproducible thrombi with pronounced interthrombus and intrathrombus heterogeneity, including alternating red blood cell-rich and platelet-rich territories.

title: Advances in research and clinical decision strategies for anticoagulation timing in acute ischemic stroke patients with atrial fibrillation.
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a major risk factor for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), and oral anticoagulation is the cornerstone of secondary prevention. The optimal timing of anticoagulation initiation remains controversial because of the need to balance the risks of early ischemic recurrence and hemorrhagic transformation. Recent randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses indicate that early initiation of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) is generally safe in appropriately selected patients and may reduce recurrent ischemic events without increasing the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. However, evidence remains limited in patients with severe stroke, hemorrhagic transformation, large infarcts, or recent reperfusion therapy, in whom the timing of anticoagulation should be individualized according to clinical and neuroimaging characteristics. The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline considers early oral anticoagulation reasonable in carefully selected patients with AIS and AF, particularly those with milder stroke severity, without specifying a uniform initiation window. Clinical decision-making should integrate stroke severity, neuroimaging findings, and individual thromboembolic and bleeding risks. Overall, current evidence supports a shift from fixed delay rules toward individualized anticoagulation strategies.

title: Case Report: Multiorgan arterial and venous thrombosis after ischemic stroke: endovascular management and subsequent transcatheter patent foramen ovale closure.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concurrent cerebral, visceral, renal, aortic, and pulmonary thrombosis is rare and may reflect multiple mechanisms. Identifying the embolic source and balancing antithrombotic therapy against intracranial bleeding are major clinical challenges.

CASE SUMMARY: A 63-year-old woman presented on 3 February 2025 with right middle cerebral artery (MCA) M1 occlusion and underwent intravenous thrombolysis followed by mechanical thrombectomy, achieving Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (TICI) grade 2b reperfusion. The procedure was complicated by self-limited M1 wall injury and right Sylvian subarachnoid hemorrhage, with subsequent right hemispheric infarction and intraparenchymal blood products. During rehabilitation, emergency imaging on 5 March 2025 demonstrated a saddle pulmonary embolism (PE) with bilateral extension, a floating abdominal aortic thrombus, occlusive superior mesenteric artery (SMA) thrombosis with preserved bowel perfusion, hepatic and pancreaticoduodenal arterial thrombosis, renal embolic lesions, and new left hemispheric and cerebellar ischemic lesions. Aortic mechanical thrombectomy was performed with a Penumbra Indigo system and a Lightning 7-Fr catheter; persistent proximal SMA thrombus was treated with two balloon-expandable Omnilink stents (8 × 59 mm and 8 × 39 mm). Intravenous unfractionated heparin was transitioned to warfarin on 12 March 2025. In March 2026, contrast transcranial Doppler documented a large right-to-left shunt after the Valsalva maneuver, and two-dimensional (2D) transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography (TTE/TEE) with color Doppler confirmed a tunnel-like patent foramen ovale (PFO) with a septum primum aneurysm. On 24 March 2026, rotational intracardiac echocardiography (rICE)-guided closure was performed under local anesthesia using a II-Hubless 22/28 mm Memopart PFO Occluder (LEPU Medical).

DISCUSSION: The records support concurrent arterial and venous thrombosis, not a single embolic cascade. The aortic thrombus plausibly caused visceral and renal embolization but not PE; the later PFO represented a potential, unproven route for paradoxical embolism. Despite substantial clot burden and RV dysfunction, incomplete data precluded reliable retrospective ESC risk classification. PFO closure was an individualized adjunct to anticoagulation given the patient's age, alternative embolic sources, and incomplete prolonged rhythm monitoring.

Identifying the embolic source and balancing antithrombotic therapy against intracranial bleeding are major clinical challenges. title: Intranasal Delivery of an Antioxidant Nanoassembly for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK Signaling.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is caused by reduced cerebral blood flow, leading to excessive oxidative stress and neurological deficits. Curcumin (Cur) is a promising therapeutic agent, but its antioxidant activity is limited by low bioavailability and poor brain penetration. Herein, an intranasal delivery strategy using a tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNAs)-Cur nanoassembly (tFNAs-Cur) was employed for CIRI treatment. tFNAs-Cur was synthesized through self-assembly, achieving a high Cur loading efficiency of 87% and exhibiting potent scavenging activity against reactive oxygen species (ROS) including O2·-, ·OH, and H2O2. In vitro studies showed that tFNAs-Cur inhibited oxygen glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced ROS elevation of cytoplasm and mitochondria, and enhanced proliferation and migration of SH-SY5Y cells. In vivo studies demonstrated that intranasal administration of tFNAs-Cur reduced cerebral infarct volume, enhanced neuronal survival, and improved neurological and behavioral outcomes in middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. Further mechanistic investigation using RNA sequencing revealed that tFNAs-Cur exerted its effects by activating the Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK signaling, thereby improving mitochondrial function and upregulating BDNF levels. Furthermore, hemolysis assays, serum biochemical measurements, and histopathological analyses demonstrated that tFNAs-Cur possessed a favorable biosafety profile both ex vivo and in vivo. This study provides an intranasal antioxidant nanoassembly strategy for CIRI and holds potential for clinical translation.
