METHODS: Because reperfusion was achieved by filament withdrawal before rt-PA administration, this model evaluates TXL-associated effects during mechanically induced reperfusion with rt-PA exposure rather than enhancement of rt-PA-mediated thrombolysis.

title: Exogenous hydrogen sulfide alleviates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury via inhibiting RIPK1-mediated neuronal necroptosis and ROS overaccumulation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral I/R injury is a significant pathological factor contributing to neuronal death and neurological dysfunction following stroke. Necroptosis and excessive oxidative stress are pivotal mechanisms that drive ischemic neuronal damage. H2S has been identified as a neuroprotective gaseous signaling molecule; however, its regulatory role in neuronal necroptosis during cerebral I/R injury remains inadequately understood.

METHODS: In vitro, we established a cell OGD model to simulate neuronal I/R injury. Following pretreatment with NaHS or Necrostatin-1, we assessed cell viability, the necroptotic rate, intracellular ROS levels, mitochondrial membrane potential, and the expression of necroptosis-related proteins. In vivo, we established a mouse model of MCAO/R. After NaHS and Nec-1 intervention, we evaluated neurological deficit scores, cerebral blood perfusion, brain water content, cerebral infarct volume, neuronal ultrastructure, and the expression of RIPKs proteins.

RESULTS: OGD treatment resulted in a time-dependent decline in SH-SY5Y cell viability, a significant increase in the rate of neuronal necroptosis, excessive accumulation of ROS, mitochondrial dysfunction, and elevated expression levels of RIPKs and MLKL. Pretreatment with moderate doses of NaHS significantly enhanced cell viability, mitigated ROS overproduction, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and inhibited OGD-induced neuronal necroptosis. Both NaHS and Nec-1 effectively suppressed the activation of the RIPK1 mediated signaling pathway. In vivo, MCAO/R induced severe neurological dysfunction, cerebral hypoperfusion, brain edema, extensive cerebral infarction, and neuronal ultrastructural damage. NaHS or Nec-1 treatment significantly improved neurological deficits, restored regional cerebral blood flow, reduced brain edema and infarct volume, and alleviated neuronal morphological damage by downregulating the expression of RIPK1 and RIPK3.

CONCLUSION: Necroptosis played a crucial role in acute cerebral I/R injury, both in vitro and in vivo, mediated by RIPK1. Exogenous H2S or Nec-1 exhibited significant neuroprotective effects against cerebral I/R injury by suppressing RIPK1-mediated neuronal necroptosis and inhibiting ROS. These findings provided a novel theoretical basis for the clinical management of ischemic stroke.

Necroptosis and excessive oxidative stress are pivotal mechanisms that drive ischemic neuronal damage. H2S has been identified as a neuroprotective gaseous signaling molecule; however, its regulatory role in neuronal necroptosis during cerebral I/R injury remains inadequately understood.

title: NAD+ Attenuates Neuroinflammation in Ischemic Stroke by Suppressing the cGAS- STING Pathway via Mitochondrial Homeostasis Restoration.
abstract: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide, with neuroinflammation playing a critical role in its pathogenesis. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway is a major driver of innate immune responses activated by endogenous DNA, including mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), and contributes significantly to post-ischemic neuroinflammation. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), a vital metabolic coenzyme, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory potential in various diseases, including stroke; however, its specific role in regulation of neuroinflammation following stroke remains unclear. In this study, we examined the protective effects of NAD+ against ischemic stroke and explored its role in modulating cGAS-STING-mediated neuroinflammatory responses. Utilizing a transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion mouse model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation BV2 microglia model, we observed that NAD+ treatment significantly reduced infarct volume and brain edema, and improved neurological outcomes. NAD+ reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and facilitated the polarization of microglia from pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. This effect was associated with the inhibition of cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway activation. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockdown of STING largely abrogated the anti-inflammatory effects of NAD+ in BV2 microglia, indicating a STING-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, NAD+ restored mitochondrial respiratory function and reduced cytoplasmic mtDNA leakage, suggesting that the improvement of mitochondrial homeostasis may underlie the suppression of cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway by NAD+. Our findings indicate that NAD+ alleviates neuroinflammation following brain ischemia/reperfusion injury by regulating mitochondrial homeostasis and attenuates the cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway activation in microglia, thereby providing new therapeutic insights for ischemic stroke.

Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), a vital metabolic coenzyme, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory potential in various diseases, including stroke; however, its specific role in regulation of neuroinflammation following stroke remains unclear.

title: Current and emerging neuromodulation techniques for motor recovery after ischemic stroke: a 2026 update.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neuromodulation technologies have emerged as promising tools to enhance motor recovery following ischemic stroke. Acute reperfusion therapy remains highly time-dependent, underscoring the need for interventions that augment post-stroke neuroplasticity. Brain stimulation techniques aim to modulate cortical excitability and promote adaptive reorganization of motor networks during the critical recovery period after stroke.

AREAS COVERED: The authors review recent advances in neuromodulation strategies for post-stroke motor recovery, as well as the key principles underlying neuromodulation. Major noninvasive modalities, including transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), and low-intensity focused ultrasound stimulation (LIFUS), are reviewed alongside emerging applications of invasive techniques such as deep brain stimulation (DBS) and vagus nerve stimulation (VNS). Recent randomized clinical trials and translational studies are also highlighted. This article is based on literature obtained through PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov searches for content published between 1 January 2020 and 30 March 202630 March 2026 and was supplemented by earlier landmark studies relevant to stroke recovery and neuromodulation.

EXPERT OPINION: Although neuromodulation technologies demonstrate encouraging safety profiles, clinical trial results feature notable neutral results. Future studies bear the burden of refining stimulation paradigms, patient selection, and rehabilitation dosing, possibly leveraging personalized, biomarker-driven patient selection.

Acute reperfusion therapy remains highly time-dependent, underscoring the need for interventions that augment post-stroke neuroplasticity. Brain stimulation techniques aim to modulate cortical excitability and promote adaptive reorganization of motor networks during the critical recovery period after stroke.

title: Prognostic performance of blood neurofilament light chain for functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This meta-analysis aimed to assess the association between blood neurofilament light chain (NfL) and functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure database were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled to quantify the association between blood NfL and functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke. We pooled the area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity; conducted meta-regression and sensitivity analyses; and assessed publication bias.

RESULTS: A total of 18 studies involving 3,448 patients were included in this meta-analysis. The pooled results demonstrated that blood NfL was associated with poor functional outcomes after ischemic stroke (OR = 1.78, 95% CI: 1.41-2.24, p < 0.001, I 2 = 87.5%, p < 0.01). The pooled AUC for blood NfL in predicting functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75-0.82), with 71% (95% CI: 62-79%) sensitivity and 74% (95% CI: 67-80%) specificity. Subgroup analyses and meta-regression revealed that participant age, sample size, study design, blood sample type, assay method, proportion of poor functional outcomes, blood sampling time, reperfusion therapy rate, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, definition of poor functional outcome, and the proportion of large artery atherosclerosis were not identified as significant sources of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis indicated that the pooled estimate was robust. Begg's test also showed no evidence of publication bias (p = 0.753), although Egger's test suggested the presence of publication bias (p < 0.001). The trim-and-fill method showed that the overall effect of this meta-analysis was stable.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis showed that elevated blood NfL levels may have prognostic value for functional outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke. However, given the substantial between-study heterogeneity and the presence of publication bias, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

title: USP11 Drives Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Via Promoting Ferroptosis by Deubiquitinating and Stabilizing ASK1.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) represents a pivotal pathological mechanism underlying ischemic cerebrovascular disorders including cerebral stroke. Currently, there are lack of effective preventive or therapeutic methods. Ubiquitin-specific protease 11 (USP11) is a member of the most prevalent ubiquitination-specific protease (USP) family. It has been shown that USP11 plays diverse and significant roles in a variety of diseases, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate cancer, and intervertebral disc degeneration. However, its precise function and molecular mechanisms involvement in CIRI remain unknown.

METHODS: USP11 knockout (USP11-KO) and adeno-associated virus 9-mediated USP11 over-expression (USP11-OE) mice were established as a mouse model of CIRI, and USP11 knockdown and overexpression adenovirus were used to establish a cell model, to investigate the effect of USP11 on CIRI in vivo and in vitro. Molecular biological studies were used to clarify the mechanism of USP11 mediated ferroptosis during CIRI.

RESULTS: The expression of USP11 is increased during CIRI. Functionally, USP11 deficiency attenuated neurological deficits, cerebral infarction, neuroinflammation, and ferroptosis during CIRI, whereas specific overexpression of USP11 exacerbated these pathological processes. Furthermore, USP11 knockdown inhibited neuronal injury, inflammatory response and ferroptosis, while USP11 overexpression promoted these processes. Mechanistically, USP11 bind to ASK1 and inhibit its K48-linked ubiquitination, thereby enhancing the activity of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling pathway. More importantly, the regulation of USP11 on neuronal ferroptosis and CIRI relied on its regulation of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling axis.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study clarified the new functions and mechanisms of USP11 during CIRI. Targeting USP11-ASK1-JNK/p38-ferroptosis may be a new promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of CIRI.

Currently, there are lack of effective preventive or therapeutic methods. Ubiquitin-specific protease 11 (USP11) is a member of the most prevalent ubiquitination-specific protease (USP) family.

title: Pre-Stroke Disability, Stroke Severity and Systemic Inflammation Outweigh Malignancy as Determinants of 90-Day Outcome After Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and coexisting malignancy have worse outcomes, but it is unclear how much of this reflects malignancy itself rather than pre-stroke function, stroke severity and systemic inflammation. Methods: We retrospectively studied consecutive adults with MRI-confirmed AIS admitted to a neurology department in Warsaw, Poland (2020-2024): 130 with documented malignancy and 100 without. Because every patient with a pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score above 2 had a poor outcome by definition, the primary analysis was restricted to patients with pre-stroke mRS 0-2 (n = 161; 80 versus 81). Logistic models were adjusted sequentially for age, sex, admission NIHSS, pre-stroke mRS and log-transformed C-reactive protein (CRP). Results: Groups were comparable in age and vascular comorbidities. Good 90-day outcome was less frequent with malignancy (40.0% versus 58.0%; p = 0.028), but the association was no longer significant after adjustment for age, sex and admission NIHSS (odds ratio [OR] 1.55, 95% CI 0.69-3.51) and was null after adding pre-stroke mRS and log-CRP (OR 0.67, 0.25-1.81). Admission NIHSS and log-CRP were the consistent independent predictors. Return to within one mRS point of baseline was achieved by 41.5% versus 59.0% (p = 0.011). Among patients with pre-stroke mRS ≤ 2, intravenous thrombolysis rates were similar (22.5% versus 22.2%) and hemorrhagic transformation did not differ (17.4% versus 18.9%). Conclusions: Malignancy added little prognostic information beyond baseline function, stroke severity and systemic inflammation, although a clinically meaningful residual effect cannot be excluded. Among eligible patients, reperfusion appeared equally safe.

title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.

This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management.

title: Case Report: Multidisciplinary and individualized management of periprocedural arterial thrombosis and ischemic stroke in children: a three-case series.
abstract: Pediatric arterial thromboembolism is rare but may cause limb loss, extensive cerebral infarction, permanent disability, or death. Evidence guiding reperfusion therapy in children remains limited. We describe three periprocedural events treated according to their vascular territory, threatened tissue, and bleeding risk. A male neonate born at 37 weeks' gestation developed catheter-associated left external iliac-femoral arterial thrombosis after umbilical arterial catheterization during treatment for shock and respiratory illness. Intravenous urokinase and low-molecular-weight heparin achieved complete thrombus resolution on ultrasonography six days after diagnosis. A 5-year-and-5-month-old boy developed acute left internal carotid-middle cerebral artery occlusion with extensive left hemispheric infarction three days after thoracoscopic resection of pulmonary sequestration. Emergency stent-retriever thrombectomy with aspiration achieved immediate recanalization, which persisted at one week; independent ambulation was restored after rehabilitation, although mild right upper-limb symptoms remained at discharge. A 4-month-old boy developed right frontotemporal-insular ischemic infarction after balloon angioplasty for recurrent aortic coarctation. Because no retrievable intracranial large-vessel occlusion was identified and the recent cardiac intervention increased the bleeding risk, aspirin, low-molecular-weight heparin, and supportive treatment were administered. Follow-up MRI one week after diagnosis showed regression of the initial lesion but revealed a new right thalamic lesion suspicious for acute infarction. These heterogeneous cases highlight the need for prompt vascular imaging and individualized multidisciplinary management based on the vascular territory, threatened tissue, patient size, recent procedures, bleeding risk, and procedural feasibility. As a descriptive case series, this report does not establish the comparative efficacy of the treatment strategies.

Evidence guiding reperfusion therapy in children remains limited. We describe three periprocedural events treated according to their vascular territory, threatened tissue, and bleeding risk.

title: Barriers to intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective case report series from Honduras.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Intravenous (IV) thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is time-dependent and frequently underused in resource-limited settings. We aimed to characterize patients with AIS who did not receive IV thrombolysis at a national referral center in Honduras and to document the barriers to treatment.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center, consecutive case report series of all eligible patients with AIS who were not thrombolyzed at Hospital Escuela Universitario between 1 October and 30 November 2025. We gathered demographics, socioeconomic status, admission severity, process-of-care intervals, contraindications, neuroimaging and thrombolytic availability, complications, and discharge outcomes. Contraindications were classified as absolute or relative according to the 2019 American Heart Association and American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines. A thrombolysis eligibility cascade was the principal analysis. The study was approved by the institutional review board.

RESULTS: A total of 23 patients were included (median age 70 years; 14 [60.9%] male). Extreme poverty (≥2 unsatisfied basic needs [UBN]) was present in 14 patients (60.9%). All 23 AIS presentations screened during the period were included, and no patient received thrombolysis (institutional thrombolysis rate 0%). The median onset-to-door time was 10.0 h (IQR 7.0-15.0), and only 1 of 22 patients with a recorded time (4.5%) arrived within 4.5 h. Late or unknown onset was the most frequent absolute contraindication (21 [91.3%]); neuroimaging was available in 22 (95.7%) patients, but the thrombolytic agent was unavailable in every patient (availability 0%). In the eligibility cascade, the single patient within the window had no absolute contraindication and could not be treated because no thrombolytic agent was available. The in-hospital mortality rate was 2 (8.7%), and a good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score 0-2) occurred in 5 of 20 patients with an assessable score.

CONCLUSION: Non-administration of thrombolysis reflected late presentation and, above all, the complete unavailability of the thrombolytic agent, whereas imaging and organizational capacity were largely in place. Drug supply was the proximate, modifiable obstacle to reperfusion in this setting.

We aimed to characterize patients with AIS who did not receive IV thrombolysis at a national referral center in Honduras and to document the barriers to treatment. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center, consecutive case report series of all eligible patients with AIS who were not thrombolyzed at Hospital Escuela Universitario between 1 October and 30 November 2025.

title: Mitochondria-associated ferroptosis in ischemic stroke: Pathophysiological evolution, interorganelle crosstalk, and therapeutic targeting.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) results from an acute interruption of cerebral blood flow and the ensuing collapse of energy metabolism. Although vascular recanalization can salvage the ischemic penumbra, its overall benefit remains constrained by a narrow therapeutic window and reperfusion injury. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, contributes to neuronal injury after IS and can amplify ischemia/reperfusion injury. By integrating energy metabolism, iron homeostasis, and redox balance, mitochondria can shape ferroptosis susceptibility within the energy-depleted, iron-dysregulated, and oxidatively stressed ischemic brain. However, most studies have examined iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation at the whole-cell level, leaving the temporal and interorganelle dimensions of mitochondrial regulation of ferroptosis insufficiently integrated. Here, we organize mitochondria-associated ferroptosis across the pathological course of IS, from metabolic reprogramming and substrate accumulation during ischemia to the reverse electron transport-associated reactive oxygen species burst during early reperfusion and subsequent disruption of mitochondrial quality control. We further examine mitochondrial crosstalk with the endoplasmic reticulum, lysosomes, lipid droplets, and nucleus, compare ferroptosis susceptibility across neurovascular unit cell populations, and map these mechanisms onto pharmacological interventions and mechanistically plausible therapeutic windows. Finally, we assess barriers to the clinical translation of mitochondria-targeted therapies and provide a stage-resolved framework for developing neuroprotective strategies in IS.

Although vascular recanalization can salvage the ischemic penumbra, its overall benefit remains constrained by a narrow therapeutic window and reperfusion injury. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, contributes to neuronal injury after IS and can amplify ischemia/reperfusion injury.

title: Clusterin interference decreases cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by suppressing TFR1-dependent ferroptosis.
abstract: Ferroptosis plays a crucial role in the pathological process of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury, but the specific regulatory mechanism of Clusterin in this process remains unclear. This study aims to investigate whether interfering with Clusterin can alleviate cerebral I/R injury by regulating neuronal ferroptosis. A cerebral I/R injury mouse model was established and the adeno-associated virus (AAV-sh-Clusterin) was stereotactically injected into the brain. Brain tissue damage was evaluated using TTC and HE staining. The expressions of blood-brain barrier proteins (Occludin, ZO-1) and inflammatory factors (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6) were detected. Downstream differentially expressed genes were analyzed through mRNA transcriptome sequencing. The expression changes of iron death-related indicators (Fe2 +, MDA, GSH, NRF2, GPX4, ACSL4, SLC7A11) were evaluated by means of biochemical methods and WB/qPCR. Subsequently, an in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) model of HT22 cells was constructed to analyze the effects of Clusterin interference on the proliferation and ferroptosis of HT22 cells. The interaction between Clusterin and TFR1 was detected, and a rescue experiment was carried out by overexpressing TFR1. Clusterin was significantly upregulated in both in vitro and in vivo models. Interference with Clusterin effectively reduced the volume of cerebral infarction, upregulated the expressions of Occludin and ZO-1, and inhibited the inflammatory response. Besides, interference with Clusterin significantly decreased the ferroptosis level in mouse brain tissue. There is a protein interaction between Clusterin and TFR1, and the rescue experiment indicated that overexpression of TFR1 could counteract the inhibitory effect of sh-Clusterin on ferroptosis and the proliferation protection effect of HT22 cells. In summary, interfering with Clusterin by inhibiting TFR1-dependent neuronal ferroptosis significantly mitigates neuronal damage and inflammatory responses induced by cerebral I/R.

title: Activatable MRI-Trackable Spherical Nucleic Acids for Idebenone Delivery Against Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a key driver of poor prognosis in ischemic stroke. Idebenone (IDBN) shows promise for mitigating IRI, but its efficacy is limited by poor brain accumulation. Moreover, IDBN cannot be visually tracked, making it difficult to confirm whether it reaches the ischemic brain and exerts therapeutic effects. Here, IDBN functionalized with a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-cleavable bond is grafted onto phosphorothioate-modified DNA strands and co-assembled with ultrasmall superparamagnetic iron oxide (USPIO) to form USPIO-IDBN-SNAs, where SNAs stands for spherical nucleic acids. Exploiting upregulated class A scavenger receptors, USPIO-IDBN-SNAs target the ischemic area without targeting modifications and increase local IDBN concentration. Hydrophobic IDBN inside the SNAs limits water access to USPIO clusters, suppressing their contrast-enhancing ability. Under oxidative stress, IDBN is rapidly released and exerts remarkable protection. This release allows USPIO clusters to re-establish contact with water, activating their contrast-enhancing ability on T2-weighted imaging. Collectively, USPIO-IDBN-SNAs provide significant neuroprotection against IRI and offer a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-visible platform to monitor IDBN release in the ischemic brain, presenting a promising theranostic approach for precise, trackable stroke therapy.

title: Combined intervention: hydroxysafflor yellow A acts synergistically with aerobic exercise to alleviate cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury via the HIF-1α/CREB pathway.
abstract: The pathological mechanisms underlying cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) are complex, and monotherapy with thrombolytic agents or pharmacological interventions alone has inherent limitations. We investigated the combined neuroprotective effects of hydroxysafflor yellow A (HSYA) and swimming exercise in a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) injury. The MCAO/R model was established via the intraluminal suture method, with 2 h of ischemia followed by reperfusion. Rats were divided into sham, model, HSYA monotherapy, and HSYA combined with aerobic exercise groups. Water maze and open field tests revealed that the combination of HSYA combined with aerobic exercise significantly improved learning and memory abilities in MCAO/R rats. 2,3,5-Triphenyltetrazolium Chloride (TTC) staining showed that this combination significantly reduced cerebral infarct volume. HE and TUNEL staining further demonstrated that HSYA combined with aerobic exercise attenuated neuronal damage. Immunofluorescence and Western blot analyses consistently revealed that HSYA combined with aerobic exercise markedly upregulated the expression of tight junction proteins ZO-1 and occludin, indicating effective repair of the damaged blood-brain barrier (BBB). Moreover, it improved synaptic function, as evidenced by increased levels of PSD95, GAP43, and SYN, as well as neurotrophins including BDNF and NGF. Molecular docking and Western blot analysis further showed that HSYA combined with aerobic exercise significantly elevated the expression of HIF-1α and p-CREB. Collectively, these findings suggest that HSYA combined with aerobic exercise facilitates synaptic functional recovery via the HIF-1α/CREB pathway, providing novel experimental evidence and theoretical support for multimodal combinatorial therapeutic strategies against CIRI.

We investigated the combined neuroprotective effects of hydroxysafflor yellow A (HSYA) and swimming exercise in a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) injury. title: Intraoperative Hypotension During Endovascular Therapy for Acute Ischemic Stroke and Functional Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal blood pressure management during endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. Intraprocedural hypotension may compromise cerebral perfusion and worsen neurological outcomes, yet existing evidence is inconsistent, and no prior meta-analysis has synthesized observational data on intraoperative hypotension during EVT.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating the association between intraoperative hypotension and outcomes in patients undergoing EVT for acute ischemic stroke. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to May 2024 without language restrictions. Eligible studies enrolled adult patients undergoing EVT with reported intraoperative blood pressure data and prespecified clinical outcomes. The primary outcome was favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included failure of reperfusion (Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction <2b), early neurological improvement, final infarct volume, and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. Pooled odds ratios with 95% CIs were estimated using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with the Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions tool and certainty of evidence with the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) framework.

RESULTS: Nine studies comprising 1737 patients were included in the systematic review, of which 7 contributed to quantitative synthesis. Intraoperative hypotension was significantly associated with lower odds of favorable functional outcome (odds ratio, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.41-0.74]; I2=0%). No significant association was found between hypotension and failure of reperfusion (odds ratio, 1.36 [95% CI, 0.85-2.18]). Evidence regarding early neurological improvement was limited. Narrative synthesis indicated that greater cumulative exposure to hypotension correlated with larger final infarct volumes. Certainty of evidence was rated high for favorable functional outcome and low for failure of reperfusion.

CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative hypotension during EVT, defined as mean arterial pressure below 60 to 70 mm Hg or a relative decrease of ≥20% to 40% from baseline, is associated with worse 90-day functional outcomes, independent of reperfusion status. These findings support hemodynamic monitoring during EVT and suggest that intraoperative hypotension is associated with worse functional outcomes.

Intraprocedural hypotension may compromise cerebral perfusion and worsen neurological outcomes, yet existing evidence is inconsistent, and no prior meta-analysis has synthesized observational data on intraoperative hypotension during EVT. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating the association between intraoperative hypotension and outcomes in patients undergoing EVT for acute ischemic stroke.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of cerebral edema in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective observational single-centre study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral edema (CED) is a common complication of acute ischemic stroke, associated with increased mortality and poor functional outcomes. While infarct size is a known predictor, the role of sodium homeostasis remains unclear. This study evaluated risk factors for CED and its impact on outcomes.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 178 patients with acute non-lacunar ischemic stroke. Cerebral edema was assessed and graded using the SITS-MOST edema scale over the first seven days. Sodium concentration and variability were monitored daily. Risk factors for CED were identified through multivariate logistic regression, and the impact of CED on mortality, functional outcomes, hemorrhagic transformation, and seizures was analyzed.

RESULTS: CED occurred in 38.2% of patients and was associated with larger infarcts (> 3 cm), higher NIHSS, lower ASPECTS, lack of reperfusion, and multi-territory involvement. No differences were observed in demographics or cardiovascular risk factors. Sodium levels were higher on days 3 and 5 in CED patients, with greater variability, while baseline levels were not predictive. Infarct size and day 3 sodium were independent predictors. CED was linked to worse outcomes, including higher 1-month mortality (23.5% vs. 1.8%), increased hemorrhagic transformation, and reduced functional independence. No association with seizures was found.

CONCLUSIONS: Infarct size remains the strongest risk factor for cerebral edema after ischemic stroke. Baseline sodium levels were not determining CED development. CED worsens outcomes but is not linked to seizure risk. These findings underscore the importance of early imaging and suggest a potential role for targeted anti-edema therapies in patients with larger strokes.

While infarct size is a known predictor, the role of sodium homeostasis remains unclear. This study evaluated risk factors for CED and its impact on outcomes.

title: Astrocytic NOX2 contributes to ROS-associated mitochondrial dysfunction in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury: modulation by electroacupuncture.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) causes severe neuronal damage, in which oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction are major pathological events. Astrocytes are important regulators of redox homeostasis in the injured brain, yet whether astrocytic NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) contributes to mitochondrial impairment after ischemia remains poorly understood. Electroacupuncture (EA) has been reported to protect against ischemic brain injury, but the cellular mechanisms involved remain unclear.

METHODS: In this study, a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model was combined with astrocyte-specific NOX2 knockdown using stereotactic viral delivery. Neurological deficits, infarct size, cerebral blood flow, reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) levels, mitochondrial morphology, and mitochondrial dynamics-associated proteins were examined.

RESULTS: MCAO/R resulted in increased astrocytic NOX2 expression, excessive ROS generation, mitochondrial fragmentation, impaired energy metabolism, and neurological dysfunction. EA treatment alleviated these changes by reducing NOX2 activation and ROS accumulation, improving mitochondrial morphology and ATP production, and restoring the balance between mitochondrial fission and fusion. These effects were reflected by decreased Drp1 and Fis1 expression and increased Mfn2 and Opa1 expression. Notably, astrocytic NOX2 knockdown produced similar protective effects and further strengthened the benefits of EA.

CONCLUSION: Astrocytic NOX2 contributes to ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ischemic brain injury. EA treatment is accompanied by reduced astrocytic NOX2 expression, attenuated oxidative stress, and restoration of mitochondrial homeostasis, suggesting that regulation of astrocytic NOX2 may contribute to the protective effects of EA. Targeting astrocytic NOX2 may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke.

Astrocytes are important regulators of redox homeostasis in the injured brain, yet whether astrocytic NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) contributes to mitochondrial impairment after ischemia remains poorly understood. Electroacupuncture (EA) has been reported to protect against ischemic brain injury, but the cellular mechanisms involved remain unclear.

title: [Predictive value and threshold effect analysis of the novel systemic immune-inflammatory complex index for functional outcomes at 90 days after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the correlation between the baseline systemic immune-inflammatory complex index (SIICI) and the 90-day functional prognosis of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) undergoing reperfusion therapy, as well as the threshold effect.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled. Patients were divided into good prognosis group [modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score was 0-2] and a poor prognosis group (mRS score was 3-6) according to the 90-day score after onset. The clinical data and blood routine indicators within 24 hours after onset were collected, and SIICI and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) were calculated. Univariate Logistic regression analysis was performed to screen 90-day functional prognosis-related influencing factors in patients with AIS after reperfusion therapy. Multivariate Logistic regression with multi-gradient adjustment was used to determine whether SIICI was an independent risk factor for poor functional prognosis or not. The restricted cubic spline (RCS) model was applied to analyze the dose-response relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor functional prognosis, and piecewise linear regression model was used for threshold effect analysis. Subjects were randomly divided into a training set and a validation set at a ratio of 7 : 3 for constructing a prognostic prediction model based on SIICI and internal validation. The receiver operator characteristic curve (ROC curve), calibration curve and decision curve analysis (DCA) were plotted to evaluate the discrimination, calibration and clinical net benefit of the model.

RESULTS: All 1 919 AIS patients were enrolled in the final analysis, including 1 176 cases (61.28%) in the good prognosis group and 743 cases (38.72%) in the poor prognosis group. Univariate Logistic regression analysis showed that advanced age, history of atrial fibrillation, bridging therapy, endovascular thrombectomy, elevated baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, prolonged total length of hospital stay, increased white blood cell count, elevated neutrophil count, elevated monocyte count, increased SII and elevated SIICI were risk factors for poor 90-day functional prognosis of AIS patients, and the history of hyperlipidemia and elevated lymphocyte count were protective factors (all P<0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis demonstrated that after adjusting for gender, age, past medical history, Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) classification and baseline NIHSS score, SIICI remained an independent risk factor for poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients [odds ratio (OR)=1.008, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.001-1.014, P=0.022], whereas SII showed no statistical significance after adjustment (OR=1.010, 95%CI was 0.999-1.020, P=0.067), suggesting that SIICI possessed better stability of independent association than the traditional inflammatory index SII. The RCS model verified a significant non-linear relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients (P<0.001). The optimal inflection point value of SIICI determined by piecewise linear regression was 15.03. When SIICI<15.03, each one-unit increase in SIICI was associated with an 11% increased risk of poor functional prognosis (OR=1.112, 95%CI was 1.078-1.147, P<0.001). When SIICI≥15.03, no statistically significant correlation was observed between SIICI and poor functional prognosis (OR=1.005, 95%CI was 0.998-1.012, P=0.136). For the SIICI-based prognosis prediction model, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.656 (95%CI was 0.626-0.686) in the training set and 0.639 (95%CI was 0.593-0.686) in the validation set, indicating favorable prognostic discrimination ability. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test yielded P=0.064, suggesting good model calibration. DCA revealed that the model obtained significant clinical net benefit within the high-risk threshold range of 0-0.8.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline SIICI is independently correlated with the 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients after reperfusion therapy and shows a significant threshold effect. It exhibits superior predictive performance compared with the traditional inflammatory index SII. The prognostic prediction model constructed based on SIICI can assist clinicians in stratifying the risk of early functional prognosis in patients with AIS undergoing reperfusion therapy.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled.

title: [Effect and mechanism of herb pair "Chuanxiong Rhizoma-Carthami Flos" in promoting cerebral angiogenesis in rat model of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury].
abstract: This study aims to investigate the protective effect of the herb pair Chuanxiong Rhizoma-Carthami Flos(CR-CF) on cerebral microvascular angiogenesis in the rat model of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and decipher its potential mechanism. A rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion(MCAO/R) was established through the modified Longa intraluminal suture method. Successfully modeled rats were randomly classified into the model, low-dose CR-CF(CR-CF-L, 0.8 g·kg~(-1)), medium-dose CR-CF(CR-CF-M, 1.6 g·kg~(-1)), high-dose CR-CF(CR-CF-H, 3.2 g·kg~(-1)), and butylphthalide soft capsules(BSC, 300 mg·kg~(-1)) groups, with 8 rats in each group. Another 8 SD rats underwent only isolation of the left common carotid artery without suture insertion and served as the sham group. The chemical constituents of CR-CF-containing cerebrospinal fluid were analyzed by LC-MS/MS. Laser speckle contrast imaging was performed to assess cerebral blood perfusion, Evans blue staining to evaluate blood-brain barrier permeability, and transmission electron microscopy to observe ultrastructural changes in the neurovascular unit. ELISA was employed to measure the levels of nitric oxide(NO), endothelial nitric oxide synthase(eNOS), angiopoietin-1(Ang-1), and vascular endothelial growth factor A(VEGFA). Immunofluorescence assay was performed to detect the expression of platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule1(CD31) and hematopoietic progenitor cell antigen(CD34). Transcriptomics was adopted to screen differentially expressed genes, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. Western blot was employed to quantify the expression of blood-brain barrier-related proteins, such as zonula occludens-1(ZO-1) and occludin, as well as hypoxia-inducible factor-1(HIF-1) pathway-related proteins. Oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation(OGD/R) was used to induce injury in rat brain microvascular endothelial cells(BMECs) for cell modeling. The optimal drug concentration was screened via the CCK-8 assay. The apoptosis of BMECs was detected by flow cytometry, and tube formation ability was evaluated by a tube formation assay. The results showed that compared with the sham operation group, the model group exhibited decreased cerebral blood perfusion, increased blood-brain barrier permeability, reduced angiogenesis, and downregulated expression of barrier-related proteins. Meanwhile, the expression of HIF-1α, VEGFA, and Notch receptor 1(Notch1) was upregulated. The CR-CF intervention improved cerebral blood perfusion, alleviated neurovascular unit injury, promoted angiogenesis, and enhanced the expression of blood-brain barrier-related proteins. Transcriptomic analysis showed that CR-CF mainly acted on the HIF-1α, VEGFA, and apoptosis signaling pathways. The cell experiments further confirmed that CR-CF-containing cerebrospinal fluid inhibited OGD/R-induced apoptosis of BMECs and restored their tube formation ability, whereas the HIF-1α inhibitor(PX-478) weakened these effects. In conclusion, CR-CF may activate the HIF-1α/VEGFA/Notch1 signaling pathway to promote cerebral microvascular angiogenesis and stabilize the blood-brain barrier, thereby ameliorating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.

title: [Mechanism of nourishing blood and activating blood circulation compatibility of Taohong Siwu Decoction in functional angiogenesis after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion].
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the effects of Taohong Siwu Decoction(THSWD) and its disassembled formulae on functional angiogenesis in rats with cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury(CIRI), as well as the compatibility mechanism. The middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion(MCAO/R) rat model was established using the intraluminal filament technique. After modeling, rats were randomly divided into a sham group, a model group, a THSWD group, a blood-nourishing(YX) group with the TCM of Rehmanniae Radix Praeparata, Paeoniae Radix Alba, Angelicae Sinensis Radix, and Chuanxiong Rhizoma, a blood-activating(HX) group with the TCM of Persicae Semen and Carthami Flos, and a nimodipine(NDP) group. Drug administration was conducted for seven days. Network pharmacology was employed to investigate the compatibility mechanism of THSWD and its disassembled formulae for vascular protection against ischemic stroke. Behavioral tests, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride(TTC) staining, and hematoxylineosin(HE) staining were performed for fundamental pharmacodynamic evaluation. Laser speckle imaging was used to assess cerebral blood flow recovery in the ischemic region. Evans blue staining was conducted to evaluate blood-brain barrier(BBB) permeability. The nitric oxide(NO) content in the serum was measured by a biochemical assay kit. The contents of endothelin-1(ET-1) in the serum and hemoglobin(HB) in the brain tissue were detected by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay(ELISA). Immunohistochemical staining was performed to detect microvessel density in the ischemic region. A transmission electron microscope was used to observe ultrastructural changes of cerebral vessels. The expression levels of tight junction proteins(claudin-5, occludin, and ZO-1), matrix metalloproteinase-9(MMP-9), tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-1(TIMP-1), vascular endothelial growth factor A(VEGFA), and angiopoietin-1(Ang-1) were detected by Western blot. Network pharmacology analysis reveals that the HX group is biased toward matrix degradation and angiogenesis, while the YX group is biased toward vascular structural protection. Animal experiments show that the THSWD group exhibits significantly improved neurological deficits, reduced infarct volume, and restored cerebral blood perfusion compared with the disassembled formula groups. YX group exhibited up-regulated protein expression levels of claudin-5, occludin, ZO-1, TIMP-1, and Ang-1, down-regulated MMP-9 protein expression level, and maintained BBB integrity and basement membrane stability. In the HX group, vascular vasoconstrictive function was improved; VEGFA expression was up-regulated; microvessel density was increased. However, the MMP-9/TIMP-1 balance shifted toward matrix degradation. The expression levels of VEGFA and Ang-1 were simultaneously up-regulated in the THSWD group, synergistically promoting the initiation and maturation of neovessels and maintaining the dynamic balance of MMP-9/TIMP-1. All in all, THSWD achieves functional angiogenesis of "removing stasis to promote regeneration without retaining stasis" through the synergistic compatibility of blood-nourishing components maintaining vascular structural stability and blood-activating components initiating neovascularization, providing a new mechanistic basis for TCM in the prevention and treatment of CIRI.

title: Danhong Injection combined with t-PA attenuates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and reduces hemorrhagic transformation: association with NF-κB/MMPs signaling.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Ischemic stroke, caused by cerebral arterial thrombosis and interrupted blood supply, is a leading cause of brain dysfunction. Tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) is the standard thrombolytic agent but is limited by hemorrhagic transformation (HT) and blood-brain barrier (BBB) damage. This study explored the beneficial effects of Danhong Injection (DHI, a Traditional Chinese Medicine) as an adjuvant combined with t-PA for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

METHODS: Based on cell viability assays, optimal concentrations were 20 μl/ml DHI + 20 μg/ml t-PA. In vitro (mouse brain microvascular endothelial cell, OGD/R model) and in vivo (MCAO rat model) experiments were conducted to assess relevant parameters.

KEY FINDINGS: In vitro, the combination improved cell morphology, reduced apoptosis, and downregulated phosphorylated NF-κB p65, MMP-2, MMP-9, and hypoxia-inducible factor-1α expression. In vivo, DHI + t-PA decreased P-Selectin, 6-keto-PGF1a, TXA2, PAI-1, MMP-2, and MMP-9 levels, alleviated cerebral infarction and HT, and enhanced neurological recovery.

CONCLUSIONS: These protective effects were accompanied by downregulation of the NF-κB/MMPs pathway, suggesting a plausible correlation linked to BBB-related protective phenotypes. Our findings provide preliminary evidence supporting DHI as a promising adjuvant to optimize t-PA-based stroke therapy.

Tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) is the standard thrombolytic agent but is limited by hemorrhagic transformation (HT) and blood-brain barrier (BBB) damage. This study explored the beneficial effects of Danhong Injection (DHI, a Traditional Chinese Medicine) as an adjuvant combined with t-PA for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

title: Dynamics of Serum Amyloid A Levels in the Blood, Brain and Liver in a Mouse Model of Focal Cerebral Ischemia.
abstract: This study examined the dynamics of serum amyloid A (SAA) levels in the blood, brain, and liver over time using a mouse model of focal cerebral ischemia induced by occlusion of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) for 4 h followed by reperfusion. Blood SAA concentrations increased transiently after cerebral infarction, coinciding with changes in brain and liver SAA gene expression and protein levels. SAA concentrations in the brain, liver, and blood increased at similar time points after cerebral infarction, suggesting that SAA may serve as an important indicator of the associated pathological condition.

title: Bridging Thrombolysis Versus Direct Endovascular Thrombectomy in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients With ASPECTS ≤5: A Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is a standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) caused by large vessel occlusion (LVO). However, the efficacy and safety of bridging thrombolysis (BT) compared to direct EVT (dEVT) remain controversial, particularly in patients with large core infarcts (Alberta stroke program early CT score [ASPECTS] ≤5). This meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of BT versus dEVT in this population.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from January 1, 2010, to September 21, 2024, for studies comparing BT and dEVT in AIS patients with ASPECTS ≤5. Outcomes included functional outcomes (mRS 0-2 and 0-3), intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), symptomatic ICH (sICH), 90-day mortality, and successful reperfusion. Data were pooled using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Twelve studies (3907 patients) were included. BT significantly improved favorable (OR: 1.43, 95% CI: 1.17-1.76) and moderate functional outcomes (OR: 1.28, 95% CI: 1.10-1.48) compared to dEVT. No significant differences were observed in sICH, ICH, 90-day mortality, or successful reperfusion.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that BT may be associated with better functional outcomes in patients with ASPECTS ≤5, without increasing major safety events compared with dEVT. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the evidence is mainly observational, and residual confounding cannot be excluded. Further well-designed randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is a standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) caused by large vessel occlusion (LVO). However, the efficacy and safety of bridging thrombolysis (BT) compared to direct EVT (dEVT) remain controversial, particularly in patients with large core infarcts (Alberta stroke program early CT score [ASPECTS] ≤5). This meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of BT versus dEVT in this population.

title: Comparative Effectiveness of Intravenous Tenecteplase versus Alteplase in Posterior Circulation Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior circulation ischemic stroke (PCIS) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, and the optimal intravenous thrombolytic strategy in this subgroup remains unclear.

METHODS: We searched databases for studies comparing intravenous tenecteplase with alteplase in adults with PCIS. The primary outcome was functional independence at 90 days (mRS 0-2). Secondary outcomes included other functional outcomes, reperfusion, hemorrhagic complications, and mortality.

RESULTS: Five studies involving 997 patients were included. Regarding efficacy outcomes, tenecteplase was associated with a significantly greater likelihood of achieving an ambulatory functional outcome at 90 days (mRS 0-3) [RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.03-1.60; p = 0.02] and improved pre-EVT perfusion [RR 2.18, 95% CI 1.06-4.46; p = 0.03]. No significant differences were observed for excellent functional outcome (mRS 0-1) [RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.91-1.56; p = 0.20], functional independence (mRS 0-2) [RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.89-1.37; p = 0.39], or post-EVT perfusion [RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.89-1.40; p = 0.34]. Regarding safety outcomes, no significant differences were observed between tenecteplase and alteplase for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) [RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.36-2.22; p = 0.81], any intracranial hemorrhage [RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.59-1.78; p = 0.94], parenchymal hematoma [RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.24-2.38; p = 0.64], or 90-day mortality [RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.66-1.17; p = 0.39].

CONCLUSION: Tenecteplase may improve reperfusion and ambulatory recovery without increasing hemorrhagic complications or mortality compared with alteplase in PCIS, although larger PCIS-specific studies are needed.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Posterior circulation ischemic stroke (PCIS) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, and the optimal intravenous thrombolytic strategy in this subgroup remains unclear. METHODS: We searched databases for studies comparing intravenous tenecteplase with alteplase in adults with PCIS. The primary outcome was functional independence at 90 days (mRS 0-2).

title: Perfusion-Based Collaterals in Prediction of Infarct Growth in Patients with Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Multicenter Comparative Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: In patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS), robust collaterals are associated with lower rates of infarct growth. Perfusion-based collateral matrices, including hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR), relative CBV (rCBV) index, and perfusion collateral index (PCI), have been used successfully to assess collaterals in patients with AIS. We aimed to assess and compare the diagnostic ability of these perfusion-based collateral indices in the prediction of infarct growth in patients with AIS after successful reperfusion.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion were included if they had pretreatment perfusion (CT or MR), successful reperfusion (modified TICI ≥ 2b), and follow-up MRI within 24-48 hours from the date of treatment. The primary outcome assessed was substantial infarct growth, which was defined as a final infarct volume of ≥10 mL compared with the baseline ischemic core volume. Perfusion-based collateral indices including HIR (volume of time-to-maximum [Tmax] >10 seconds/volume of Tmax >6 seconds) and rCBV index (mean of rCBV values within the volume of Tmax > 6 seconds) were calculated using RAPID software (Version 5.0.4), and PCI (volume of delay2-6 seconds multiplied by its corresponding mean rCBV) was calculated using Olea software (SP.23). The association between perfusion-based collateral indices, along with demographic and clinical variables for determination of infarct growth, was tested using appropriate univariate analysis. Multivariable logistic regression using a stepwise backward selection approach was performed to identify independent predictors of infarct growth.

RESULTS: Among 116 included patients, 58 (50%) had infarct growth ≥10 mL. Infarct growth volume (median, interquartile range) was: 11, 2.6-34.7 mL. Poor collaterals determined by PCI and rCBV index was significantly (P < .01) associated with infarct growth, whereas HIR was not (P = .83). Following multivariate logistic regression, 3 variables remained as independent predictors of infarct growth: baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (OR = 1.10; 95% CI: 1.02-1.15; P = .005); rCBV index (OR = 0.005; 95% CI: 0.00-0.14; P = .002); and PCI (OR = 0.99; 95% CI: 0.98-0.99; P = .01).

CONCLUSIONS: Perfusion-based collateral indices that integrate CBV (rCBV index and PCI) outperformed delay-based HIR in the prediction of substantial infarct growth in patients with AIS, and may play an important role in treatment decision-making, patient transfer decisions, and prognostication.

Perfusion-based collateral matrices, including hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR), relative CBV (rCBV) index, and perfusion collateral index (PCI), have been used successfully to assess collaterals in patients with AIS. We aimed to assess and compare the diagnostic ability of these perfusion-based collateral indices in the prediction of infarct growth in patients with AIS after successful reperfusion.

title: Deterioration of Peri-Infarct Microvascular Hemodynamics Following Successful Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke Predicts Infarct Growth.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microvascular hemodynamic deterioration is a proposed mechanism underlying the no-reflow phenomenon in acute ischemic stroke. Experimental studies suggested that relative heterogeneity of capillary transit time (RTH) is a potential imaging biomarker of microvascular impairment. We investigated the relationship between peri-infarct RTH and infarct growth, measured on immediate post-thrombectomy (PT) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with successful reperfusion.

METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study from the University of California, Los Angeles, patients with acute ischemic stroke from 2015 to 2020 were included if they had excellent reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2c) and diffusion- and perfusion-weighted MRIs at baseline, immediately PT, and 24 to 48 hours after thrombectomy. Peri-infarct regions were defined as time to maximum ≥6-second regions on baseline MRI that were not infarcted on immediate PT MRI. Following image coregistration, quantitative values of perfusion parameters, including RTH, were obtained from peri-infarct regions on immediate PT MRI. Two primary outcomes were assessed: (1) infarct growth ≥10 mL and (2) poor functional outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale score >2). Associations between clinical and imaging parameters and outcomes were evaluated using univariate analysis. Age, sex, and covariates that were significant in univariate analysis were included in logistic regression analyses.

RESULTS: Among 47 patients included in the analysis (62% women; mean age, 72±13 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, 14), 20 (43%) patients had substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcome. Peri-infarct RTH was significantly (P=0.005) higher in patients with infarct growth >10 mL than those without and remained as an independent predictor (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-2.0]; P=0.04). Similarly, the peri-infarct RTH was significantly higher (P<0.001) in patients with poor functional outcomes than those with good functional outcomes and remained as a significant predictor of poor functional outcome (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-1.9]; P=0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: Increased peri-infarct RTH on immediate PT MRI predicts substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcomes in successfully reperfused patients with acute ischemic stroke. Results highlight the role of microvascular dysfunction depicted by elevated RTH as a potential marker of no-reflow phenomenon despite excellent macrovascular reperfusion.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Microvascular hemodynamic deterioration is a proposed mechanism underlying the no-reflow phenomenon in acute ischemic stroke. Experimental studies suggested that relative heterogeneity of capillary transit time (RTH) is a potential imaging biomarker of microvascular impairment. We investigated the relationship between peri-infarct RTH and infarct growth, measured on immediate post-thrombectomy (PT) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with successful reperfusion.

title: Longxue tongluo capsule enhances ischemic stroke recovery via microbiota-metabolite-gene interactions.
abstract: The gut-brain axis represents an emerging therapeutic target. This study seeks to investigate the regulatory effects of LXTL on the brain-gut axis and to elucidate its mechanism of action during the ischemic stroke recovery period. This study investigated the effects of LXTL on a middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion model. The assessment of recovery effects was conducted through the evaluation of brain injury scores, Y-maze performance, open field tests. Furthermore, comprehensive analyses were conducted on the gut microbiota, damaged brain tissue, cecal contents, and brain samples using metagenomic sequencing, transcriptomic sequencing, and non-targeted metabolomics. And the selected targets were verified. Integrated analyses were conducted by constructing correlation networks and performing joint pathway enrichment to elucidate the connections between microbial alterations, metabolite changes, and gene expression modifications. LXTL improved cognitive and exploratory behaviors, reduced brain damage and neuron loss, and enhanced gut health by increasing beneficial bacteria like Eubacterium and Kurthia. It boosted SCFAs, neuroactive metabolites, and altered nucleotide metabolism. LXTL is linked to genes involved in neurorepair and immune homeostasis, correlates with microglial polarization, and is associated with genes such as Ngfr, Card9, Chat, Nkg7, and Gch1 within the pertinent pathways. The integrated network linked LXTL-enhanced microbiota, gut and brain metabolites, and repair genes, facilitating recovery through a neurorepair-immune-metabolic triad. LXTL aids ischemic stroke recovery by altering gut microbiota and gut-brain metabolite profiles, while regulating brain gene networks related to neuroplasticity, inflammation, and metabolism. This demonstrates LXTL's multi-target effects through the gut-brain axis, underscoring the potential of herbal medicine in stroke rehabilitation.
englishSummary: The gut-brain axis represents an emerging therapeutic target. This study seeks to investigate the regulatory effects of LXTL on the brain-gut axis and to elucidate its mechanism of action during the ischemic stroke recovery period. This study investigated the effects of LXTL on a middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion model.

title: Dihydromyricetin attenuates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury associated with modulation of sirtuin 1-forkhead box O3 signaling and mitophagy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial neurological disability, and effective strategies for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) are limited. Dihydromyricetin (DHM) has shown neuroprotective properties in experimental neurological disorders, but its effects and associated molecular mechanisms in CIRI remain incompletely understood. This study therefore evaluated the protective effects of DHM pretreatment and examined the signaling events associated with these effects in experimental CIRI.

METHODS: A mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion followed by reperfusion and an HT-22 cell model of oxygen-glucose deprivation followed by reoxygenation were used to evaluate the effects of DHM. In vivo outcomes included infarct volume, histopathological injury, neurological deficits, and recognition memory. In vitro outcomes included cell viability, lactate dehydrogenase release, apoptosis, oxidative stress, adenosine triphosphate content, and mitochondrial morphology. Network pharmacology was used to nominate candidate regulatory targets. Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) expression and deacetylase activity, forkhead box O3 (FOXO3) acetylation and subcellular localization, and mitophagy-related changes were assessed by immunoblotting, nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation, immunofluorescence, and co-immunoprecipitation. The selective SIRT1 inhibitor EX527 and small interfering RNA-mediated SIRT1 knockdown were used to examine SIRT1 involvement, whereas bafilomycin A1 and Parkin knockdown were used to assess mitophagic flux and the functional contribution of Parkin. A cellular thermal shift assay was used to test whether DHM produced a detectable change in SIRT1 thermal stability.

RESULTS: DHM pretreatment reduced infarct volume, improved neurological scores and recognition memory, and ameliorated histopathological injury in mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. In HT-22 cells subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation, DHM improved cell viability and adenosine triphosphate content, reduced oxidative stress and apoptosis, and preserved mitochondrial morphology. These effects were accompanied by increased SIRT1 expression and deacetylase activity, reduced FOXO3 acetylation, increased nuclear FOXO3, and changes in phosphatase and tensin homolog-induced kinase 1/Parkin and mitophagy-related markers consistent with enhanced mitophagic flux. EX527 and SIRT1 knockdown attenuated several molecular and protective effects of DHM, and Parkin knockdown weakened DHM-associated improvements in cellular outcomes. The cellular thermal shift assay did not detect a DHM-induced shift in SIRT1 thermal stability.

CONCLUSION: In the tested experimental models, DHM attenuated experimental CIRI, and these effects were associated with increased SIRT1 activity, FOXO3 deacetylation and nuclear accumulation, and Parkin-mediated mitophagy. Post-ischemic treatment studies and direct molecular validation are required to establish therapeutic relevance and the precise causal relationships among these events.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial neurological disability, and effective strategies for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) are limited. Dihydromyricetin (DHM) has shown neuroprotective properties in experimental neurological disorders, but its effects and associated molecular mechanisms in CIRI remain incompletely understood. This study therefore evaluated the protective effects of DHM pretreatment and examined the signaling events associated with these effects in experimental CIRI.

title: Electroacupuncture alleviates ferroptosis through miR-145-5p/ACSL4 axis to reduce post-reperfusion brain injury in ischemic stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ferroptosis induced by reperfusion in ischemic stroke (IS) represent core mechanisms that exacerbate brain injury and neurological dysfunction. Electroacupuncture (EA) is widely used in neurological rehabilitation, but its specific mechanism for improving reperfusion injury in ischemic stroke remains unclear.

METHODS: We established a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mouse model, the impacts of EA on infarction volume, cerebral cortex damage, and neuronal apoptosis were observed using pathological staining. Additionally, an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) SH-SY5Y cell model were established. miR-145-5p and Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) expression were assessed through qRT-PCR, and the targeted regulatory relationship between the two was validated by a dual luciferase assay. CCK-8 assay, EdU staining, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) assay kit, flow cytometry, and Calcein/PI staining were applied to detected cell proliferation and damage. Markers associated with oxidative stress and ferroptosis were detected using different assay kits, while ferroptosis-related proteins levels were assessed through Western blot.

RESULTS: In vivo, EA reduced cerebral infarction volume in MCAO mice, lowered neurological deficit scores, alleviated cerebral edema and blood-brain barrier damage, and inhibited neuronal apoptosis. MiR-145-5p was downregulated in MCAO mice, EA treatment upregulated miR-145-5p and downregulated ACSL4 expression, and inhibited the excessive production of NO and NOS isoforms expression in ischemic brain tissue, thereby improving oxidative stress and ferroptosis. Silencing miR-145-5p or overexpressing ACSL4 both weakened the beneficial impact of EA on MCAO mice. OGD/R diminished viability and proliferation capacity in SH-SY5Y cells, increased LDH release, and elevated apoptosis rates. MiR-145-5p overexpression suppressed ACSL4 expression, ameliorated oxidative stress and ferroptosis, and mitigated OGD/R-induced cellular damage, whereas ACSL4 overexpression reversed this protective effect.

CONCLUSION: EA alleviates oxidative stress and ferroptosis in IS after reperfusion through upregulating miR-145-5p and suppressing ACSL4 expression.

Electroacupuncture (EA) is widely used in neurological rehabilitation, but its specific mechanism for improving reperfusion injury in ischemic stroke remains unclear. METHODS: We established a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mouse model, the impacts of EA on infarction volume, cerebral cortex damage, and neuronal apoptosis were observed using pathological staining.

title: Cinchonain Ib alleviates the cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by regulating mitophagy through AKT/mTOR signaling pathway.
abstract: Cinchonain Ib has demonstrated numerous potential pharmacological properties. However, its therapeutic efficacy against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury and underlying molecular mechanisms remained elusive. The mitophagy has been widely studied and demonstrated to play a critical role in the pathogenesis of IR, and currently therapeutic drugs were inefficient. This study aimed to investigate the effects of cinchonain Ib against IR and elucidate its underlying mechanism. We explored the role of cinchonain Ib using neuroblastoma (N2a) cell exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R), and mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). The results indicated that cinchonain Ib supplementation effectively ameliorated IR injury due to the mitigations of cell death and mitophagy through AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. In MCAO mice model, cinchonain Ib administration significantly reduced neuronal death, enhanced neurological recovery, and attenuated mitophagy. Furthermore, in the N2a-induced OGD/R model, cinchonain Ib exerted an inhibitory effect on the cell death, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and mitophagy. Western blot analysis revealed that cinchonain Ib inhibited the activation of the AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, consequently attenuating mitophagy and mitigating the IR injury. Overall, our data indicated that cinchonain Ib was a promising therapeutic agent for early prevention and treatment of ischemic stroke.

However, its therapeutic efficacy against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury and underlying molecular mechanisms remained elusive. The mitophagy has been widely studied and demonstrated to play a critical role in the pathogenesis of IR, and currently therapeutic drugs were inefficient.

title: Stepwise neutrophil-to-neuron targeting nanotherapy for mitochondrial protection and blood-brain barrier preservation in ischemic stroke.
abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, yet the clinical efficacy of reperfusion therapies remains severely constrained by a narrow therapeutic time window and secondary ischemia-reperfusion injury. Preserving the viability of the ischemic penumbra through early, multi-target neuroprotection represents a promising strategy to extend this window; however, effective approaches that simultaneously address neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption are lacking. Here, we report a dual-modal, stepwise-targeting lipid nanoparticle (DM-LNP) platform that integrates mitochondrial protection with matrix metalloproteinase-12 (MMP-12) silencing to achieve coordinated neurovascular protection in ischemic stroke. DM-LNP is engineered with a sialic acid-based neutrophil-targeting outer layer and a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive thioketal linker that enables ligand switching to expose a neuron-targeting Tet1 peptide within the ischemic microenvironment. This design allows sequential neutrophil-mediated BBB traversal (Modal I) and precise neuronal targeting (Modal II). Functionally, DM-LNP delivers MMP-12 siRNA to suppress downstream MMP activation and preserve BBB integrity, while a spermidine-derived gene carrier promotes Pink1-Parkin-mediated mitophagy, restores mitochondrial homeostasis, reduces oxidative stress, inhibits neuronal apoptosis, and drives microglial polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. In transient and prolonged middle cerebral artery occlusion models, DM-LNP significantly improves cerebral blood flow recovery, reduces infarct volume, alleviates neurological deficits, and extends the effective reperfusion window up to 8 h post-ischemia. Together, this work establishes a multifunctional, ROS-responsive nanotherapeutic strategy that stabilizes the neuron-microglia-BBB axis and offers a viable approach for extending reperfusion benefits in ischemic stroke.

Preserving the viability of the ischemic penumbra through early, multi-target neuroprotection represents a promising strategy to extend this window; however, effective approaches that simultaneously address neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption are lacking. Here, we report a dual-modal, stepwise-targeting lipid nanoparticle (DM-LNP) platform that integrates mitochondrial protection with matrix metalloproteinase-12 (MMP-12) silencing to achieve coordinated neurovascular protection in ischemic stroke.

title: Safety and efficacy of repeated intravenous thrombolysis within 3 months for acute ischemic stroke: a systematic review and individual-patient data meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current stroke guidelines consider a previous acute ischemic stroke (AIS) within 3 months a relative contraindication to intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) because of the perceived risk of symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage (sICH). The recommendation is largely based on expert consensus, while growing evidence suggests repeated IVT (RIVT) may be feasible in selected patients.

AIMS: To systematically review the efficacy and safety of RIVT for recurrent AIS within 90 days of a previous IVT-treated stroke.

RESULTS: We performed a systematic review and individual-patient data meta-analysis, including 28 reports (63 patients), with individual patient data available for 44 cases. Overall, 66.7% of patients achieved a favorable outcome, with a 7.5 days median interval between treatments. Meta-analysis showed a non-significant trend toward better functional outcomes after RIVT (pooled OR = 1.52, 95% CI 0.97-2.39; I2 = 0%) and no significant increase in functional deterioration between stroke episodes (pooled OR = 1.28, 95% CI 0.75-2.19; I2 = 0%). Outcomes were not influenced by treatment interval, age, sex, stroke etiology, vascular territory, or onset-to-treatment time. No sICH occurred after RIVT. Asymptomatic intracranial or systemic haemorrhages were reported in 15.9% of patients, while fatal events (5%) were unrelated to neurological complications. Haemorrhagic and fatal events occurred predominantly in patients with cardioembolic and more severe strokes.

CONCLUSIONS: RIVT within 90 days is a rare event and its efficacy is understudied. It may be a reasonable reperfusion strategy in carefully selected patients with recurrent AIS, suggesting that the interval from the previous stroke should not be considered an isolated exclusion criterion for IVT.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Current stroke guidelines consider a previous acute ischemic stroke (AIS) within 3 months a relative contraindication to intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) because of the perceived risk of symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage (sICH). The recommendation is largely based on expert consensus, while growing evidence suggests repeated IVT (RIVT) may be feasible in selected patients. AIMS: To systematically review the efficacy and safety of RIVT for recurrent AIS within 90 days of a previous IVT-treated stroke.
