title: Anti-inflammatory effects of the injectable hydrogen-releasing material Mg2Si on rheumatoid foot.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune inflammatory disease that typically affects multiple symmetrical joints, particularly the foot. To date, the intricate pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis remains elusive, with a primary hallmark being increased oxidative stress and excessive production of reactive oxygen species. Molecular hydrogen, which can selectively scavenge hydroxyl radicals, has been widely used to treat inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis. However, traditional hydrogen delivery strategies struggle to maintain high concentrations, significantly compromising the therapeutic efficacy of rheumatoid arthritis. As a new type of micro-nano material, magnesium silicide (Mg2Si) generates high concentrations of hydrogen after local injection. In this study, Mg2Si was locally injected into the ankle joints of collagen-induced arthritis rats to observe the ameliorative effect of Mg2Si on arthritis in rats with rheumatoid foot. Compared with the blank control group, the model group presented increased inflammation according to the arthritis score, inflammatory factor level, and various clinical examinations, including pathology, ultrasound, digital radiography, and micro-computed tomography. In contrast, after treatment with molecular hydrogen, which was released by Mg2Si, the arthritis symptoms of rats with rheumatoid foot were significantly alleviated. As a novel micro-nanomaterial, Mg2Si can maintain a high concentration of hydrogen after local injection. The above results suggest that the molecular hydrogen released by Mg2Si have anti-inflammatory effects on rheumatoid arthritis, which opens up a new approach for the clinical treatment of patients with rheumatoid arthritis.

To date, the intricate pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis remains elusive, with a primary hallmark being increased oxidative stress and excessive production of reactive oxygen species. title: Hydrogen induces microglial M2 polarization and improves neurological outcomes of rats with traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated that hydrogen confers neuroprotection, although the associated mechanism is poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which hydrogen protects against neural injury. A traumatic brain injury model was established using controlled cortical impact injury, and then rats were twice exposed to 4% hydrogen (21% oxygen) for 1 hour. Results showed that hydrogen inhalation reduced brain edema and neurological deficits in traumatic brain injury rats. Hydrogen inhalation increases the number of M2-type microglia while reducing the number of M1-type microglia. Additionally, hydrogen inhalation can downregulate the expression of Jak2, Stat1, Stat3, and Hmgb1 genes. Therefore, hydrogen inhalation may exert a neuroprotective effect after traumatic brain injury by inhibiting the JAK/STAT signal transduction and subsequently influencing the polarization of microglia.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy for a Patient with Antithrombin Deficiency and Intraprocedural Thrombus Formation.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Antithrombin (AT) deficiency is a rare type of inherited thrombophilia that commonly increases the risk of venous thromboembolism. However, its association with ischemic stroke remains unclear. Herein, we report a case of intraprocedural thrombus formation during mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in a patient with known AT deficiency.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 49-year-old male patient presented with left hemiparesis and conjugate deviation. He had a history of embolic stroke and previously documented AT deficiency. Imaging revealed right middle cerebral artery M1 occlusion, and intravenous thrombolysis followed by MT was performed. During the procedure, extensive thrombus formation developed in the internal carotid artery, resulting in temporary occlusion. Additional heparinization and repeated thrombectomy were required to restore blood flow. Partial reperfusion was achieved, and the procedure was completed with expanded Treatment in Cerebral Ischemia grade 2a recanalization. Postoperatively, AT concentrate, heparin, and warfarin were administered. The patient regained his premorbid activities of daily living, and recurrent ischemic stroke was not observed during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: AT deficiency may have been one of several factors contributing not only to embolic stroke but also to intraprocedural thrombotic instability during MT. In patients with known AT deficiency, thrombus formation may be promoted by inadequate anticoagulation and procedural factors, such as device manipulation and prolonged intervention. Cautious perioperative assessment of AT activity, consideration of AT concentrate supplementation, and appropriate anticoagulation monitoring may be important for preventing secondary thrombus formation during reperfusion therapy.

However, its association with ischemic stroke remains unclear. Herein, we report a case of intraprocedural thrombus formation during mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in a patient with known AT deficiency.

title: Temporal Trend and Geographic Variation in Anticoagulation of Patients Hospitalized with Acute Pulmonary Embolism: the RIETE Registry from 2013 to 2024.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: A recent U.S. study of initial anticoagulation in adults with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring hospitalization found intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) use exceeded 50%. Guidelines, however, recommend low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) over UFH for most patients requiring parenteral anticoagulation. Use patterns in other geographic regions are unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed data from Registro Informatizado de la Enfermedad TromboEmbólica, a prospective multinational registry of consecutive patients with venous thromboembolism. We included adults hospitalized for acute PE from 2013 through 2024 in 273 hospitals across 31 countries. We assessed temporal trend and regional variation in initial anticoagulation. Using multivariable regression, we identified variables independently associated with UFH.

RESULTS: Among 36,210 adults, 83.2% received subcutaneous LMWH, 7.1% UFH, and 6.8% direct oral anticoagulants. LMWH use decreased slightly from 2013 to 2024 (85.8-79.2%; unadjusted), while UFH increased (8.9-10.4%). Wide geographic variation was observed in overall use of LMWH (37-95%) and UFH (2-39%). When adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates, increased weight, recent surgery, recent major bleeding, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, severe renal dysfunction, abnormal vital signs, and early reperfusion therapy were positively associated, whereas age > 80 years, active cancer, chronic lung disease, prior ischemic stroke, and year were negatively associated with UFH. Compared with Spanish hospitals, hospitals in other European countries, the United States, and Asia were independently associated with UFH use.

CONCLUSION: Results highlight opportunities for some geographic regions to align anticoagulation practices more closely with evidence-based guidelines recommending LMWH as the preferred parenteral agent in most patients with PE requiring hospitalization.

title: Automated Quantitative Assessment of Recanalization in Endovascular Thrombectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains a major cause of death and disability worldwide. Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) has substantially improved outcomes by restoring cerebral blood flow. The TICI score, the current standard for recanalization assessment, is a semiquantitative grading system that is commonly used to evaluate the effectiveness of thrombectomy, but it suffers from interrater variability and is poorly correlated with clinical outcomes. Here, we propose a novel and fully automated quantitative TICI (qTICI) score derived from DSA during EVT that integrates morphologic descriptors, vascular network topology, and perfusion dynamics to provide a numeric quantitative reperfusion metric.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a prospectively collected cohort of 295 patients with AIS who underwent EVT, we developed an automated pipeline to extract vascular morphology and perfusion metrics from postrecanalization DSA images. We integrated selected features to compute qTICI and evaluated its performance against adjudicated extended TICI (eTICI) grades, provided by expert interventional neuroradiologists, to predict clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Although the qTICI score demonstrated moderate agreement with the eTICI grades (micro-average area under the curve [AUC] 0.70), it outperformed eTICI in predicting both early and long-term outcomes among successfully recanalized patients (72-hour NIHSS: AUC = 0.60 vs 0.47; 90-day mRS: AUC = 0.55 vs 0.46). Combining qTICI with additional clinical variables further enhanced its predictive performance. Multivariable analyses showed a greater contribution of qTICI to outcome predictions compared with eTICI.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that automated qTICI offers an objective and enhanced alternative to visual grading with modest improvements in prognostic accuracy for AIS outcomes. Prospective, multicenter validation is warranted to standardize reperfusion assessment and support integration of qTICI into clinical trials and stroke care.

title: Copper dyshomeostasis and cuproptosis in representative vascular and neurovascular diseases: Molecular mechanisms, disease-specific evidence, and unresolved questions: A scoping review.
abstract: Copper dyshomeostasis often coexists with mitochondrial dysfunction, redox imbalance, inflammation and disrupted proteostasis, but none of these changes establishes mechanistically defined cuproptosis. This scoping review, reported according to PRISMA-ScR, applies an author-defined, four-category evidence framework (copper dyshomeostasis, general copper-related injury, cuproptosis-compatible findings, mechanistically defined cuproptosis) to cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), vascular cognitive impairment (VCI)/vascular dementia (VaD), atherosclerosis and hypertension-related vascular remodeling. For each context, it charts how far the evidence extends along the cuproptosis-defining mechanistic chain and appraises methodological quality separately. In CIRI, copper was quantified in bulk tissue, and readouts came from neurons, neuron-like lines or unsorted brain. In VCI/VaD, the most mechanistic study relied on ionophore-delivered copper in umbilical venous rather than cerebral endothelium, and the only endogenous-hypoperfusion study with a chelator arm had no lipoylation-specific readout. In atherosclerosis, extracellular copper-mediated lipoprotein oxidation must be distinguished from intracellular cuproptosis. The only study to state a non-reducing, non-boiled protocol for higher-order DLAT species, however, measured copper as bulk aortic content. The most complete hypertension study documented the lipoylation lesion, with an independent chelator comparator and labile Cu(I) imaging, but measured no cell death. Across all four contexts, no study demonstrated compartment-resolved copper in a dying cell population or attributed death to a defined lineage, and none reached mechanistically defined cuproptosis. The evidence is disease-specific, with different gaps in each context, and does not support a unified etiology. Closing these gaps requires compartment-resolved copper, validated lipoylation and aggregation assays, and death readouts in the same defined cells.

title: Adjunct Intra-Arterial Thrombolysis following Endovascular Thrombectomy in Different Patient Subgroups: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Ten Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite successful endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), many patients with acute ischemic stroke fail to achieve excellent functional outcome. We evaluated whether adjunct intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) improves this outcome and whether patient subgroups modify its effect.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing adjunctive IAT following EVT with EVT alone. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale score of 0-1 at 90 days. Subgroup analyses were stratified by bridging intravenous thrombolysis (IVT), thrombolytic agent, occlusion site, and Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (TICI) reperfusion grade.

RESULTS: Ten RCTs comprising 2,988 randomized participants were included, of whom 2,958 contributed to the primary-outcome analysis. Excellent functional outcome occurred in 44.9% of patients receiving adjunctive IAT and 36.9% receiving EVT alone (RR 1.22, 95% CI 1.10-1.35). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in functional independence, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or mortality. However, these confidence intervals did not exclude clinically important harm. Formal interaction tests did not detect effect modification by bridging IVT status, thrombolytic agent (alteplase or tenecteplase), or TICI reperfusion grade. The benefit was statistically significant in anterior but not in posterior circulation occlusion, although the test for subgroup interaction was not significant.

DISCUSSION: Adjunctive IAT improved excellent functional outcome. However, the safety estimates were imprecise, and the optimal patient population requires further investigation.

We evaluated whether adjunct intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) improves this outcome and whether patient subgroups modify its effect. METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing adjunctive IAT following EVT with EVT alone.

title: Mechanical thrombectomy with CEREGLIDE 71 Intermediate Catheter: A single-center post-market experience.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the efficacy and safety of the CEREGLIDE 71 Intermediate Catheter in a real-world clinical setting.

METHODS: This was a retrospective, single-center, post-market observational study. All consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) who underwent mechanical thrombectomy (MT) with CEREGLIDE 71 between October 2024 and September 2025 were included. The primary outcome was the rate of successful recanalization (final modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] ≥2b). Secondary efficacy outcomes included complete revascularization (final mTICI ≥2c), first-pass mTICI ≥2c, and first-pass mTICI ≥2b. Safety and clinical outcomes included device-related adverse events, such as vessel dissection, perforation, or catheter breakage, and good functional outcome at 90 days (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score ≤2). The subgroup of patients treated with a direct aspiration first-pass technique (ADAPT) as the first-line approach was also analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 75 patients underwent MT with CEREGLIDE 71 between October 2024 and September 2025. First-line technique was ADAPT in 76% of procedures (57/75) and combined technique in 24% (18/75). Successful revascularization (mTICI ≥2b) was achieved in 88.0% of patients (66/75). Good functional outcome (90-day mRS ≤2) was observed in 57.3% of patients (43/75). No device-related adverse events were recorded. In the ADAPT subgroup, the SNAKE technique allowed the catheter to reach the clot in 93.0% of cases (53/57).

CONCLUSIONS: CEREGLIDE 71 appeared to be a feasible and effective option for MT in patients with AIS due to large vessel occlusion (LVO), reaching the occlusion site with the SNAKE technique alone in most procedures.

METHODS: This was a retrospective, single-center, post-market observational study. title: First-principles analysis of the metal-free H2 dissociation mechanism by semiquinone radicals in mitochondrial Complex I and III.
abstract: Although ameliorative effects of molecular hydrogen (H2) have been reported in a wide range of pathological conditions, an unresolved issue is the molecular mechanism by which H2 is activated in animal cells, which lack the metal hydrogenases that dissociate the exceptionally strong nonpolar H-H bond. Using first-principles calculations (geometries optimized with spin-unrestricted B3LYP-D3BJ/def2-SVP/CPCM and energies evaluated with ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPP) with the active-site clusters of the Q-chamber of mitochondrial respiratory-chain Complex I (PDB 7QSK) and the Qo site of Complex III (PDB 1PP9), this study examined whether semiquinone could directly dissociate H2 in the low-dielectric environment buried within the enzyme and examined what changes when a conserved residue is added as a second hydrogen atom acceptor. At both sites, the anionic semiquinone Q˙- had no reaction pathway for cleaving H-H, and only the neutral QH˙, protonated by nearby residues, opened a homolytic hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) pathway with a well-defined transition state and a bound product. The continuous shift in the spin density on the transferring hydrogen from nearly 0 in the reactant to +0.99 for free H˙ confirmed, at the electronic level, that this is a true homolytic HAT and neither a proton transfer nor a hydride transfer. The reaction energies (+21 to +26 kcal mol-1) agree with an estimate based on the difference between the bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of the O-H bond of ubiquinol QH2 and the H-H bond that is broken. The same BDFE comparison also makes QH˙ a spin-allowed hydrogen-atom abstractor superior to superoxide by about 30 kcal mol-1. For HAT with a single hydrogen atom acceptor, the reaction energy of QH˙ + H2 → QH2 + H˙ is +28.3 kcal mol-1, and the barrier cannot fall below this value. In the Q-chamber, the conserved Tyr108 residue can act as a second acceptor, and for hydrogen atom transfer with H2 held between QH˙ and TyrO˙, the barrier falls to +27.0 kcal mol-1. However, this reactive QH˙ arises only under hyper-reductive pressure, where quinone-pool overreduction and high membrane potential coincide, upon occupation and protonation at the buried semiquinone reaction site. Therefore, H2 dissociation itself is established only when the semiquinone reaction-site environment under hyper-reductive pressure is present as a necessary condition. Because H2 possesses one of the strongest σ bonds, the barrier is high and sharp, and quantum tunnelling makes a substantial contribution to crossing it at body temperature. At the one-dimensional Eckart level, this contribution does not exceed thermal activation, and it is obtained as a lower bound. The crossover temperatures, set by the imaginary frequency at the saddle, are 293.9 K for Complex I and 264.7 K for Complex III. The buried semiquinone reaction site makes a barrier against one of the strongest known σ bonds, which is thin enough to bring the crossover temperature to within 16 K of body temperature, and is itself a quantitative result of the study. The Marcus inverted region (bell-shaped kinetics) that we observed in solution in the previous work shows that H2 can be activated under metal-free conditions, but in that case, it is the electron that tunnels, moving along a coordinate distinct from the hydrogen nucleus analysed here. For the in-enzyme mechanism, the moderate primary isotope effect predicted at the same level (kH/kD ≈ 4) could be tested by detecting dissociated deuterium using D2 as a tracer. Taken together, the above results shift the mechanistic account of H2 medicine from classical antioxidant scavenging to redox regulation as a quantum-tunnelling-assisted conditional hydrogenase activity conditioned by reductive pressure and position it as a field of quantum biology.

title: Timing of transition from mechanical thrombectomy to intra-arterial alteplase and reperfusion quality in thrombectomy-refractory stroke.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO), but a subset of lesions remains refractory or technically challenging despite repeated mechanical attempts. Intra-arterial (IA) alteplase may be used as rescue therapy, but the optimal timing of transition from mechanical to pharmacological therapy remains unclear. We examined the association between the timing of this transition and reperfusion quality.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 90 consecutive patients with LVO treated with MT between July 2021 and December 2022. Sixteen patients received rescue IA alteplase after ineffective or unfeasible MT. Procedure time was divided into an MT phase (femoral puncture to IA alteplase initiation) and an IA phase (IA alteplase initiation to the end of the procedure). The primary outcome was excellent reperfusion, defined as modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) 2c-3.

RESULTS: Successful reperfusion (mTICI ≥2b) was achieved in 15 patients (93.8%), including excellent reperfusion in 8 (50.0%). The MT phase was shorter in the excellent than in the non-excellent reperfusion group (median, 49.5 vs. 87.5 minutes; p=0.028), whereas the difference in the IA phase was not statistically significant (36.5 vs. 75.5 minutes; p=0.068). No symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage occurred. Good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale ≤2) at 3 months was observed in 2 patients (12.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory series, a shorter period of MT before transition to IA alteplase was associated with excellent reperfusion. This hypothesis-generating finding suggests that the timing of transition may matter and warrants evaluation in larger, controlled studies.

Intra-arterial (IA) alteplase may be used as rescue therapy, but the optimal timing of transition from mechanical to pharmacological therapy remains unclear. We examined the association between the timing of this transition and reperfusion quality.

title: Cucurbitacin B inhibits the P2RY2/MYC transcriptional axis to disrupt ATP-mediated neuroinflammatory amplification loops.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sustained microglial activation drives neuroinflammation in cerebral ischemia. Cucurbitacin B (CuB), a naturally occurring tetracyclic triterpenoid compound mainly found in Cucurbitaceae, exerts anti-neuroinflammatory effects, yet its precise mechanism remains unclear. The aim of this study was to elucidate the self-amplifying circuit perpetuating neuroinflammation and to determine how CuB disrupts it.

METHODS: The anti-inflammatory effects of CuB were assessed in LPS-stimulated BV-2 microglia. Untargeted metabolomics (UHPLC-QTOF-MS) was employed to characterize metabolic alterations. Molecular mechanisms were further investigated in LPS- or ATP-stimulated BV-2 microglia using siRNA knockdown, overexpression, dual-luciferase assays, chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by quantitative PCR (ChIP-qPCR), electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) and specific pharmacological inhibitors. The pathophysiological relevance and neuroprotection were validated in a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model.

RESULTS: CuB suppressed inflammatory mediator expression and cytokine secretion in LPS-stimulated microglia. Metabolomics in LPS-stimulated microglia revealed profound dysregulation across eight interconnected metabolic modules, including purinergic signaling and calcium homeostasis. Mechanistically, danger-associated ATP activated P2Y2 receptors, triggering PLC/IP3R-mediated Ca2+ overload that stimulated calcineurin to induce MYC. MYC in turn bound the P2RY2 promoter (confirmed by ChIP-qPCR and EMSA) to drive its transcription, establishing a pathogenic ATP/P2RY2/Ca2+/calcineurin/MYC feedforward loop. CuB disrupted this circuit at multiple nodes by reducing ATP release, blocking P2RY2, suppressing Ca2+ overload, inhibiting calcineurin-MYC, and normalizing metabolic dysregulation. In vivo, MYC/P2RY2 upregulation coincided with glial activation, inflammatory cytokine production and infarct expansion.

CONCLUSIONS: This work identifies an ATP/P2RY2/Ca2+/calcineurin/MYC feedforward loop that amplifies neuroinflammation. CuB acts as a multi-target circuit breaker, offering a novel therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke.

Cucurbitacin B (CuB), a naturally occurring tetracyclic triterpenoid compound mainly found in Cucurbitaceae, exerts anti-neuroinflammatory effects, yet its precise mechanism remains unclear. The aim of this study was to elucidate the self-amplifying circuit perpetuating neuroinflammation and to determine how CuB disrupts it.

title: Neuroprotective effects of hAEC-derived exosomes against ischemic injury are associated with Foxm1 and IGF1.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exosomes secreted by human amniotic epithelial stem cells (hAECs-Exos) have attracted considerable attention as potential therapeutic candidates for ischemic stroke. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying their neuroprotective effects remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: Oxygen-glucose deprivation followed by reoxygenation (OGD/R) was applied to HT22 and BV2 cells, and a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion (MCAO) was also established. The involvement of Foxm1 in hAECs-Exos-mediated protection was investigated using Foxm1 overexpression and hAECs-Exos derived from Foxm1-knockdown donor cells. Insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) was examined as a potential downstream mediator of Foxm1 through gene silencing and chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP). A rescue experiment combining Foxm1 overexpression with IGF1 silencing was performed to examine the functional relationship between these molecules. In vivo, the effects of hAECs-Exos or Foxm1-knockdown hAECs-Exos on MCAO rats were assessed via intracerebroventricular injection.

RESULTS: Upregulation of Foxm1 significantly mitigated neuronal damage triggered by OGD/R, as indicated by enhanced cellular viability, alleviated oxidative stress, suppressed inflammation, and decreased apoptosis. Conversely, hAECs-Exos derived from Foxm1-knockdown donor cells exhibited attenuated protective effects in both cell types. Mechanistically, ChIP supported the association of Foxm1 with the IGF1 promoter region, while Foxm1 overexpression increased IGF1 protein expression. IGF1 silencing attenuated the protective effects of hAECs-Exos, and simultaneous IGF1 silencing weakened the protective effects associated with Foxm1 overexpression. In vivo, hAECs-Exos increased Foxm1 and IGF1 expression in MCAO rat brains, improved neurological function, decreased infarct areas, and mitigated pathological damage. These effects were attenuated following administration of hAECs-Exos derived from Foxm1-knockdown donor cells.

CONCLUSIONS: hAECs-Exos protect against ischemic injury in cellular and animal models, with Foxm1 and IGF1 implicated in the observed neuroprotective effects.

title: Procedural Time Independently Predicts Functional Outcome After First-Pass Reperfusion in Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Modified first-pass effect (mFPE) is an established benchmark of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) success in large-vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke, yet its clinical benefit may be time sensitive. Prior studies indicate that procedural time (PT) exceeding 30 minutes carries higher complications rates and worse outcomes. We assessed whether procedural duration exerts a continuous, dose-dependent effect on clinical outcomes among patients achieving mFPE.

METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective study analyzed patients who achieved mFPE after MT for acute ischemic stroke between February 2018 and March 2024. Primary outcomes were 30- and 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2). Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), and mortality. Multivariate logistic regression models evaluated associations between PT (modeled continuously and dichotomized by a 30-minute cut-off) and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 417 patients achieving mFPE, 302 (72.4%) had PT ≤30 minutes. Shorter PT was independently associated with functional independence at 30 days (aOR 1.72, 95% CI 1.06-2.80; p=0.03) but not at 90 days (aOR 1.44, 95% CI 0.89-2.32; p=0.14). Modeled continuously within each time window, PT showed no significant association with functional independence, although ordinal analysis suggested worse mRS with longer PT only in the >30-minute group at 30 days (aOR 1.18; p=0.04). Median LOS was shorter for PT ≤30 minutes (6 (3-10) vs. 7 (4-13) days, p=0.01). sICH and mortality did not differ by PT.

CONCLUSION: Among patients achieving mFPE, shorter PT remained independently associated with better functional outcomes at 30 days, but not at 90 days, with no significant gradient within either window, supporting the importance of procedural efficiency even after technically successful single-pass reperfusion.

We assessed whether procedural duration exerts a continuous, dose-dependent effect on clinical outcomes among patients achieving mFPE.

title: Protocol for filament-induced transient middle cerebral artery occlusion with laser speckle imaging and outcome assessment in mice.
abstract: The transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model in mice is important for investigating endogenous protective mechanisms and potential therapeutic strategies for ischemic stroke. Here, we present a protocol for verifying successful occlusion and reperfusion using filament-induced tMCAO, with real-time monitoring of cerebral blood flow by laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI). We also describe steps for neurological testing, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining, and representative histological analyses for assessing ischemic brain injury and model quality. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Jiang et al.1.

title: Serum Exosomes from Subacute Phase Post-cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Promote Microglial Pro-inflammatory Phenotype Polarization and Exacerbate Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption in Mice.
abstract: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) restores circulation but induces cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury characterized by blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and microglial-mediated neuroinflammation. Exosomes circulate systemically following CPR, yet their temporal profiles and specific roles remain poorly understood. C57BL/6 mice (n = 5/group) underwent asphyxial cardiac arrest and CPR. BBB permeability was assessed longitudinally (3 h to 14 d) using Evans blue extravasation. Serum exosomes were isolated at 1 d and 3 d post-CPR and characterized. To determine immunomodulatory effects, exosomes were administered via intracerebroventricular injection into recipient mice, and BBB integrity and microglial polarization (CD86, CD206) were evaluated by immunofluorescence and flow cytometry. Additionally, primary cultures of microglia cells isolated from CPR mice were exposed to exosomes in vitro (n = 3/group), and pro-inflammatory phenotype/anti-inflammatory phenotype markers and inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, iNOS, TGF-β, Arg1, IL-10) were quantified. CPR induced transient BBB disruption peaking at 3 d post-resuscitation. Serum exosomes isolated at both 1 d and 3 d exhibited characteristic cup-shaped morphology. Intracerebroventricular administration of post-CPR exosomes significantly exacerbated BBB leakage and skewed microglial polarization toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype (elevated CD86⁺; reduced CD206⁺), with 3-day exosomes eliciting more potent detrimental effects than 1-day exosomes. In vitro, exposure to 3-day exosomes similarly produced stronger pro-inflammatory transcriptional responses and increased nitric oxide (NO) production compared with 1-day exosomes. Serum exosomes derived from post-CPR mice exhibit pro-inflammatory activity, aggravating BBB disruption and promoting microglial pro-inflammatory phenotype polarization upon central delivery. These findings suggest that circulating exosomes may contribute to post-resuscitation neuroinflammatory injury, and highlight exosome-related pathways as candidate targets worthy of further investigation.

title: Ultrasound-Responsive Iron-Barium Titanate Schottky Heterojunction-Embedded Hydrogel Accelerates Burn Wound Healing through Bidirectional Hydrogen-Piezocatalytic Redox Modulation.
abstract: Burn wound healing is regulated by a spatiotemporal redox hierarchy, where early reactive oxygen species (ROS) overload drives inflammation, while late ROS deficiency hinders regeneration. Programming this bidirectional sequence requires time-phased, counter-directional ROS control. Herein, we report a nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates hydrogen therapy with piezocatalytic therapy, enabling on-demand redox programming across the entire healing cascade. The system constructs a metal-semiconductor Schottky heterojunction derived from the in situ reduction of Fe2+ within the mesopores of barium titanate. The mesoporous confinement and interfacial coupling program the hydrolysis of nanoscale zero-valent iron for sustained, early-stage hydrogen delivery to scavenge toxic ROS, while the established Schottky barrier efficiently suppresses charge recombination, thereby executing ultrasound-triggered piezoelectric polarization and charge separation for on-demand ROS generation in later-stage pro-regenerative signaling. Embedded within a polyacrylamide/carboxymethyl chitosan double-network hydrogel with inherent antibacterial activity, the resulting system exhibits superior antioxidant capacity and piezocatalytic responsivity, as well as promotion of fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage polarization. In a mouse burn model, this redox-programmable platform orchestrates phased healing, attenuating early inflammation, sustaining neovascularization, and suppressing late fibrosis, achieving accelerated wound closure. Collectively, this work establishes a redox programming paradigm via heterojunction catalysis, coupling spatiotemporal ROS scavenging and generation for dynamic tissue regeneration.

title: Real-world characteristics of endovascular treatment for middle cerebral artery M2 segment occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture: a prospective multicenter registry study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of endovascular treatment (EVT) in middle cerebral artery M2 segment occlusion remains inconclusive, particularly in rural areas with aging populations. We characterized EVT and medical management (MM) for M2 occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, and explored clinical factors associated with outcomes.

METHODS: We analyzed a prospective multicenter acute ischemic stroke registry (July 2020-June 2022; 11 stroke centers). Patients with M2 occlusion were classified into EVT or MM groups; characteristics, workflow metrics, and outcomes were described and referenced against previously reported series.

RESULTS: Among 210 patients, 34 had M2 occlusion (EVT, n=10; MM, n=24). At 90 days, functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2) was 40.0% (EVT) and 45.8% (MM); symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage, 0% and 4.2%; mortality, 20.0% and 12.5%; successful reperfusion, 70.0% (EVT). Both groups were older than in previous reports (median 81 years). The EVT group also received rt-PA less often (30.0%) and had longer puncture-to-reperfusion times (81 minutes), whereas the MM group had lower pre-stroke independence (67%) and higher mortality, despite lower severity.

CONCLUSION: Advanced age, delayed reperfusion, and greater pre-stroke dependency distinguished this rural cohort from previous reports and likely account for its outcomes, underscoring the need for locally tailored patient selection for EVT in M2 occlusion.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The role of endovascular treatment (EVT) in middle cerebral artery M2 segment occlusion remains inconclusive, particularly in rural areas with aging populations. We characterized EVT and medical management (MM) for M2 occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, and explored clinical factors associated with outcomes. METHODS: We analyzed a prospective multicenter acute ischemic stroke registry (July 2020-June 2022; 11 stroke centers).

title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors.

RESULTS: Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52, p = 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58, p = 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11, p = 0.049).

DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored.

title: Incidence and predictors of suboptimal functional outcomes despite successful reperfusion in paediatric stroke: a cohort study from the Save ChildS Pro registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Successful vessel reperfusion with persistent clinical deficit occurs in 40-60% of adults undergoing mechanical thrombectomy but has never been characterised in childhood stroke. We aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of so-called futile recanalisation, in which the occluded artery is reopened but the patient does not recover good function, in paediatric mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischaemic stroke.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the Save ChildS Pro registry, an international, multicentre, observational registry that included children aged 28 days to 18 years presenting with acute ischaemic stroke across 45 centres in 12 countries between Jan 1, 2020, and Aug 31, 2023. Patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy and had successful recanalisation (expanded Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [eTICI] grade ≥2b) were included. The primary outcome was suboptimal functional outcome despite successful recanalisation, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score greater than 2 at 90 days, on a scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (death) on which 0-2 denotes functional independence; three additional thresholds (mRS score >1, Pediatric Stroke Outcome Measure [PSOM] >1·0, and PSOM >0·5) were analysed as sensitivity analyses. Adjusted associations between candidate predictors (age, baseline Pediatric National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [PedNIHSS] score, baseline Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score [ASPECTS], and final eTICI grade) and each outcome were estimated using Firth-penalised multivariable logistic regression. Save ChildS Pro is registered with the German Clinical Trials Registry (DRKS00018960).

FINDINGS: 101 patients (54 [53%] males and 47 [47%] females; median age 11·0 years [IQR 6·0-15·0]) had successful recanalisation with 90-day follow-up and comprised the analytical cohort. A suboptimal outcome (mRS score >2) occurred in 18 (18%) of 101 patients. On Firth-adjusted multivariable analysis, lower final eTICI grade was significantly associated with suboptimal outcome (adjusted OR 0·44 [95% CI 0·23-0·84], p=0·012), and younger age was associated in the same direction (0·87 [0·78-0·97] per year, p=0·0098); baseline PedNIHSS score and baseline ASPECTS were not independently associated with a suboptimal outcome. Findings were directionally consistent across the three sensitivity thresholds.

INTERPRETATION: In this analysis, 18% of children with successful recanalisation had a suboptimal functional outcome at 90 days, markedly lower than the proportion reported in adults (40-60%). Lower recanalisation quality and younger age were independently associated with suboptimal outcome, whereas baseline PedNIHSS score and ASPECTS had limited prognostic value. These findings highlight the need for longer-term studies and challenge the direct translation of adult prognostic frameworks to paediatric stroke, supporting age-specific approaches. Given the limited event count, these findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation.

FUNDING: None.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the Save ChildS Pro registry, an international, multicentre, observational registry that included children aged 28 days to 18 years presenting with acute ischaemic stroke across 45 centres in 12 countries between Jan 1, 2020, and Aug 31, 2023.

title: Not all endothelium is equal: regional and sex-dependent roles of DDAH1 in regulating endothelial function.
abstract: Asymmetrical dimethylarginine (ADMA), an endogenous inhibitor of nitric oxide synthases (NOS), is primarily metabolized by dimethylarginine dimethylaminohydrolases (DDAH1 and 2). This study used endothelial-specific DDAH1 knockout (DDAH1En-/-) mice to test whether reduced endothelial DDAH1 activity impairs cerebral endothelial function and worsens outcomes after cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion. Using male and female, DDAH1En-/- and control (DDAH1fl/fl) mice, we assessed vasoreactivity of middle cerebral (MCA), common carotid (CCA), and systemic arteries (thoracic aortae and first-order mesenteric arteries) ex vivo; and quantified CCA expression of genes associated with vascular smooth muscle (VSM) contractility. ADMA concentrations, and mRNA expression of protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMT), and DDAH were quantified in human cerebral (hCMEC/D3) and aortic (HAEC) endothelial cells. Outcomes following transient MCA occlusion (tMCAo) were also evaluated in male mice. In male DDAH1En-/- mice, NO-dependent vasodilator responses in MCA and CCA were significantly impaired compared to controls, while responses in systemic arteries were unaffected. Vasoconstrictor responses were paradoxically reduced in CCA from male DDAH1En-/- mice in association with altered expression of genes involved in VSM contractility. In contrast to males, vasoreactivity was unaltered in MCA and CCA from female DDAH1En-/- mice. Both PRMT1 and DDAH mRNA expression were higher in hCMEC/D3 compared with HAEC cells, in association with no change in ADMA concentrations. Lastly, in male DDAH1En-/- mice, infarct volumes and functional outcomes post-tMCAo were comparable with controls. These findings underscore a role for endothelial DDAH1 in maintaining endothelial function in cerebral arteries from male but not female mice. However, endothelial DDAH1 does not influence stroke outcomes.

title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear.

METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS).

RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory.

DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT.

title: Cerebral Blood Flow-Derived Myogenic Dynamics Reveal Impaired Postischemic Cerebrovascular Recovery in Experimental Stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Restoration of cerebral blood flow (CBF) after ischemic stroke does not necessarily indicate recovery of cerebrovascular regulation. We tested whether myogenic-band dynamics derived directly from CBF signals provide information beyond mean perfusion during cerebral ischemia and after acute stroke.

METHODS: Transient focal cerebral ischemia was induced in 29 Sprague-Dawley rats using middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. Bilateral laser-Doppler flowmetry (LDF)-derived CBF signals were decomposed using empirical mode decomposition and Hilbert transform, and myogenic-band activity (0.15-0.4 Hz) was quantified by absolute and relative power. Cross-validated logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether myogenic-band power provided discriminative information beyond mean CBF alone.

RESULTS: Ipsilateral mean CBF fell from 73.5±51.8 p.u. at baseline to 52.2±38.0 p.u. during late ischemia (P=0.0088), then increased to 126.6±91.5 p.u. after 3 hours of reperfusion (P=0.0050 versus baseline). Relative myogenic-band power decreased from 37.43±14.65% to 13.35±7.51% during ischemia (P<0.0001) and remained below baseline after reperfusion (20.74±12.02%, P=0.00033 versus baseline); contralateral relative power was comparatively preserved. Combining mean CBF and myogenic-band power improved discrimination of baseline from late ischemia (AUC, 0.99 versus 0.70 for mean CBF alone) and late reperfusion (AUC, 0.88 versus 0.70).

CONCLUSIONS: Frequency-specific analysis of LDF-derived CBF reveals persistent, lateralized abnormalities in myogenic-band dynamics that are not captured by mean perfusion alone. The persistence of depressed myogenic activity despite restored or elevated mean CBF demonstrates incomplete recovery of frequency-specific oscillatory dynamics after reperfusion. These findings support myogenic-band power as a potential functional measure of persistent postischemic cerebrovascular dysfunction.

title: Regulatory roles and molecular mechanisms of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification in ischemia-reperfusion injury.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) represents a prevalent internal epitranscriptomic modification of mRNA that influences post-transcriptional gene regulation. Clinically, ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury contributes to tissue damage in acute kidney injury, ischemic stroke, and myocardial infarction, particularly after blood flow is restored.

METHODS: We searched Google Scholar, Web of Science, and PubMed for literature published through May 2026. The retrieval focused on articles detailing how m6A effector proteins-specifically writers, erasers, and readers-mediate I/R pathogenesis within hepatic, renal, cardiac, and cerebral tissues.

RESULTS: m6A-associated regulation influences RNA metabolism during I/R injury. Context-dependent changes in m6A regulators and target transcripts are linked to oxidative stress, inflammatory cascades, and specific programmed cell death pathways, including ferroptosis and pyroptosis, across various organ systems.

CONCLUSION: Profiling these organ-specific m6A molecular networks may inform future research on targeted epitranscriptomic interventions for IRI.

title: Intrinsic Redox-Responsive NIR-II Lanthanide Luminescent Nanoprobes Enabled by Phonon-Assisted Cooperative Quenching for Reversible Redox Imaging In Vivo.
abstract: Lanthanide nanoparticles (LnNPs) are photostable second near-infrared window (NIR-II) emitters well suited to long-term redox imaging. However, responsive LnNP nanoprobes generally require surface-installed molecular recognition components to transduce chemical changes into luminescence signals, which may introduce additional functionalization complexity and compromise long-term signal reliability. Here, we identify a redox-regulated phonon-assisted cooperative quenching (PACQ) phenomenon in NaCeF4:Nd, where Ce(III)/Ce(IV) conversion modulates Nd(III) emission through lattice-mediated interactions. To elucidate this intrinsic response, a model NaLuF4@NaCeF4:Nd architecture was constructed to expose the NaCeF4:Nd shell and reveal the underlying PACQ mechanism. Oxidation-induced changes in Ce electronic configuration and local lattice environment weaken Ce-mediated quenching and restore NIR-II Nd(III) emission. Based on this mechanism, we further develop a ratiometric NaErF4:Yb@NaLuF4@NaCeF4:Nd nanoprobe (RPACQ), where the Er(III) emission provides a stable internal reference. RPACQ exhibits reversible H2O2/glutathione responses, with second-scale activation, concentration-dependent ratiometric responses in vitro, and excellent photostability. In a cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) model, RPACQ provides proof-of-concept for in vivo redox imaging. Collectively, this work establishes an intrinsic lanthanide nanoparticle strategy for reversible NIR-II luminescence regulation without external molecular reporters, potentially opening new avenues for engineering responsive lanthanide nanomaterials.

title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial.
abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. title: Inhibition of Ptbp1 in microglia alleviates neuroinflammation by the Cbx5-Ifitm3 axis.
abstract: Polypyrimidine tract-binding protein 1 (Ptbp1) is a member of the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins that govern numerous aspects of the messenger RNA life cycle, including splicing, stability, and translation. This study investigated its role in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) with a focus on microglia. A model of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion in mice and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) model in mouse BV2 cells were used. Ptbp1 was significantly upregulated in microglia following CIRI. Inhibition of Ptbp1 attenuated the inflammatory response in BV2 cells and reduced damage to co-cultured neurons under OGD/R conditions; it also reduced tissue inflammation, mitigated brain tissue damage, and improved neurological function on days 1, 3 and 7 after reperfusion in vivo. Mechanistically, Ptbp1 destabilized chromobox protein homolog 5 (Cbx5), thereby attenuating Cbx5/Suv39h1-mediated H3K9me3 enrichment and transcriptional repression at the interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 (Ifitm3) promoter, promoting Ifitm3 expression and enhancing Tlr4/p65 signaling. The regulation of Cbx5 mRNA stability by Ptbp1 and the inhibitory effect of Cbx5 on Ifitm3 were also confirmed in IMG cells. The present findings suggest that Ptbp1 reduces the stability of Cbx5 mRNA, thereby attenuating Cbx5/Suv39h1-mediated transcriptional repression of Ifitm3, enhancing Tlr4/p65 signaling and the inflammatory response, and exacerbating neuronal damage and CIRI.

title: ISLES'24: Final stroke infarct prediction with multimodal imaging and clinical data. Where do we stand?
abstract: Accurate estimation of brain infarction (i.e., irreversibly damaged tissue) is critical for guiding treatment decisions in acute ischemic stroke. Reliable infarct prediction informs key clinical interventions, including the need for patient transfer to comprehensive stroke centers, the potential benefit of additional reperfusion attempts during mechanical thrombectomy, decisions regarding secondary neuroprotective treatments, and, ultimately, prognosis of clinical outcomes. This work introduces the Ischemic Stroke Lesion Segmentation (ISLES) 2024 challenge, which focuses on the prediction of final infarct volumes from pre-interventional acute stroke imaging and clinical data. ISLES'24 provides a comprehensive, multimodal setting where participants can leverage all clinically and practically available data - including full acute CT imaging, sub-acute follow-up MRI, and structured clinical information - across a train set of N=150 cases. On the hidden test set (N=98), the top-performing model, a multimodal nnU-Net-based architecture, achieved a Dice score of 0.285 ± 0.213 and an absolute volume difference of 21.2 ± 37.2 mL, underlining the significant challenges posed by this task and the need for further advances in multimodal learning. This overview of the ISLES'24 challenge offers two primary contributions: first, it provides a standardized, clinically realistic benchmark for post-treatment infarct prediction, built on a comprehensive, open, and multimodal longitudinal stroke imaging dataset; second, it provides insights into the strengths and limitations of current algorithms and delineates key research directions to guide the development of next-generation infarct prediction models.

title: Sustained intestinal hydrogen delivery enhances exercise endurance in mice with coordinated gut-liver-muscle metabolic responses.
abstract: Molecular hydrogen (H2) exerts unique metabolic-modulating effects, yet its clinical translation is hindered by a fundamental pharmacokinetic challenge. Rapid systemic diffusion and short intestinal residence time require frequent dosing regimens to maintain sustained tissue exposure. Here, we demonstrate that sustained intestinal H2 delivery improves exercise endurance and correlates with coordinated metabolic responses across the intestine, liver, and skeletal muscle. Mechanistically, continuous intestinal H2 exposure is associated with reduced intestinal inflammatory and oxidative alterations, increased hepatic FOXO1 and gluconeogenesis-related protein abundance, as well as altered expression of glycolysis- and lactate-handling components in skeletal muscle. These observations support a working model in which sustained intestinal H2 exposure is associated with coordinated gut-liver-muscle metabolic responses during strenuous exercise. Although these coordinated metabolic changes were initially observed using a high-frequency hydrogen-rich water (HRW) gavage protocol, this approach is limited by repeated-administration requirements. To address this translational barrier and prolong H2 exposure duration, we engineered Mg@SiO2@ES, an orally deliverable, intestine-targeted hydrogen-generating micro-reactor. This formulation is designed to resist gastric degradation and enable sustained H2 release selectively within the intestinal lumen. It recapitulates multiple metabolic and exercise-related phenotypes observed with repeated HRW gavage. In murine acute exhaustive-exercise models, a single pre-exercise gavage of Mg@SiO2@ES enhanced exercise performance. This improvement was accompanied by attenuated oxidative stress, lower blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels, and better preservation of circulating glucose and intramuscular glycogen stores. Collectively, these findings highlight the potential of sustained intestinal H2 delivery to elicit systemic metabolic responses. They also demonstrate bioengineered gas-releasing micro-reactors as a promising strategy for further exploration of targeted H2 delivery in metabolic and exercise-related research.

title: Adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis with endovascular thrombectomy for acute large-vessel occlusion stroke: a network meta-analysis of randomized trials.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is standard care for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO), but nearly half of patients with successful reperfusion do not achieve functional independence. Adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) aims to address residual distal thrombi and microcirculatory impairment; however, the efficacy and safety of IAT in comparison with other thrombolytics remain uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing EVT alone vs. EVT combined with IAT using alteplase (ALT), tenecteplase (TNK), or urokinase (UK) in AIS-LVO patients. Primary outcomes were excellent clinical outcome (mRS 0-1) and functional independence (mRS 0-2) at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Eight RCTs involving 2,564 patients were included. For excellent clinical (mRS 0-1), EVT + IA-ALT ranked highest [surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) 96.2%], followed by EVT + IA-TNK (59.8%). Both showed significant benefits over EVT alone [EVT + IA-TNK vs. EVT: RR 1.20, 95% CI 1.05-1.39. EVT + IA-ALT vs. EVT: RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.21-1.63 and EVT + IA-TNK (0.125 mg/kg) vs. EVT: RR 1.54, 95% CI 1.07-2.20. EVT + IA-ALT (0.225 mg/kg) vs. EVT: RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.21-1.63]. For functional independence (mRS 0-2), EVT + IA-ALT also ranked highest, but no combination strategy showed a statistically significant benefit over EVT alone in pairwise comparisons. Regarding safety, point estimates for sICH risk did not differ significantly between combination strategies and EVT alone. However, EVT + IA-TNK demonstrated a statistically significant advantage over EVT + IA-ALT in terms of lower all-cause mortality (RR 1.58, 95% CI 1.01-2.46).

CONCLUSIONS: EVT + IA-ALT and EVT + IA-TNK may improve excellent clinical outcome without a statistically significant increase in sICH; however, clinically important bleeding risk cannot be excluded. In exploratory indirect comparisons, EVT + IA-TNK was associated with lower all-cause mortality than EVT + IA-ALT, although this finding is based on sparse evidence and should be interpreted with caution.

title: Reperfusion enhances treg-mediated neuroprotection and IL-10 signaling in a mouse model of large vessel occlusion.
abstract: The indications for acute reperfusion therapies in ischemic stroke have recently expanded to include patients with large ischemic cores, highlighting an urgent need for targeted neurotherapeutics that maximize tissue salvage. Preclinical studies suggest that early reperfusion, even after extensive ischemic injury, can mitigate infarct expansion and activate endogenous regenerative pathways, though the precise mechanisms driving these therapeutic benefits remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying successful reperfusion to identify novel avenues for immunotherapy. Using transient (t-MCAO) and permanent (p-MCAO) middle cerebral artery occlusion mouse models, we comprehensively analyzed central and peripheral immune cell dynamics. Our analysis revealed that successful reperfusion significantly elevates regulatory T cell (Treg) proportions compared to non-reperfused controls. Across experimental groups, higher interleukin-10 (IL-10) levels generally accompanied greater Treg abundance and better motor performance. Targeted intra-arterial delivery of IL-10 at the exact time of reperfusion directly attenuated cerebral injury and improved neurological outcomes. These findings suggest that amplifying anti-inflammatory signaling post-reperfusion may provide neuroprotection, positioning intra-arterial IL-10 as a potential adjunctive neurotherapeutic strategy to enhance the efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy.

title: Acute Reperfusion Therapies for Medium and Distal Vessel Occlusions.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medium and distal vessel occlusions (MDVO) account for a substantial proportion of acute ischemic strokes (AIS) and carry a considerable burden of long-term disability. The optimal acute reperfusion strategy for these occlusions remains uncertain. We aimed to synthesize the current evidence on intravenous thrombolysis (IVT), endovascular treatment (EVT), and intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) for MDVO.

METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of randomized-controlled clinical trials (RCTs), observational studies, and meta-analyses, complemented by updated meta-analyses of randomized data where feasible.

RESULTS: The definition of MDVO remains inconsistent complicating the interpretation and pooling of evidence. IVT achieves recanalization in a minority of distal occlusions, yet retains benefit, including in extended time windows. In our updated meta-analysis of five RCTs, EVT did not improve functional outcomes compared with best medical treatment while increasing symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. Reperfusion benefit across modalities appears to vary according to stroke severity, occlusion location, timing, and tissue viability. IAT, which delivers thrombolytics directly to the occlusion while minimizing mechanical manipulation of fragile distal vessels, is under investigation as a targeted alternative, with numerous dedicated RCTs ongoing but none yet published.

CONCLUSIONS: No single reperfusion strategy serves this heterogeneous population uniformly. IVT remains the reperfusion therapy with established benefit for most patients with MDVO, whereas EVT has not improved outcomes in unselected MDVO and IAT remains investigational. Pending further evidence, management beyond IVT should remain cautious rather than routine.

title: Acute Myocardial Infarction Following Tenecteplase: A Case Report of Complex Dual Pathology.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ischemic stroke is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, with tenecteplase being a cornerstone of acute management. While tenecteplase carries a known risk of bleeding, major thrombotic events such as acute myocardial infarction (AMI) after stroke reperfusion are less commonly described.

CASE REPORT: We present the case of a 67-year-old man who presented with acute stroke symptoms. After ruling out intracranial hemorrhage and managing blood pressure, he received tenecteplase, and all neurological deficits resolved. Soon after, he developed acute chest pain, and his repeat electrocardiogram confirmed a ST-elevation myocardial infarction. He underwent emergent cardiac catheterization, revealing 100% occlusion of the left circumflex artery, which was successfully revascularized with thrombectomy and angioplasty. Intravascular ultrasound further supported the presence of embolic phenomenon. Pathology of the retrieved material identified thrombus alongside atherosclerotic plaque fragments. The patient experienced complete symptom resolution and was discharged after a short hospitalization.This case highlights the complexities encountered when a patient with acute ischemic stroke who is treated with tenecteplase subsequently develops an AMI. Potential mechanisms include a coincidental plaque rupture, possibly exacerbated by the stress of the acute stroke, a rare paradoxical prothrombotic effect of thrombolysis, or a combination thereof. The pathological finding of mixed thrombus and atherosclerotic plaque underscores the underlying disease contributing to this event.

CONCLUSION: This case accentuates the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for new cardiovascular events in post-thrombolysis patients, especially those with significant cardiovascular risk factors. Rapid and judicious diagnostic evaluation is crucial for timely management of these complex, life-threatening complications.

title: Blocking FOXO4 confers neuroprotection against oxidative stress and ischemia-reperfusion caused neuronal injury.
abstract: Previous studies suggest that FOXO4 facilitates inflammation and oxidative stress in non-brain tissues under stress or disease conditions, indicating that downregulation of FOXO4 may be neuroprotective in ischemia-reperfusion-induced brain injury. This possibility has not been tested in a cerebral ischemia-reperfusion context, however. Here, we exposed FOXO4 knockout (KO) primary neuronal cultures to oxidative stress or oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), and subjected KO mice to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). We also used a structure-based approach combined with cell-based assays to identify a FOXO4 inhibitor and evaluated its effects in tMCAO-treated wild-type (WT) mice. Our results showed that FOXO4 KO reduced oxidative stress- and OGD-induced neuronal death, attenuated tMCAO-induced infarct volume, improved animal survival, decreased neurological deficits, and enhanced functional recovery compared with WT cells or mice. Immunohistochemical staining and Western blot analyses further indicated reduced neuroinflammation in the KO brain. The identified FOXO4 inhibitor Actinomycin D suppressed FOXO4 activity at a low dose, reduced brain injury, and improved functional recovery in WT mice following tMCAO. Together, these findings indicate that FOXO4 is a potential therapeutic target and that suppression of its activity may promote neuronal survival after ischemic stroke-induced brain injury.

title: Spatiotemporal Core-Shell Microspheres Enable Hydrogen-Mediated Redox Priming and Kartogenin-Induced Cartilage Regeneration for Osteoarthritis Bio-Rescue.
abstract: The effective management of osteoarthritis (OA) remains a formidable clinical challenge due to a chronically inflamed joint microenvironment and the limited self-regenerative capacity of articular cartilage. To address these barriers, we developed an ultrasound-responsive core-shell microsphere platform engineered via a customized microfluidic capillary device. This system features a kartogenin (KGN)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) core encapsulated within a sodium alginate shell enriched with tin disulfide (SnS) nanosheets (SSN). Following intra-articular injection, non-invasive ultrasound stimulation triggers the localized SSN to generate low-concentration hydrogen gas (H2). This in situ H2 generation rapidly scavenges excess reactive oxygen species to restore redox homeostasis, thereby mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction and preserving chondrocyte viability. Consequently, this targeted antioxidative intervention suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion and polarizes synovial macrophages toward a pro-regenerative M2 phenotype. Within this newly stabilized microenvironment, the sustained release of KGN from the PLGA core successfully reverses extracellular matrix metabolic imbalances to promote cartilage repair. In a rat model of OA, this dual-functional, spatiotemporally controlled platform profoundly halted joint degeneration and preserved histological cartilage integrity. Collectively, this ultrasound-triggered core-shell microsphere system offers a highly promising, disease-modifying strategy for comprehensive OA therapy.

title: The RETRIAD Study: Comparative First-Pass Reperfusion Performance of EmboTrap III, Trevo NXT, and APERIO Stent Retrievers in Acute Large-Vessel Occlusion Stroke: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Contemporary stent retrievers differ in design, yet direct comparative evidence regarding their first-pass reperfusion performance using a standardized endpoint remains limited. This study compared first-pass reperfusion outcomes among APERIO, Trevo NXT, and EmboTrap III. Methods: In this exploratory, single-center retrospective cohort study, 200 patients were screened between 1 March 2024 and 1 August 2026. Forty patients had not completed 90-day follow-up at the time of the initial data analysis. An additional 104 patients were excluded because of tandem occlusion (n = 29), recanalization after intravenous thrombolysis before thrombectomy (n = 8), distal vessel occlusion (n = 30), or successful direct aspiration without stent-retriever deployment (n = 37). The final cohort comprised 56 patients treated with first-line combined stent-retriever and aspiration thrombectomy using APERIO (n = 28), Trevo NXT (n = 14), or EmboTrap III (n = 14). The primary endpoint was strict first-pass effect (FPE), defined as first-pass expanded Treatment in Cerebral Ischemia (eTICI) grade 2c-3. Results: Strict FPE was achieved in 16/28 (57.1%), 9/14 (64.3%), and 9/14 (64.3%) patients, respectively (global exact p = 0.879). Both comparisons with APERIO yielded an absolute risk difference of +7.1 percentage points (95% CI, -23.2 to +33.6). Exploratory adjusted analyses yielded imprecise estimates. Heidelberg-classified symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in zero, three, and two patients, respectively. Conclusions: No statistically detectable difference in strict FPE was demonstrated among the three device-based treatment strategies. However, the small sample size, wide confidence intervals, and nonrandomized treatment allocation preclude conclusions regarding device equivalence or causal effects.

title: Scutellarin as a multi-target neuroprotective agent: Analytical evidence, pharmacokinetic insights and translational strategies across neurodegenerative disorders.
abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are a leading cause of disability and mortality globally, but effective disease-modifying therapeutic strategies are still largely unavailable. Scutellarin is a flavonoid glycoside extracted from Erigeron breviscapus (Vant.) Hand-Mazz. It has been widely studied in preclinical models of neurodegenerative disorders. In this study, we performed a systematic review of preclinical animal studies. We combined comprehensive database retrieval with quantitative synthesis of eligible outcomes. The pooled results demonstrated that scutellarin significantly reduced cerebral infarct volume and improved neurological deficit scores in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion models. It also ameliorated learning and memory impairments in experimental Alzheimer's disease (AD) models. Consistent neuroprotective effects were also found in models of depression, anxiety, Parkinson's disease, etc. Mechanistic analysis indicated that scutellarin produces multi-level neuroprotective effects. It acts by reducing oxidative stress, inhibiting neuroinflammation, suppressing apoptosis, stabilizing the neurovascular unit and other neurobiological processes. This review first evaluated the preclinical efficacy of scutellarin through systematic review and meta-analysis. It then integrated cross-disease mechanisms with network pharmacology, reverse virtual screening and molecular docking to identify computationally predicted targets. Although scutellarin shows promising preclinical effects, its clinical translation faces major limitations. These limitations include low oral bioavailability, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and insufficient data on brain exposure. Overall, scutellarin is a multi-target neuroprotective candidate. Future studies should focus on target validation, exposure-response modeling, delivery optimization and clinically relevant translational evaluation.

title: An immediate reperfusion sign might increase the likelihood of favourable outcomes in patients with intracranial atherosclerotic disease-related stroke who received stent-retriever-based thrombectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTS: To investigate the relationship between the presence of an "immediate reperfusion sign (IRS)" during retrievable stent-based thrombectomy and clinical outcomes in patients with large vessel-occluded acute ischaemic stroke related to intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) treated with stent retrievers.

METHODS: Consecutive ICAD-LVO stroke patients who were treated with stent retrievers and whose imaging records were available for the assessment of the IRS were included. The sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes were calculated. Univariate analysis and partial correlation analysis were also performed.

RESULTS: Eighty-two ICAD-LVO patients were identified from 421 endovascularly treated AIS patients from 2015 to 2024. Fifty-four of them were ultimately included in the analysis, and an IRS was observed in 41 of these patients (75.9%). Favourable outcomes were significantly more frequent in the IRS (+) group (51.2% versus 7.7%, p=0.005). The sensitivity of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes was 95.5% (21/22), the specificity was 37.5% (12/32), the positive predictive value was 51.2% (21/41), and the negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.3% (12/13). Additionally, the presence of an IRS, as well as age, baseline NIHSS score and successful final reperfusion, was significantly different between the favourable and unfavourable groups. Partial correlation analysis revealed a moderate correlation (r=0.412; p=0.002) between the comprehensive reperfusion score (in which the presence of an IRS and successful final reperfusion was counted as 1 point) and favourable outcomes.

CONCLUSION: In our respective cohort of patients, the presence of an IRS during stent-retriever-based thrombectomy appeared to indicate a higher rate of first-pass-effect and a 3-month favourable outcome in acute LVO stroke patients with ICAD.

METHODS: Consecutive ICAD-LVO stroke patients who were treated with stent retrievers and whose imaging records were available for the assessment of the IRS were included. The sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes were calculated.
