title: Residual SYNTAX score and optical coherence tomography-derived thin-cap fibroatheroma in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: an exploratory descriptive pilot study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. While percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the definitive reperfusion strategy, residual disease burden and plaque vulnerability both influence clinical recovery. The residual SYNTAX score (rSS) quantifies untreated macroscopic coronary artery disease, whereas optical coherence tomography (OCT) resolves microscopic plaque architecture, notably thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA). This pilot study explored the descriptive characteristics and short-term outcomes associated with combining rSS and OCT-derived TCFA in a highly selected STEMI cohort.

METHODS: This retrospective observational pilot study included 30 patients with STEMI who underwent primary PCI and culprit lesion OCT evaluation at a tertiary care center. Patients were stratified into four groups according to the presence of culprit TCFA and the post-PCI rSS threshold ( ≤ 4 vs. > 4): group 0 (TCFA absent, rSS > 4), group 1 (TCFA absent, rSS ≤ 4), group 2 (TCFA present, rSS > 4), and group 3 (TCFA present, rSS ≤ 4). The primary clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE)-a composite of all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularization, heart failure hospitalisation, and ischemic stroke-assessed over 3 months.

RESULTS: The cohort (mean age, 54.5 ± 10.1 years; 83.3% male, 40% with diabetes mellitus) had a 53.3% prevalence (16 of 30) of culprit lesion TCFA. Complete or reasonable revascularization (rSS ≤ 4) was achieved in 12 patients (40.0%). The overall cumulative 3-month MACE rate was 30.0% (9 of 30). MACE occurred in 1 of 7 patients (14.3%) in group 0, 1 of 7 (14.3%) in group 1, 4 of 11 (36.4%) in group 2, and 3 of 5 (60.0%) in group 3 (Fisher exact test, P = 0.23; log-rank P = 0.38). Patients with TCFA accounted for 7 of 9 clinical events (77.8%). Given the small subgroup sizes (n < 12), multivariable predictive risk modeling was not performed.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory pilot cohort of STEMI patients undergoing PCI, the presence of OCT-derived TCFA was descriptively associated with higher short-term adverse event rates across both complete and incomplete revascularization strata. Given the small sample size and clear indication bias, these findings are strictly hypothesis-generating and support the need for adequately powered prospective registries to evaluate dual anatomical-biological risk stratification.

title: Cavitation jet treatment-assisted glycosylation of hemp seed protein: Structural regulation and emulsion stability.
abstract: This study employed cavitation jet treatment to facilitate the effective glycosylation of hemp seed protein (HSP) with chitosan (CS). Initially, the treatment disrupted intra- and inter-molecular hydrogen bonds, inducing HSP structural unfolding. This critical conformational transition exposed internal reactive amino groups, enabling them to interact with CS carbonyl groups and achieving a maximum grafting degree of 34.54%. Consequently, the secondary structure of HSP was reorganized from an ordered state into a more relaxed, disordered configuration. The subsequent covalent attachment of hydrophilic CS chains effectively shielded exposed hydrophobic regions, significantly enhancing the complex's water affinity. Therefore, overall functional performances were markedly improved: solution properties were enhanced through increased solubility and decreased turbidity, while emulsion performance was optimized, evidenced by a superior EAI (55.89 m2/g), an extended ESI (84.35 min), and improved apparent viscosity and viscoelasticity. This approach provides a practical strategy for the high-value utilization of hemp by-products.

title: False patency, true occlusion: perfusion imaging and dual stent-retriever thrombectomy for a calcified carotid terminus embolus.
abstract: Calcified cerebral emboli are an uncommon cause of acute ischemic stroke and may produce a false-patency sign on computed tomography angiography because their high attenuation can mimic intravascular contrast material. We report the case of a 77-year-old woman who presented with a wake-up stroke approximately 14 hours after she was last known well, with right hemiplegia and global aphasia. Noncontrast computed tomography showed a markedly hyperattenuating intraluminal focus at the left carotid terminus and proximal M1 segment, suggesting a calcified cerebral embolus. Computed tomography angiography appeared to show severe stenosis with residual luminal patency, whereas computed tomography perfusion demonstrated extensive hypoperfusion involving the left middle cerebral artery and bilateral anterior cerebral artery territories. Because the severe neurologic deficit and perfusion abnormality were discordant with the apparent patency on computed tomography angiography, cerebral angiography was performed. Digital subtraction angiography demonstrated complete occlusion of the left M1 origin and near-complete occlusion of the left A1 segment; the right A1 segment was congenitally hypoplastic. A rigid calcified embolus spanning the carotid-terminus bifurcation was retrieved using a balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent technique under proximal flow arrest, achieving complete reperfusion in a single pass. Histopathologic examination confirmed calcified embolic material. This case highlights the value of multimodal imaging and confirmatory angiography when clinical and imaging findings are discordant. In this patient, balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent retrieval was a tailored and feasible strategy; however, a single case cannot establish its superiority over other thrombectomy approaches.

title: Exosomes in remote ischemic preconditioning-mediated organ protection: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
abstract: Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is an endogenous protective strategy that confers resistance against sustained ischemia-reperfusion injury in distant organs. RIPC induces protective responses through complex neuronal, humoral, and systemic signaling pathways. Increasing evidence suggests that exosomes may serve as important mediators of humoral inter-organ communication during RIPC. Exosomes are small extracellular vesicles released by donor cells that transport biologically active molecules, including lipids, proteins, messenger RNAs, and microRNAs, to recipient cells, thereby modulating cellular responses to injury. Emerging evidence indicates that RIPC-associated exosomes and their molecular cargo contribute to protection against ischemia-reperfusion injury in organs such as the heart, brain, kidney, and spinal cord. Several exosomal molecules, including miRNAs, HSP90, HIF-1α, and NOX2, have been implicated in the regulation of cellular pathways associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, mitochondrial function, and tissue survival. In particular, alterations in exosomal miRNAs and protein and metabolite profiles following RIPC suggest that exosomes may participate in the transmission of protective signals from remote ischemic tissues to target organs. The therapeutic potential of exosomes is further supported by their ability to transport multiple bioactive molecules and their potential application as biomarkers or delivery vehicles for therapeutic cargo. However, the specific exosomal components responsible for RIPC-mediated protection and their causal contribution to inter-organ signaling remain to be fully established. Therefore, the present review summarizes the emerging evidence on the role of exosomes in RIPC-mediated organ protection, with particular emphasis on cardiovascular and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, the molecular cargo involved, underlying protective mechanisms, and their potential therapeutic and translational applications.
englishSummary: Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is an endogenous protective strategy that confers resistance against sustained ischemia-reperfusion injury in distant organs. RIPC induces protective responses through complex neuronal, humoral, and systemic signaling pathways. Increasing evidence suggests that exosomes may serve as important mediators of humoral inter-organ communication during RIPC.

title: β-Asarone Alleviates Post-stroke Neuroinflammation and Improves Mitochondrial Quality Via the BNIP3/BNIP3L-dependent Mitophagy Pathway.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, with mitophagy playing a central role in post-stroke neurological dysfunction. β-Asarone, a major bioactive component derived from the traditional herb Acorus tatarinowii, possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties. However, whether β-asarone ameliorates IS by regulating mitophagy and its underlying mechanisms remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether β-asarone exerts neuroprotective effects against IS by modulating BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy. A middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) cell model were established. Neuroprotective effects were evaluated using neurological behavioral scores, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining, hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining, and Nissl staining. Mitochondrial function was assessed by measuring reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). Mitophagy was observed via transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and fluorescence microscopy. Western blot (WB) analysis was performed to detect BNIP3/BNIP3L pathway proteins. Results showed that β-asarone enhanced mitophagy, improved mitochondrial function, and alleviated post-stroke neuroinflammation. Conversely, the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA) impaired mitophagic function, exacerbating ischemia-induced brain injury and inflammation, while β-asarone treatment reversed these detrimental effects. In summary, β-asarone mitigates neuroinflammation and neuronal injury after IS, at least partly through promoting BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy, highlighting this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for IS.

However, whether β-asarone ameliorates IS by regulating mitophagy and its underlying mechanisms remains unclear.

title: Inhibition of miR-140-5p attenuates OGD/R-induced neuronal injury by targeting IL1RAPL1.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major contributor to neuronal damage and long-term neurological dysfunction after stroke. Our previous studies demonstrated that miR-140-5p expression is markedly upregulated following cerebral ischemia and that in vivo overexpression of miR-140-5p exacerbates cognitive impairment, suppresses neurogenesis, and promotes neuronal death in ischemic mouse models; however, its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the downstream molecular targets of miR-140-5p and to elucidate the mechanisms by which miR-140-5p regulates neuronal injury after I/R.

METHODS: We established an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in primary cortical neurons and assessed viability via Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8). miR-140-5p expression after OGD/R was examined, and loss-of-function experiments evaluated the effects of miR-140-5p inhibition. Synaptic integrity was assessed by immunofluorescence, and inflammatory cytokines by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Proteomic analysis identified potential downstream targets, which were validated via Western blotting and dual-luciferase reporter assays.

RESULTS: We found that miR-140-5p expression was significantly upregulated in mouse cortical neurons after OGD/R. Functional inhibition of miR-140-5p markedly enhanced neuronal survival, promoted synaptic remodeling, and attenuated inflammatory responses following OGD/R injury. Mechanistically, miR-140-5p was shown to directly target Il1rapl1 and modulate downstream c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) signaling, thereby regulating neuronal viability, inflammation, and synaptic plasticity under ischemia-reperfusion conditions.

CONCLUSION: This study reveals a novel miR-140-5p-mediated regulatory mechanism in neuronal injury following cerebral ischemia-reperfusion and suggests a potential therapeutic target for ischemic brain injury.

Our previous studies demonstrated that miR-140-5p expression is markedly upregulated following cerebral ischemia and that in vivo overexpression of miR-140-5p exacerbates cognitive impairment, suppresses neurogenesis, and promotes neuronal death in ischemic mouse models; however, its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the downstream molecular targets of miR-140-5p and to elucidate the mechanisms by which miR-140-5p regulates neuronal injury after I/R.

title: Metal-based hydrogen-generating therapeutic systems: From reactive chemistry to route-specific exposure and translational design.
abstract: Molecular hydrogen (H2) has shown broad therapeutic relevance in oxidative injury, inflammation, metabolic dysfunction and tissue repair, yet its clinical translation remains limited by rapid diffusion, poor retention and a poorly defined dose-exposure relationship. Metal-based H2-generating systems offer an engineering strategy to produce or release H2 at pathological sites or material-tissue interfaces, where local exposure can be shaped by material design. This review reframes these platforms as material-formulation-route-indication systems rather than isolated material classes. The field now extends from classical metal hydrides to broader metal-containing platforms that generate or release H2 through hydrolysis, corrosion, electrochemical reactions or hydrogen storage-mediated release. Their therapeutic behavior is governed by route-specific exposure fields shaped by H2 release, accompanying reaction chemistry, formulation-defined compartments and tissue environments. Accordingly, route-oriented evaluation is essential because the same reactive core can produce distinct exposure profiles, safety boundaries and translational requirements across oral, local, vascular and implantable contexts. Mechanistically, H2-dependent redox and cytoprotective biology provides an important entry point, but therapeutic outcomes arise from a multi-effector local chemical milieu involving metal-derived species, coupled physicochemical changes and, in some platforms, external activation. Translational development therefore requires controlled materials engineering, route-specific exposure metrics, mechanism-matched validation, a PK/PD-like exposure-response framework adapted for reactive material systems and manufacturing strategies aligned with chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) requirements. The field should advance toward route-specific, exposure-defined and mechanism-validated local reaction therapy.

title: Diagnostic delay and predictors of true stroke among patients with suspected in-hospital stroke: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Timely diagnosis is essential for acute treatment of in-hospital stroke. We aimed to investigate factors associated with diagnostic delay and clinical predictors of true stroke among patients with suspected in-hospital stroke.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we screened head computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging orders between Jan 2023 and Jan 2026 for patients hospitalized outside the Departments of Neurology and Neurosurgery who developed new neurological symptoms within 24 h of symptom onset or last known well and were clinically suspected of having in-hospital stroke. Multivariable analyses were performed to identify factors associated with diagnostic delay and true stroke.

RESULTS: A total of 183 patients (110 men, median age 77 years) were included. Median time from last known well to imaging-based final diagnosis was 292 min. Overall, 77 patients (42.1%) had true stroke, including 70 ischemic strokes, 5 intracerebral hemorrhages, and 2 subarachnoid hemorrhages. Wake-up symptom onset [Exp (β) 3.34, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.61-4.28] and initial medical emergency team activation [Exp (β) 0.71, 95% CI 0.56-0.91] were associated with diagnostic delay. Persistent neurological symptoms [odds ratio (OR) 1.44, 95% CI 1.24-1.68] and FAST-positive symptoms (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.12-1.46) were associated with true stroke. Among the 70 patients with ischemic stroke, 17 (24.3%) underwent reperfusion therapy.

CONCLUSION: Wake-up symptom onset and medical emergency team activation were associated with diagnostic delay, whereas persistent and FAST-positive symptoms were associated with true stroke. These findings may facilitate earlier recognition and improve triaging patients with suspected in-hospital stroke.

We aimed to investigate factors associated with diagnostic delay and clinical predictors of true stroke among patients with suspected in-hospital stroke. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we screened head computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging orders between Jan 2023 and Jan 2026 for patients hospitalized outside the Departments of Neurology and Neurosurgery who developed new neurological symptoms within 24 h of symptom onset or last known well and were clinically suspected of having in-hospital stroke.

title: Endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction in the setting of mechanical thrombectomy: a conceptual link between cardiometabolic vulnerability and microvascular reperfusion failure.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has made macrovessel reopening achievable in acute ischemic stroke, but angiographic success does not ensure effective tissue-level reperfusion or microvascular oxygen delivery. This narrative review examines endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction as a plausible blood-facing interface that may connect pre-existing cardiometabolic vulnerability with post-thrombectomy microvascular dysfunction. Targeted English-language literature from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar through 30 April 2026 was synthesized, with emphasis on MT, impaired microvascular reperfusion (IMR), no-reflow, blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular-unit (NVU) biology, glycocalyx-related biomarkers, cardiometabolic risk, perfusion imaging, and microcirculatory rescue. The evidence base is heterogeneous and is explicitly separated into direct human MT/LVO evidence, indirect human biomarker or imaging evidence, experimental cerebral evidence, non-cerebral/cross-disease vascular evidence, and hypothesis-generating mechanistic inference. Ischemic priming, abrupt reperfusion, oxidative and inflammatory stress, complement activation, metabolic stress, distal embolization, device-endothelial trauma, and host vulnerability may converge on the luminal endothelial surface. Glycocalyx dysfunction may amplify leukocyte adhesion and capillary plugging, platelet adhesion and microthrombosis, impaired mechanosensing and nitric-oxide signaling, BBB destabilization, and heterogeneous capillary flow; however, direct causal proof in human MT is lacking. Circulating syndecan-1, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan are therefore best interpreted as time- and compartment-dependent systemic signals rather than direct readouts of the cerebral glycocalyx. Post-EVT microcirculatory rescue trials show that downstream perfusion may remain therapeutically actionable, but they do not demonstrate glycocalyx repair as the operative mechanism. A practical translational strategy is to combine serial, compartment-annotated biomarkers with prespecified early perfusion/barrier imaging and tissue endpoints, while explicitly modeling cardiometabolic vulnerability and competing microvascular mechanisms. The glycocalyx framework should therefore be considered a testable network hypothesis rather than an established primary cause of post-thrombectomy no-reflow or futile recanalization.

title: Diabetes-Associated Fibrin Enrichment in Cerebral Thrombi and Its Procedural Implications for Mechanical Thrombectomy.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Diabetes is associated with altered fibrin biology, but its relationship with fibrin content in cerebral thrombi and the procedural relevance of this relationship during mechanical thrombectomy remain unclear. We investigated the association between diabetes and fibrin content in thrombectomy-retrieved cerebral thrombi and whether diabetes-associated differences in fibrin content mediated procedural outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had retrieved thrombi available for histological analysis. Red blood cell, platelet, and fibrin contents were quantified immunohistochemically. The association between diabetes and fibrin content was evaluated using multivariable linear regression, with complementary sensitivity analyses based on intravenous tissue-type plasminogen activator administration and atrial fibrillation status. Mediation analyses were performed to estimate the indirect effects of diabetes on procedural outcomes through diabetes-associated changes in fibrin content. Results: Among 312 patients, 98 (31.4%) had diabetes. Patients with diabetes had greater fibrin content than those without diabetes (median, 37.0% [interquartile range, 26.4-52.9] vs. 30.9% [17.7-45.0]; p = 0.004), whereas red blood cell and platelet contents did not differ significantly between the groups. Diabetes remained associated with greater fibrin content in the primary adjusted analysis (β = +6.68 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.19-11.18; p = 0.004), and the association persisted after additional conditioning on initial glucose and in sensitivity analyses. Among patients with diabetes, neither HbA1c nor initial glucose was associated with fibrin content. Mediation analyses did not identify a detectable indirect effect of diabetes through fibrin content on successful reperfusion, complete reperfusion, first-pass effect, number of passes, or the requirement for ≥3 passes. Conclusions: Diabetes was independently associated with greater fibrin content in cerebral thrombi retrieved during mechanical thrombectomy, supporting the presence of a diabetes-associated fibrin-enriched thrombus phenotype. However, no detectable indirect effect of diabetes-associated differences in fibrin content on the examined procedural outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy was identified. These findings suggest that although diabetes is associated with a distinct quantitative change in cerebral thrombus composition, a corresponding procedural consequence was not detectable in the present study.

We investigated the association between diabetes and fibrin content in thrombectomy-retrieved cerebral thrombi and whether diabetes-associated differences in fibrin content mediated procedural outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had retrieved thrombi available for histological analysis.

title: Factors associated with in-hospital mortality after stroke at a tertiary hospital in Angola.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most Angolan patients with stroke reach hospital beyond the thrombolysis window, and many deaths occur within 72 h of admission. We investigated routinely recorded variables associated with in-hospital mortality at Hospital do Prenda.

METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study at Hospital do Prenda, a public tertiary hospital in Luanda, from January 2023 to December 2025. The unit of analysis was the hospitalisation episode; four episodes ending in transfer were excluded. Hypertension and type 2 diabetes were extracted from free-text fields using predefined string rules. Univariable analyses used Pearson chi-square, crude odds ratios (OR; 95% CI), and Mann-Whitney tests. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, year, stroke subtype, recorded comorbidities, and head-CT status. Given the low events-per-variable ratio (~7) and poor calibration in some models, adjusted estimates were considered exploratory associations rather than independent prognostic effects.

RESULTS: Among 479 episodes, 75 patients died (15.7%; 95% CI 12.7-19.2). Median age was 58.5 years among decedents versus 52.0 among survivors (p = 0.049). Median length of stay was 3 versus 6 days (p < 0.0001), reflecting early mortality rather than a prognostic exposure. Mortality increased from 6.7% at age 45-54 years to 28.0% at ≥75 years and remained graded after adjustment (≥75 years: adjusted OR 5.92, 95% CI 2.28-15.38; p = 0.0003). Mortality among patients <45 years was also elevated (17.2%; adjusted OR 2.97, 95% CI 1.28-6.87), predominantly among haemorrhagic strokes (22.2% versus 10.8% for ischaemic stroke; age-by-subtype interaction p = 0.0009). Sex, year, stroke subtype, recorded hypertension, and diabetes were not associated with mortality. Absence of head CT showed higher crude mortality (30.0% versus 15.0%; OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.90-6.52). Recorded hypertension prevalence was only 19.8%, indicating substantial under-ascertainment.

CONCLUSION: Older age was the strongest admission-available correlate of in-hospital mortality, while elevated mortality among younger patients was concentrated in haemorrhagic stroke. Under-ascertainment limits interpretation of comorbidities. Absence of stroke-severity, functional-status, ICU, ventilation, and reperfusion data further limits causal or independent prognostic inference.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Most Angolan patients with stroke reach hospital beyond the thrombolysis window, and many deaths occur within 72 h of admission. We investigated routinely recorded variables associated with in-hospital mortality at Hospital do Prenda. METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study at Hospital do Prenda, a public tertiary hospital in Luanda, from January 2023 to December 2025.

title: The inhibitory effect of gadolinium-conjugated diflunisal on platelet function through regulating outside-in signaling of αIIbβ3 integrin.
abstract: The gadolinium-conjugated diflunisal derivative ETN102 has previously been shown to suppress cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) levels, reduce glial activation, and attenuate neuronal damage associated with stroke. In the present study, we investigated whether ETN102 modulates platelet aggregation and activation. ETN102 selectively inhibited thrombin-induced platelet aggregation while sparing platelet responses to other agonists, including collagen, adenosine diphosphate (ADP), and U46619. ETN102 also reduced adenosine triphosphate (ATP) secretion under aggregating conditions without altering thromboxane B2 (TXB2) generation, suggesting that its antiplatelet effect is independent of the COX-1-dependent thromboxane signaling. Flow cytometric and biochemical analyses further demonstrated that ETN102 suppressed thrombin-induced αIIbβ3 integrin activation, platelet spreading, clot retraction, and the phosphorylation of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) and proline-rich tyrosine kinase 2 (Pyk2), without affecting granule secretion, intracellular Ca2+ mobilization, or phosphorylation of Syk, PI3K, and AKT signaling molecules. In vivo, ETN102 significantly prolonged carotid artery occlusion time in a ferric chloride (FeCl3)-induced thrombosis model and increased tail bleeding time and hemoglobin content. In addition, ETN102 reduced infarct volume and improved neuronal survival markers in a murine model of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury. These findings demonstrate that ETN102 is a thrombin-context selective modulator of platelet integrin αIIbβ3 outside-in signaling, with antithrombotic and neuroprotective potential.

title: Endovascular treatment of tandem lesions: prognostic factors of functional outcome and the efficacy of emergent carotid stenting.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prognostic risk factors for endovascular therapy (EVT) in acute ischemic stroke with tandem lesions, and to evaluate the efficacy and safety of emergent carotid artery stenting.

METHODS: Patients with acute internal carotid artery tandem occlusion who underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) were enrolled. Baseline clinical and procedural data were collected. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score, and the safety endpoint was symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH). Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to balance covariates between patients receiving emergent carotid artery stenting (eCAS) and non-stenting controls. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors. Subgroup analyses were conducted on relevant risk factors.

RESULTS: A total of 112 eligible patients were included, with a mean age of 66.19 ± 9.23 years; 76 (67.86%) were male. Fifty-eight patients (51.79%) achieved a favorable functional outcome (good prognosis group). Univariate analysis revealed significant differences (P < 0.05) between the two groups in baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, puncture-to-reperfusion time, history of hypertension, and history of atrial fibrillation. After multivariable adjustment, hypertension, baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, and puncture-to-reperfusion time were identified as independent risk factors for unfavorable 90-day functional outcomes in tandem lesion patients undergoing EVT. Emergent carotid artery stenting (eCAS) was not an independent predictor of 90-day favorable functional outcome (adjusted OR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.17-1.58, P = 0.246). Significant differences in stroke history and smoking history were found between the emergent stenting and non-stenting groups at baseline. Female sex and puncture-to-reperfusion time were independent risk factors for sICH in tandem lesion patients. Subgroup analysis indicated that in those aged ≥ 65 years, emergent stenting was associated with unfavorable 90-day functional prognosis (OR = 0.042, 95% CI 0.004-0.469, P = 0.01).

CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, hypertension, baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, and puncture-to-reperfusion time may serve as independent predictors of 90-day favorable functional outcomes in tandem lesion patients treated with EVT. Female sex and longer puncture-to-reperfusion time appear to be potential risk factors for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. Emergent carotid artery stenting was not found to be an independent predictor of 90-day functional prognosis in our cohort, and no significant increase in sICH risk was observed in association with eCAS. These preliminary findings require further validation in large-scale multicenter prospective studies.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prognostic risk factors for endovascular therapy (EVT) in acute ischemic stroke with tandem lesions, and to evaluate the efficacy and safety of emergent carotid artery stenting. METHODS: Patients with acute internal carotid artery tandem occlusion who underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) were enrolled. Baseline clinical and procedural data were collected.

title: Prehospital delay and thrombolysis rates in posterior circulation stroke: a multicenter Latin American study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the delay to emergency arrival in adults with acute Posterior circulation ischemic strokes (PCS) and the likelihood of receiving intravenous thrombolysis compared to anterior circulation ischemic strokes (ACS) across six different hospitals in Latin America.

METHODS: This multicenter study in Latin America hospitals including three hospitals in Peru (Cusco, Arequipa, and Lima City), one in Colombia (Bogotá), one in Chile (Valdivia), and one in Mexico City. We analyzed adult patients treated between 2018 and 2023 with a confirmed diagnosis of ischemic stroke (IS). We evaluated demographic characteristics, initial NIHSS score, onset-to-door time (ODT), rate of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT), and other stroke-related characteristics. Medians with interquartile ranges (IQR) were calculated. IVT (yes/no) was evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression including stroke circulation, age, sex, admission NIHSS, ODT, previous stroke, and previous evaluation at another hospital as covariates. Continuous predictors were modeled per year, NIHSS point, and ODT hour, respectively. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% CI were reported, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: A total of 1,460 patients were included, 501 (34.3%) of whom had PCS, with a median age of 70 years (IQR 59-80). We found significant differences in median ODT between PCS and ACS (13 h, IQR 5-46 vs. 8.5 h, IQR 4-20; p < 0.001) and in IVT rates. In the adjusted analysis, each additional hour of ODT was associated with lower odds of IVT (aOR 0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.92), whereas stroke circulation was not independently associated with IVT (PCS vs. ACS: aOR 0.66, 95% CI 0.39-1.11). Higher admission NIHSS was associated with higher odds of IVT (aOR 1.06 per point, 95% CI 1.03-1.09).

CONCLUSION: Patients with posterior circulation stroke had longer prehospital delays and lower observed rates of intravenous thrombolysis than those with anterior circulation stroke. However, stroke circulation was not independently associated with IVT after adjustment for ODT and other clinically relevant covariates. These findings highlight early recognition and reduction of prehospital delay as potential targets for improving access to reperfusion therapy in Latin America.

METHODS: This multicenter study in Latin America hospitals including three hospitals in Peru (Cusco, Arequipa, and Lima City), one in Colombia (Bogotá), one in Chile (Valdivia), and one in Mexico City. We analyzed adult patients treated between 2018 and 2023 with a confirmed diagnosis of ischemic stroke (IS).

title: IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis determines phosphodiesterase 1c activation inducing vascular endothelial cell damage, contributes to cerebral vascular injury and neuroinflammation.
abstract: Cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase 1 (PDE1) plays critical roles in mediating neuroinflammation, neuron degeneration, and cognitive impairment through suppressing the fundamental cAMP and cGMP signaling, presenting a promising therapeutic target in combating neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative disease. However, the crucial mechanism correlating PDE1 activation and how it regulates neuroinflammation are less studied. Here, we found that the level of PDE1c significantly increased in the cerebral tissue of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) rats, especially of the endothelial cell population. Treating the human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) or dithiothreitol (DTT) significantly increased the expression level of PDE1c at both transcription and translation levels and induced vascular cell damage. These were alongside IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis activation. Inhibition of IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis by pharmacological interventions such as TUDCA or PAIR2 or gene silencing efficiently decreased PDE1c level and ameliorated vascular cell damage. Moreover, deficiency or inhibition of PDE1c by its inhibitor PDE1-IN-4 suppressed vascular cell damage and inflammatory markers activation but marginally affected IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis. Also, no additive effects were observed when treating PDE1-IN-4 in the Xbp-1s knockdown cells. Collectively, our study revealed that IRE-1α/XBP-1s axis might be a crucial upstream regulator of PDE1c in controlling vascular endothelial barrier homeostasis, presenting a novel therapeutic strategy in ameliorating CIRI.

title: Electroacupuncture Inhibits Neuronal Ferroptosis in MCAO/R Model Mice by Regulating the GSK-3β/NRF2 Signaling Pathway.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuronal ferroptosis following acute ischemic stroke (AIS) contributes to ischemic brain injury and is regulated by nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), a key regulator of antioxidant defense and iron homeostasis. Whether electroacupuncture (EA) suppresses neuronal ferroptosis by regulating NRF2 stability and nuclear translocation through upstream glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK-3β) remains unclear. We investigated whether EA inhibits neuronal ferroptosis and alleviates ischemic brain injury by modulating the GSK-3β/NRF2 axis.

METHODS: Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) models were established in C57BL/6 and conditional Nrf2-knockout mice. The GSK-3β inhibitor laduviglusib (CHIR-99021; CHIR), the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1), and conditional Nrf2 knockout were used to investigate the anti-ferroptotic mechanism of EA and the regulatory hierarchy between GSK-3β and NRF2. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), western blotting, and immunofluorescence were used to examine the GSK-3β/NRF2 pathway and ferroptosis-related molecules. NRF2 nuclear localization, neuronal nuclei (NeuN) /acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) double immunofluorescence, and co-immunoprecipitation were used to assess NRF2 nuclear translocation, neuronal ferroptosis, and the GSK-3β-NRF2 interaction, respectively.

RESULTS: EA inhibited GSK-3β activity after MCAO/R, restored NRF2 protein expression, promoted nuclear accumulation, and upregulated NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1). EA also downregulated ACSL4 and transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1), upregulated glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11), reduced NeuN/ACSL4-colocalized neurons, decreased ferrous iron (Fe2+) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and increased superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, glutathione (GSH) content, and the GSH/oxidized glutathione (GSSG) ratio. CHIR and Fer-1 produced similar anti-ferroptotic effects, and co-immunoprecipitation confirmed GSK-3β-NRF2 interaction. Conditional Nrf2 knockout did not affect EA- or CHIR-mediated GSK-3β phosphorylation but markedly attenuated their effects on NQO1, SLC7A11, GPX4, and TfR1. EA also alleviated mitochondrial ultrastructural damage, reduced cerebral infarction and Fluoro-Jade B (FJB)-positive neurons, and improved neurological function and motor coordination in MCAO/R mice.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify the GSK-3β/NRF2 axis as an important regulatory mechanism of regulating neuronal ferroptosis after MCAO/R and support EA as a potential therapeutic strategy for alleviating neuronal ferroptosis and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury through GSK-3β inhibition and NRF2 activation.

Whether electroacupuncture (EA) suppresses neuronal ferroptosis by regulating NRF2 stability and nuclear translocation through upstream glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK-3β) remains unclear. We investigated whether EA inhibits neuronal ferroptosis and alleviates ischemic brain injury by modulating the GSK-3β/NRF2 axis.

title: From recanalization to recovery: inflammation and futile reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion. This clinical-angiographic mismatch may reflect persistent tissue injury, including inflammatory injury, alongside pretreatment damage and other determinants of outcome. Experimental findings and clinical associations implicate persistent inflammatory activation, thrombo-inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, microvascular no-reflow, and blood-brain barrier disruption as contributors to secondary tissue injury after MT. Here, we examine potential inflammatory contributions to futile reperfusion and consider how inflammatory biomarkers might inform risk stratification after MT. Ischemia activates microglia, endothelial cells, platelets, complement pathways, and circulating immune cells. Subsequent reperfusion may amplify oxidative stress, cytokine signaling, neutrophil-endothelial interactions, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, matrix metalloproteinase activity, and barrier failure. Together, these processes can promote microvascular obstruction, cerebral edema, hemorrhagic transformation, infarct growth, and impaired neurological recovery despite successful angiographic reperfusion. Among circulating biomarkers, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio has been studied repeatedly, alongside platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, interleukin-6, matrix metalloproteinase-9, and other molecular markers. Their specificity, incremental predictive value, and clinical utility require further validation in standardized thrombectomy cohorts. We therefore view inflammation as a plausible biological link between macrovascular reperfusion and persistent tissue-level injury after MT. From a translational perspective, the immediate priorities are to standardize sampling protocols, characterize dynamic inflammatory trajectories, develop multimodal prediction models, and test biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies.
englishSummary: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion.

title: Edaravone for Potential Mitigation of Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Kidney Disease.
abstract: Edaravone (EDA) is a synthetic free-radical scavenger FDA-approved for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) treatment in the United States and is used clinically for treatment of acute ischemic stroke in Japan and other countries. While its antioxidant activity has been the primary focus of investigation in the mitigation of oxidative-stress-related injury, EDA exhibits anti-inflammatory, anti-fibrotic, anti-apoptotic, and anti-necrotic effects in animal models. These properties make it a potentially attractive therapeutic agent for kidney disease, where oxidative stress and inflammation contribute to renal cell injury, mitochondrial dysfunction, and progression of disease. In this review, we cover the underlying mechanisms of oxidative stress and inflammation in renal injury, and pharmacological and free-radical-scavenging mechanisms of EDA. Preclinical evidence in several kidney diseases, including ischemic/reperfusion injury, nephrotoxin-induced disease, and diabetic kidney disease, has been used to assess EDA for efficacy. In addition, we explore the modulatory roles of key signaling pathways, such as Nrf2 and NF-κB, in protective effects of EDA against oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, necrosis, and fibrosis. Finally, we highlight the potential of EDA as a therapy in future clinical applications for various kidney diseases such as acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). It should also be emphasized that as EDA's renal efficacy evidence described in this review is largely limited to animal studies, robust human clinical data are lacking. Therefore, additional clinical studies are still needed to fully elucidate the efficacy, safety, and benefits of EDA for prevention and treatment of human kidney disease.

title: NE52-QQ57 attenuates post-ischemia protein phosphorylation in the mouse brain.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cerebral ischemia induces a reduction in brain pH. GPR4, a proton-sensing G protein-coupled receptor is highly expressed in vascular endothelial cells. Pharmacological inhibition of GPR4 with NE52-QQ57 (NEQQ) reduces ischemia-induced blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and brain injury. To facilitate targeting GPR4 in vivo, it is important to better define the effect of NEQQ on post-ischemia signaling and the pharmacokinetics of NEQQ in vivo.

METHODS: We performed biochemical analysis following transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). We used Liquid Chromatography-Mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to quantify the concentration of NEQQ in serum, brain, and peripheral tissues.

RESULTS: NEQQ administration decreased the phosphorylation of PKA substrates, PKC substrates, ERK1/2, and CREB. LC-MS/MS analysis detected NEQQ in both ipsilateral and contralateral hemisphere of the brain at 5 h and 24 h after reperfusion, demonstrating that NEQQ crosses the BBB. In peripheral tissues, NEQQ exhibited highest level in kidney and lowest in the heart. In sham controls, average serum concentrations were ~4 and 0.9 μg/g at 5 and 24 h, respectively. Following tMCAO, ipsilateral brain exhibited higher levels as compared to the contralateral side at 5 h while the difference diminished at 24 h.

CONCLUSIONS: NEQQ attenuated the ischemia-induced activation of multiple signaling pathways. NEQQ exhibited broad distribution in peripheral organs, and its brain level was sufficient for GPR4 inhibition at 24 h after injection. These findings support the use of NEQQ as a pharmacological inhibitor of GPR4-mediated signaling following ischemic stroke.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Cerebral ischemia induces a reduction in brain pH. GPR4, a proton-sensing G protein-coupled receptor is highly expressed in vascular endothelial cells. Pharmacological inhibition of GPR4 with NE52-QQ57 (NEQQ) reduces ischemia-induced blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and brain injury.

title: Persistent Hypoperfusion on Post-Recanalization Digital Subtraction Angiography Perfusion Maps in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite high recanalization rates with endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion stroke, a large proportion of patients remain disabled. This study aims to investigate the clinical impact of persistent hypoperfusion that was detected immediately after recanalization.

METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with large vessel occlusion with near-complete or complete recanalization, perfusion maps were generated from post-recanalization digital subtraction angiography. Focal hypoperfusion within the ischemic territory was detected and categorized as regional or cortical according to spatial distribution. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2). The associations of no-reflow and outcomes were examined by multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 375 patients (median age 69 [interquartile range 57-77] years; 67.5% men), persistent hypoperfusion was detected in 29.6% of patients. Patients with hypoperfusion had higher baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (median 14 versus 12, P=0.076) and more thrombectomy passes (P=0.021). The presence of persistent hypoperfusion was strongly associated with reduced functional independence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.23, 95% CI 0.13-0.39, P<0.001), higher rates of hemorrhagic transformation (aOR=1.88, 95% CI 1.14-3.11; P=0.013) and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aOR=2.95, 95% CI 1.20-7.23; P=0.018). Quantitative analysis revealed minimum regional cerebral blood flow as a key factor of functional outcome (aOR=1.67, 95% CI 1.07-2.60; P=0.023). There is no significant agreement with 24-hour computed tomography perfusion-defined hypoperfusion (κ=0.106, P=0.524).

CONCLUSIONS: Persistent hypoperfusion could be detected immediately post-recanalization in one-third of successfully treated large vessel occlusion strokes. The adverse impact to functional outcome highlights its potential as an intraprocedural biomarker for future adjunctive therapies.

This study aims to investigate the clinical impact of persistent hypoperfusion that was detected immediately after recanalization. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with large vessel occlusion with near-complete or complete recanalization, perfusion maps were generated from post-recanalization digital subtraction angiography.

title: The role of excitotoxicity in post-cardiac arrest brain injury.
abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Post-cardiac arrest brain injury (PCABI) remains the leading cause of neurological disability and death following cardiac arrest. While considerable improvements have been made in achieving return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) following cardiac arrest, effective neuroprotective therapies have lagged behind. This review examines the potential utility of targeting early glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity and explores why previous neuroprotective strategies have failed to improve clinical outcomes.

RECENT FINDINGS: Preclinical models have recognized glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity as a key mechanism contributing to early ischemia-reperfusion injury following cardiac arrest. Early interruption of this excitotoxic cascade may preserve vulnerable neurons and mitigate downstream secondary brain injury. Emerging therapies targeting glutamate have demonstrated mixed but encouraging early clinical results. We propose that these therapies should be integrated into a broader multimodal neuroprotective strategy that adapts to the evolving pathophysiology of PCABI.

SUMMARY: The failure of neuroprotective therapies after cardiac arrest may reflect delayed therapeutic delivery rather than the absence of viable biological targets. Future progress will require improved characterization of human cerebral ischemia, earlier implementation of neuroprotective interventions, and therapies that are tailored to the evolving biology of PCABI.

This review examines the potential utility of targeting early glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity and explores why previous neuroprotective strategies have failed to improve clinical outcomes.

title: Optimal Catheter Size for Medium Vessel Occlusion in Aspiration Thrombectomy.
abstract: The efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion remains controversial, and optimal recanalization strategies are lacking. We investigated factors associated with successful recanalization using aspiration thrombectomy in patients with medium vessel occlusion. We conducted a retrospective study on patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent aspiration thrombectomy for M2 occlusion between July 2021 and November 2025. We examined the factors associated with successful recanalization by focusing on the ratio of the catheter outer diameter to the target vessel inner diameter (Catheter-to-vessel ratio). Overall, 64 patients were included. First-pass successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction ≥ 2c) was achieved in 24 patients. In patients with successful recanalization, the ratio of the catheter outer diameter to the target vessel inner diameter (Catheter-to-vessel ratio) was significantly higher than in those without successful recanalization (p = 0.029). In multivariate analysis, the Catheter-to-vessel ratio was independently associated with successful recanalization after adjustment for catheter position and thrombus size (odds ratio per 0.1 increase, 3.688; 95% confidence interval, 1.478-9.202; p = 0.0007). In the receiver operating characteristic analysis, the threshold for the Catheter-to-vessel ratio distinguishing successful recanalization was 0.70, with a sensitivity of 79% and a specificity of 63%.In aspiration thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion, a Catheter-to-vessel ratio ≥ 0.70 may be an exploratory indicator associated with first-pass successful reperfusion.

We investigated factors associated with successful recanalization using aspiration thrombectomy in patients with medium vessel occlusion. We conducted a retrospective study on patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent aspiration thrombectomy for M2 occlusion between July 2021 and November 2025.

title: Advanced Imaging-Guided Intravenous Thrombolysis Beyond 4.5 Hours: A Single-Center Experience in Mexico.
abstract: Introduction Intravenous thrombolysis is the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke within the first 4.5 hours; however, many patients present with unknown symptom onset or delayed presentation. Advanced neuroimaging allows identification of salvageable brain tissue and extension of the therapeutic window up to nine hours, and recent evidence suggests that, in carefully selected patients, reperfusion may be beneficial up to 24 hours after stroke onset. Objective The objective of this study is to report the institutional experience with advanced imaging-guided intravenous thrombolysis in the extended therapeutic window, including its frequency of use and workflow times. Methods We conducted a retrospective, descriptive study including consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke who received intravenous thrombolysis between March 2022 and May 2025. Patients treated beyond 4.5 hours after symptom onset or with unknown onset time were identified and analyzed. Eligibility for thrombolysis was determined using computed tomography (CT) perfusion or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) mismatch criteria. Descriptive analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 27 (Released 2019; IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results Fourteen patients (17.7%) out of a total of 79 were identified. Female sex predominated (79%), with a mean age of 67 ± 17 years and a median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 9 points. The most frequently affected territory was the anterior circulation (79%), primarily the middle cerebral artery. Onset was unknown in 36% of cases. Median time from symptom onset was 327 minutes; door-to-imaging time was 30 minutes, and door-to-needle time was 74 minutes. No in-hospital mortality was recorded. Conclusions Advanced imaging-guided thrombolysis is feasible in tertiary care centers in Mexico, thereby expanding access to reperfusion therapy for patients with delayed presentation.

Advanced neuroimaging allows identification of salvageable brain tissue and extension of the therapeutic window up to nine hours, and recent evidence suggests that, in carefully selected patients, reperfusion may be beneficial up to 24 hours after stroke onset. title: Periprocedural body temperature and clinical outcomes after successful reperfusion in large vessel occlusion stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional recovery remains heterogeneous among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke, even after successful reperfusion. Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 219 patients with large-vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke (LVO-AIS) who underwent EVT and achieved successful reperfusion, defined as a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score of 2b-3. Pre and post-EVT body temperatures were recorded. The primary outcome was favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2 at 90 days. Logistic regression analyses and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between body temperature and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Among the 219 included patients, 104 (47.5%) achieved favorable functional outcome at 90 days. Pre-EVT temperature was not significantly associated with functional outcome. In unadjusted analysis, each 1 °C increase in post-EVT temperature was associated with lower odds of favorable functional outcome (OR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.20-0.79; P = 0.01) and higher odds of mortality (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.11-3.66; P = 0.02). However, these associations were attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.19-1.15; P = 0.10; adjusted OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.49-3.02; P = 0.67). In exploratory subgroup analyses, a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and lower odds of favorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15 (adjusted OR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.08-0.98; P = 0.047), although the interaction was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.64).

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, body temperature was not independently associated with functional outcome in the overall cohort. Although a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and unfavorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15, the interaction was not significant. This finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation with pre-specified subgroup analyses.

Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain.

title: CYC1 silencing exacerbates hypoxia-induced neuronal death via mitochondrial apoptosis under hyperglycemia.
abstract: Cytochrome c1 (CYC1) is a subunit of mitochondrial complex III, which is known to play a key role in ischemic brain injury. However, the functional role of CYC1 in hyperglycemic cerebral ischemia/reperfusion remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the effect of CYC1 gene knockdown in an in vitro model mimicking hyperglycemic ischemia/reperfusion. HT22 cells with normal CYC1 expression (wild-type) and CYC1-knockdown cells were exposed to 4 h of hypoxia under high-glucose and acidic conditions, followed by reoxygenation. Assessments were conducted at 0, 6, and 12 h post-reoxygenation. Cell viability (CCK-8), cell injury (LDH release), ROS production (DHE probe), mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1 probe), and apoptosis (TUNEL staining) were evaluated. CYC1 knockdown reduced cell viability, increased LDH release and ROS production, decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, and upregulated expression of Cyt c, cleaved caspase-3, and AIF, indicative of activation of the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. These results indicate that CYC1 deficiency exacerbates hippocampal neuronal injury under hypoxic, high-glucose, and acidic conditions mimicking diabetic cerebral ischemia.

However, the functional role of CYC1 in hyperglycemic cerebral ischemia/reperfusion remains unclear. title: Implementation of a HUB-and-spoke telestroke network to improve access to intravenous thrombolysis in Indonesia: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Access to specialist-supported hyperacute stroke care remains limited in many regions of Indonesia. Telestroke may facilitate remote neurological assessment, interpretation of neuroimaging, reperfusion decision-making, and coordination of referral to comprehensive stroke centres. We evaluated the early implementation of a hub-and-spoke telestroke network in the Greater Bandung metropolitan area and described its observed treatment processes and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients evaluated through a five-spoke telestroke network connected to Hasan Sadikin Central General Hospital (RSHS), Bandung, between May 2024 and January 2025. Patients receiving formal telestroke consultation were classified according to their final diagnosis and clinical pathway. The final telestroke analytic cohort included patients meeting the prespecified study criteria; stroke mimics were excluded from the comparative stroke cohort. Intravenous thrombolysis was analyzed using an ischemic-stroke-specific denominator. Demographic characteristics, stroke severity, referral times, reperfusion treatment, and neurological outcomes were assessed. Continuous variables were summarized as mean ± standard deviation or median (interquartile range), as appropriate, and categorical variables as n/N (%). Effect estimates with 95% confidence intervals were reported where appropriate.

RESULTS: Forty patients were identified in the telestroke database during the study period. One patient with a stroke mimic was excluded, resulting in 39 patients in the final telestroke analytic cohort, including 30 patients with ischemic stroke and 9 with intracerebral hemorrhage. Patients managed through the telestroke pathway had a substantially shorter median onset-to-hub interval than those managed through the conventional referral pathway (3.5 hours [IQR 2.5-6.0] vs. 20.0 hours [IQR 7.0-72.0]; p<0.001). Among patients with ischemic stroke, intravenous thrombolysis was administered in 8/30 patients (26.7%) in the telestroke pathway and 6/164 patients (3.7%) in the conventional referral pathway. The observed odds of intravenous thrombolysis were higher in the telestroke pathway (OR 9.58, 95% CI 3.04-30.20; p<0.001). The telestroke group also demonstrated a greater median reduction in NIHSS during hospitalization (ΔNIHSS 3 [IQR 2-5] vs. 1 [IQR 0-4]; p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Implementation of a hub-and-spoke telestroke network was feasible in the Greater Bandung metropolitan area and provided a structured pathway for specialist stroke consultation, reperfusion assessment, and referral coordination. The observed differences in referral time and intravenous thrombolysis utilization suggest potential process-level advantages, but these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the retrospective design, small telestroke cohort, and substantial differences between the participating and comparator hospital pathways. Prospective multicentre evaluation is required to determine the effectiveness and generalizability of the model.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Access to specialist-supported hyperacute stroke care remains limited in many regions of Indonesia. Telestroke may facilitate remote neurological assessment, interpretation of neuroimaging, reperfusion decision-making, and coordination of referral to comprehensive stroke centres. We evaluated the early implementation of a hub-and-spoke telestroke network in the Greater Bandung metropolitan area and described its observed treatment processes and clinical outcomes.

title: Preprocedural CT Radiomic Features of the Basal Ganglia Are Associated with Post-Thrombectomy Hyperdense Transformation: A LASSO-Based Logistic Regression Analysis.
abstract: Purpose: To investigate whether radiomic characteristics of visually unremarkable basal ganglia on preprocedural non-contrast computed tomography (CT) are associated with subsequent post-thrombectomy hyperdense transformation (HT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center study included a derivation cohort of 84 patients with preserved Alberta Stroke Programme Early CT Scores (ASPECTS ≥ 8), no visually appreciable basal ganglia abnormality, anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion, and complete reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy between January 2022 and July 2023. An independent temporal validation cohort comprised 31 consecutive eligible patients treated between August and November 2023. The ipsilateral basal ganglia were manually segmented on preprocedural non-contrast CT, and radiomic features were extracted using LIFEx. Candidate features underwent interobserver reproducibility assessment and correlation filtering before least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation. The final model was applied without modification to the temporal validation cohort. Nested cross-validation and learning-curve analysis were additionally performed to assess model-development optimism and stability. Results: The final model retained two texture features, Gray-Level Run Length Matrix Short Runs Emphasis and Gray-Level Size Zone Matrix Grey Level Variance. In the derivation cohort, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.760 (95% CI, 0.652-0.855), with 48.8% sensitivity, 95.3% specificity, and 72.6% accuracy. When applied without modification to the independent temporal validation cohort, the AUC was 0.677 (95% CI, 0.475-0.858), with 33.3% sensitivity, 93.8% specificity, and 64.5% accuracy. Nested cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.673 ± 0.037, with variability in feature selection across resampling iterations. Learning-curve analysis showed an early plateau, with little improvement in cross-validated discrimination as the training sample increased within the evaluated range. Conclusions: Radiomic analysis of visually unremarkable basal ganglia on preprocedural non-contrast CT identified an exploratory two-feature imaging signature associated with subsequent post-thrombectomy HT. The model retained modest discriminatory ability in temporal validation, although internal resampling demonstrated model-development optimism and limited feature-selection stability. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant further evaluation using larger datasets, alternative modeling approaches, and independent multicenter validation.

title: Carbenoxolone Modulates Dopamine D2 Receptor-Associated Inflammatory Responses After Ischemic Stress.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in reperfusion therapy, ischemic brain injury remains a major cause of disability. Astrocytes play a central role in postischemic inflammation and tissue remodeling, but the molecular drivers of their reactive state transitions remain unclear. Here, we investigated whether carbenoxolone modulates reactive astrocyte phenotypes through astrocytic Drd2 signaling after cerebral ischemia.

METHODS: In vivo rat cerebral ischemia-reperfusion model and in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion paradigms were used. Infarct volume and neurological outcomes were assessed in vivo. Transcriptomic profiling was performed by RNA sequencing, followed by validation of representative genes using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Functional effects were evaluated in astrocytes and neuron-astrocyte coculture systems, and the involvement of Drd2 was examined using genetic knockdown approaches.

RESULTS: Carbenoxolone reduced infarct volume and improved neurological outcomes both in the acute phase and 14 days after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion in rats. RNA sequencing revealed that carbenoxolone attenuated inflammatory signaling and reduced the expression of reactive astrocyte markers, including interleukin-1 beta and Cd44. RNA sequencing identified Drd2 as a prominently upregulated gene in carbenoxolone-treated rats compared with saline controls. These transcriptional changes were validated at both the mRNA level by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction and the protein level by Western blotting. Functionally, under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion conditions, carbenoxolone enhanced cell survival in astrocytes and neuron-astrocyte cocultures, but not in neurons alone, indicating an astrocyte-mediated protective effect. Genetic silencing of Drd2 increased the reactive astrocyte marker Cd44 (cluster of differentiation 44) under basal conditions and partially attenuated carbenoxolone-induced cytoprotection after oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion.

CONCLUSIONS: Carbenoxolone modulates postischemic inflammatory responses and reactive astrocyte-associated programs, with evidence supporting a role for Drd2 signaling in these effects. These findings provide mechanistic insight into carbenoxolone-mediated neuroprotection and suggest Drd2 signaling as a potential therapeutic target in ischemic brain injury.

Astrocytes play a central role in postischemic inflammation and tissue remodeling, but the molecular drivers of their reactive state transitions remain unclear. Here, we investigated whether carbenoxolone modulates reactive astrocyte phenotypes through astrocytic Drd2 signaling after cerebral ischemia.

title: The selective IGF-1 fusion protein scp776 targets apoptotic cells and promotes recovery of ischemia/reperfusion injured tissues: Engineering and preclinical validation.
abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and acute ischemic stroke (AIS) continue to be substantial burdens on global health, despite recent advances in care. Current treatment strategies focus on blockage removal and establishment of reperfusion, but there are no approved treatments to protect cells from apoptosis resulting from hypoxia or reperfusion injury. Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) is a pleiotropic modulator of mitogenic and anti-apoptotic pathways across multiple cell types. Administration of IGF-1 reduces cell death and promotes recovery following ischemic injury. However, the development of IGF-1 therapeutics for apoptotic injuries has been limited by its short half-life, extensive protein binding, and non-specificity. We aimed to develop a targeted IGF-1 therapeutic, capable of preferential accumulation in injured tissues with large populations of apoptotic cells. A fusion protein consisting of an IGF-1 signaling domain, an albumin backbone, and an Annexin-V targeting domain was optimized for binding to apoptotic cells through iterative protein engineering. In vivo targeting to injured tissue, and in vitro prevention of apoptosis in cardiomyocytes, neurons, and neuroglia was demonstrated for the lead molecule scp776. Single dose scp776 treatment reduced infarct sizes in rat and pig AMI models. In a cynomolgus monkey model of AIS, a 5-day regimen of scp776 reduced lesion volume and neurological deficits within the acute post-ischemic window (first 3 days) and significantly improved survival at two weeks. These results demonstrate the potential of this novel class of targeted growth factors in different tissue types and motivate the clinical assessment of scp776-mediated rescue from acute ischemic injury.

Current treatment strategies focus on blockage removal and establishment of reperfusion, but there are no approved treatments to protect cells from apoptosis resulting from hypoxia or reperfusion injury. Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) is a pleiotropic modulator of mitogenic and anti-apoptotic pathways across multiple cell types.

title: Beyond Absolute Blood Pressure Targets During Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Narrative Review of Intraprocedural Hemodynamics.
abstract: Hemodynamic management is a central component of procedural care for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) during endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Current guideline recommendations predominantly provide absolute blood pressure (BP) targets for intraprocedural management. Studies have also examined relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, and blood pressure variability (BPV), providing additional measures of systemic hemodynamic exposure during EVT. However, definitions, baseline reference pressures, measurement intervals, and BPV metrics vary widely across studies, and associations with neurological outcomes are inconsistent. Importantly, these systemic BP parameters do not directly establish cerebral perfusion. This limitation supports investigating cerebral autoregulation as a complementary, patient-specific assessment. Evidence linking individualized autoregulatory limits to outcomes remains predominantly post-EVT, with very limited evidence during the pre-recanalization phase under anesthesia. This review examines intraprocedural BP during EVT under anesthesia beyond absolute pressure targets. It considers relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, pressure-time burden, BPV, and individualized autoregulatory limits in relation to cerebral perfusion. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed for studies evaluating hemodynamics during EVT under anesthesia, supplemented by screening of selected reference lists. Studies examining intraprocedural BP targets, relative changes, hypotension duration, pressure-time burden, and BPV in relation to neurological or imaging outcomes under anesthesia were prioritized, with emphasis on the pre-recanalization period. Post-EVT hemodynamic studies were not included in the primary synthesis, except where they informed the discussion of cerebral autoregulation and future research. Intraprocedural hemodynamic variables during EVT characterize different aspects of systemic arterial-pressure exposure that may be relevant to cerebral perfusion in the ischemic penumbra. Absolute pressure, relative change, magnitude and duration of hypotension, pressure-time burden, and BPV should be regarded as complementary rather than interchangeable measures. Differences in reference pressures, definitions, measurement intervals, exposure periods relative to recanalization, and anesthesia techniques limit comparisons and standardization across studies. Future prospective studies, particularly during general anesthesia (GA), should integrate clearly defined systemic BP metrics with dynamic cerebral autoregulation. This may help determine which parameters or combinations best reflect cerebral physiological vulnerability. Individualized autoregulation-guided BP targets remain investigational and require prospective validation before they can inform routine clinical hemodynamic management.

title: Mechanism of Buyang Huanwu Decoction in regulating arachidonic acid metabolism to mediate microglial polarization and alleviate cerebral ischemic injury.
abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: BYHWD, a classical prescription for post-stroke rehabilitation, protects against cerebral ischemia by modulating microglial polarization, oxidative stress, and lipid metabolism.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the mechanism by which Buyang Huanwu Decoction regulates arachidonic acid metabolism to mediate microglial polarization and alleviate cerebral ischemic injury.

METHODS: The study employed a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) using SD rats, as well as oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) models in bEnd.3 and BV.2 cells. The subjects received BYHWD treatment. The protective effects of BYHWD on brain tissue were evaluated using neurological function scoring, HE staining, immunofluorescence, ELISA, PCR, and biochemical assays. The effects of BYHWD on the function and morphology of microvascular endothelial cells were examined using immunofluorescence, tube formation assays, and cytoskeletal staining. Metabolomic profiling was performed to screen for differential metabolites and associated pathways involved in BYHWD-mediated improvement of lipid metabolism. The identified key targets were validated by a combination of Western blotting, immunofluorescence, and biochemical assays. Finally, Mendelian randomization analysis was employed to confirm the causal relationship.

RESULTS: In vivo and in vitro studies showed that BYHWD markedly improved neurological function and attenuated neuronal injury. The underlying mechanism involves the inhibition of arachidonic acid metabolism and the regulation of glycerophospholipid metabolism to restore lipid homeostasis, along with the attenuation of inflammatory responses and oxidative stress damage, as well as the promotion of cerebral microvascular repair. Mendelian randomization analysis further confirmed that lipid metabolic disturbances are a risk factor for large artery atherosclerosis stroke.

CONCLUSION: BYHWD protects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by blocking arachidonic acid metabolism, adjusting glycerophospholipid pathways to restore lipid homeostasis reducing inflammation and oxidative stress, and facilitating the restoration of injured blood vessels.

title: Gastrointestinal tract delivery of hydrogen by dynamic gas-releasing frameworks.
abstract: Given the broad therapeutic benefits of molecular hydrogen, gastrointestinal delivery of this gasotransmitter is attractive for treating localized inflammatory diseases, yet conventional H2-releasing formulations suffer from limited solubility and poor tunability. Here, we develop gas-releasing frameworks (GRFs) for effective H2 delivery to the gastrointestinal tract. GRFs provide 20,000-fold higher hydrogen storage than hydrogen-rich water (HRW), prevent burst leakage in acidic gastric fluid, and enable sustained, inflammation-targeted H2 release in the intestine. After H2 release, the dynamic framework sequesters toxic boron within a reconstituted Si-O-B architecture, promoting fecal rather than systemic boron accumulation and improving long-term biosafety. Consequently, GRFs outperform HRW in mitigating oxidative damage and inflammation in dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis, radiation-induced colitis, and high-fat diet-induced non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Collectively, these gas-releasing frameworks provide a feasible, safe, and translatable strategy for gastrointestinal delivery of therapeutic gases and treatment of inflammatory disorders.

title: Postischemic endothelial immune reprogramming in stroke.
abstract: Large-vessel recanalization is essential in acute ischemic stroke, but it does not guarantee microvascular reperfusion. Endothelial responses may contribute to persistent tissue hypoperfusion through leukocyte trafficking and immunothrombosis. Many of these responses may begin during ischemia and may continue or intensify when blood flow returns. We therefore use postischemic or ischemia/reperfusion-associated terminology unless experiments isolate the contribution of reperfusion. We propose that endothelial immune reprogramming requires a coordinated molecular program, localization to a defined vascular segment and time, and a corresponding change in immune-regulatory function. An isolated increase in an adhesion molecule or circulating biomarker indicates activation or injury but cannot identify such a state. Barrier/stress, adhesive/chemotactic, and prothrombotic responses overlap. Experimental studies implicate endothelial signaling, leukocyte arrest, and platelet interactions with neutrophil extracellular traps, but have not established a common sequence of endothelial states. Human evidence comes mainly from circulating biomarkers, thrombectomy thrombi, post-mortem tissue, and perfusion imaging. The available findings have yet to link a defined cerebral endothelial state to downstream perfusion and clinical outcome in the same patients. Prospective studies should combine serial vascular biomarkers, repeated perfusion imaging, and longitudinal follow-up, with endothelial-enriched molecular profiling when tissue is available. Therapeutic studies should test whether modifying a reversible endothelial program relieves no-reflow while preserving later immune resolution and vascular repair. These approaches remain investigational.
